docs.title: Boilerplate
docs.text:
Boilerplate pairs a Python development environment, one tool for each job, with templates that build on one another to stamp out projects. Use its templates as they are, or put your own standards on top of one instead of forking it. It renders each template with Copier, a tool for project templates, and you don't need to know Copier to use it.

Boilerplate takes care of the setup chores around writing code, the kind developers call yak shaving: a working toolchain and a configured project. You start at the work.

Each pick is the most modern and lightweight option for its job: uv for installing Python and managing dependencies, Ruff for linting and formatting, Pyright in strict mode for type checking, pytest for testing and VS Code as the editor. The templates configure them in pyproject.toml and .vscode/, so the editor and the command line format code the same way.

Less yak. More stack.

New project, dependencies installed, pytest passing.

The Quickstart shows the same steps in text.

Quickstart Browse Templates Hub

Coming from Copier?

Start with Why Boilerplate? for the pitch, or go straight to Template Composition for the extends mechanics.

Already on uv?

uv init gives you a package; Boilerplate gives you the judgment around it.

Evaluating Boilerplate?

Why Boilerplate? covers the ethos and the environment; Implementation Status shows what is implemented.

docs.title: Why choose Boilerplate?
docs.text:
• Instant productivity

    Scaffold fully configured projects with one command.

  • Locked dependencies

    uv.lock pins the environment, so every machine resolves the same.

  • Toolchain

    uv, ruff, and pytest arrive preconfigured and ready to go, plus a strict pyright configuration checked live via Pylance.

  • Cross-platform

    Windows 11 installs are automated; Linux/WSL2 and macOS follow the same steps manually.

  • Minimal configuration

    Defaults from the first render, so there is less setup before you write code.

  • Template composition

    Layer templates with extends — one command, one merged question set, deterministic precedence when layers overlap.

Planned

boilerplate update — a three-way merge that consumes the lock boilerplate new writes to move a generated project to a newer template version — is planned. See the roadmap for sequencing, the update model design for the approach, and Implementation Status for what exists today.

docs.title: Mini quickstart
docs.text:
Windows 11macOS and Linux 
# Install (-ExecutionPolicy Bypass is per-process only)
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheRealBillSiegler/boilerplate/v0.4.0/scripts/install.ps1 | iex"
# Scaffold
boilerplate new project my-first-project

With Git and uv installed:

uv tool install git+https://github.com/TheRealBillSiegler/boilerplate.git@v0.4.0
boilerplate new project my-first-project

Then run uv run pytest inside my-first-project. The Quickstart walks every step with expected output, and Installation covers manual setup.

docs.title: CLI examples
docs.text: A few common tasks with concise, copy-pastable commands.

docs.title: Discover templates
docs.text:
• List the templates you can create a project from:
boilerplate list

  Name        Version   Description
 ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  project     0.3.0     A general-purpose Python project, with its tools configured.
  streamlit   0.2.0     A Streamlit app, built on the general-purpose template.

docs.title: Create a new project
docs.text:
• Latest project template into a new folder:
boilerplate new project my_app
  • Non-interactive with defaults, overwrite a non-empty destination:
boilerplate new project --non-interactive -f my_app

docs.title: Inspect a template graph
docs.text:
• Text tree format (the streamlit template extends project, so its graph shows the chain):
boilerplate graph streamlit --format tree

- streamlit@0.2.0
  - project@0.3.0
  • JSON written to file:
boilerplate graph streamlit --format json -o graph.json

The JSON payload's shape (the streamlit template extends project, so its graph has two layers):

{
  "sequence": [
    "project@0.3.0",
    "streamlit@0.2.0"
  ],
  "layers": [
    {
      "specifier": "project@0.3.0",
      "name": "project",
      "version": "0.3.0",
      "path": ".../templates/project",
      "deps": []
    },
    {
      "specifier": "streamlit@0.2.0",
      "name": "streamlit",
      "version": "0.2.0",
      "path": ".../templates/streamlit",
      "deps": ["project@0.3.0"]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Compose a template
docs.text:
• Show final merged questions and the per-layer contributions:
boilerplate compose project --sections final,layers
  • Export all major sections to a directory and stay quiet:
boilerplate compose project --all -o out --quiet
  • Quick shape check with the stats section:
boilerplate compose project --sections stats

Layers: project@0.3.0
STATS
layers: 1
layers_count: 1
total_keys: 41
total_scalars: 37
top_level_fields: 10
directives:
  - _jinja_extensions
  - _secret_questions
  - _tasks
tasks: 1
max_depth: 3
delta_keys: null
delta_scalars: null

docs.title: Boilerplate CLI reference
docs.text: Use the Boilerplate CLI to scaffold projects, inspect compositions, and list templates. See also CLI Examples for common workflows.

docs.title: boilerplate
docs.text:
Pairs a Python development environment, one tool for each job, with templates that build on one another to stamp out projects.

Get started:

boilerplate list
boilerplate new project my-app
boilerplate new streamlit my-dashboard

Usage:

boilerplate [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

Options:

  -v, --verbose                Enable debug logging.
  -q, --quiet                  Hide the banner and progress, success, and hint
                               messages.
  --color <auto|always|never>  Color output.  [default: auto]
  --ci                         Never prompt and log JSON to stderr. Implies
                               --non-interactive on new.
  --version                    Show version and exit.
  --install-completion         Install completion for the current shell.
  --show-completion            Show completion for the current shell, to copy
                               it or customize the installation.

docs.title: compose
docs.text:
Show the merged configuration a template composes, layer by layer.

  • final: the fully merged configuration
  • layers: each layer's own values
  • states: each layer's configuration after it applies
  • deltas: what each layer changed
  • stats: summary counts

Prints to stdout by default. --output writes each section to a file in a directory.

Usage:

boilerplate compose [OPTIONS] {template}

Options:

  template                Template to use (name or name@version).  [required]
  --sections <str>        Sections to show, comma-separated: final, layers,
                          states, deltas, stats.
  --all                   Show every section.
  --stats                 Show only the summary.
  --format <yaml|json>    Output format.  [default: yaml]
  -o, --output <path>     Directory to write the sections into.
  --quiet                 Print nothing to stdout; pair with --output to only
                          write files.
  --templates-dir <path>  Extra directory to search for templates, in addition
                          to the bundled ones.

docs.title: graph
docs.text:
Show the layers a template is built from, in the order they apply.

Visualizes template dependencies in three formats:

  • table: numbered list with each layer's path
  • tree: which template extends which
  • json: the same data for tools

Usage:

boilerplate graph [OPTIONS] {template}

Options:

  template                    Template to use (name or name@version).
                              [required]
  --templates-dir <path>      Extra directory to search for templates, in
                              addition to the bundled ones.
  --format <table|tree|json>  Output format.  [default: table]
  -o, --output <path>         Write the JSON to this file instead of stdout.

docs.title: list
docs.text:
List the templates you can create a project from.

Usage:

boilerplate list [OPTIONS]

Options:

  --templates-dir <path>      Extra directory to search for templates, in
                              addition to the bundled ones.
  --format <table|json|wide>  Output format.  [default: table]

docs.title: new
docs.text:
Create a new project from a template.

Usage:

boilerplate new [OPTIONS] {template_spec} [destination]

Options:

  template_spec           Template to use (name or name@version).  [required]
  destination             Destination directory. Required unless a terminal
                          can prompt for it.
  -f, --force             Overwrite a non-empty destination. Does not imply
                          --non-interactive.
  --non-interactive       Use defaults without prompting; fail when a required
                          question has none.
  -n, --dry-run           Show the layers and destination without writing any
                          files.
  --no-tasks              Skip the template's post-creation tasks.
  --data <str>            Answer for one question, as key=value. May be
                          repeated.
  --data-file <path>      YAML file of question: answer pairs (UTF-8).
  --format <text|json>    Output format.  [default: text]
  --templates-dir <path>  Extra directory to search for templates, in addition
                          to the bundled ones.

docs.title: validate
docs.text:
Check that a template directory is well-formed.

Usage:

boilerplate validate [OPTIONS] {template_dir}

Options:

  template_dir          Path to the template directory to validate.
                        [required]
  --format <text|json>  Output format.  [default: text]
  --strict              Treat warnings as errors.

docs.title: Option notes
docs.text: Option Note --color auto Colors stdout and stderr independently, each only when that stream is itself a terminal; turns color off on both when NO_COLOR or BOILERPLATE_ACCESSIBLE is set. list --format wide Adds each template's path as a column. new --format json One JSON object with template, destination, and layers; --dry-run adds dry_run: true.

docs.title: Shell completion
docs.text:
Tab completion for commands and options is built in. Run this once from the shell you want it in, then restart the terminal:

boilerplate --install-completion

The CLI detects your shell and supports bash, zsh, fish, and PowerShell (Windows PowerShell and PowerShell 7). Installing writes to your home directory:

Shell What --install-completion writes bash ~/.bash_completions/boilerplate.sh, sourced from ~/.bashrc zsh ~/.zfunc/_boilerplate, plus fpath and compinit lines in ~/.zshrc fish ~/.config/fish/completions/boilerplate.fish PowerShell The completion script, appended to your PowerShell profile; also sets the CurrentUser execution policy to Unrestricted

To read the script before installing it, or to place it yourself, print it for the detected shell:

boilerplate --show-completion

Completion covers command and option names; template names are not completed.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Every environment variable the CLI reads. The generic CI variable is never read — only the BOILERPLATE_-prefixed flags below switch modes. BOILERPLATE_CI, BOILERPLATE_NON_INTERACTIVE, BOILERPLATE_ACCESSIBLE, and BOILERPLATE_NO_BANNER are on for any value except unset, empty, 0, or false (case-insensitive); NO_COLOR is on by mere presence, any value included; the Settings-parsed variables below accept 1/0, true/false, yes/no, on/off, and exit 2 (CONFIG_ERROR) on anything else. The Settings variables are also read from a .env file in the working directory. PYTHONIOENCODING is forced to utf-8 while a template renders and restored afterward — it's not read as a setting.

Variable Effect Where it's read BOILERPLATE_CI Same as the global --ci flag: forces CI mode (non-interactive; post-generation tasks still run unless --no-tasks is passed) and one-JSON-object-per-event logs on stderr. boilerplate.cli.cli BOILERPLATE_NON_INTERACTIVE Same as boilerplate new --non-interactive: renders without prompting. boilerplate.cli.commands.new BOILERPLATE_ACCESSIBLE Same as --color never (forces color-free output), and hides the banner. boilerplate.cli.display.core, boilerplate.cli.display.terminal_probe BOILERPLATE_NO_BANNER Hides the banner: the braille logo and ASCII name that open the top-level help. boilerplate.cli.display.terminal_probe TERM dumb or unknown hides the banner; linux (the Linux text console) prints its name without the braille logo. boilerplate.cli.display.terminal_probe NO_COLOR The standard color-disable convention; disables console color, prints the banner's name without its braille logo, and switches log output from Rich to one JSON object per event. boilerplate.cli.display.core, boilerplate.logging_config BOILERPLATE_DEBUG Same as --verbose when --verbose isn't passed: sets DEBUG-level logging. boilerplate.settings.Settings, applied in boilerplate.cli.cli BOILERPLATE_REQUEST_ID Correlation ID attached to every structured log line for the invocation; auto-generated once per run when unset. boilerplate.logging_config BOILERPLATE_DEFAULT_TEMPLATES_DIR Overrides the bundled templates directory searched first. boilerplate.settings.Settings BOILERPLATE_EXTRA_TEMPLATE_DIRS Adds directories searched after the default, as a JSON array: ["C:/tpls","D:/more"]. boilerplate.settings.Settings BOILERPLATE_LOG_DIR, BOILERPLATE_FILE_LOGGING_ENABLED Parsed and validated at startup (an invalid value exits 2); no command consumes them yet. boilerplate.settings.Settings APPDATA Locates the config directory holding profile.toml on Windows (%APPDATA%\boilerplate\). boilerplate.settings.paths XDG_CONFIG_HOME Locates the config directory holding profile.toml on POSIX ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/boilerplate/, falling back to ~/.config/boilerplate/). boilerplate.settings.paths

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Every command exits with one of six codes (defined in boilerplate.constants.ExitCode):

Code Name Meaning 0 SUCCESS Command completed. 1 FAILURE Unexpected error. 2 CONFIG_ERROR Configuration could not be loaded. 3 VALIDATION_ERROR Input failed validation: an unknown command or option, bad answers, a missing interactive terminal (TTY), conflicting options, or a non-empty destination without --force. 4 ACTION_REQUIRED Recoverable pause; user intervention needed. Defined in the taxonomy but not yet produced by any shipped command — its first producer will be the planned update conflict pause. 130 USER_CANCELLED Cancelled at a prompt (Ctrl+C).

boilerplate validate <template_dir> reports a template that fails its own checks (missing or malformed boilerplate.yml/copier.yml, duplicate keys, schema errors, or a --strict warning) on exit code 1 (FAILURE), not 3 — exit 3 there is reserved for a malformed invocation, namely a template_dir argument that isn't a directory at all.

docs.title: Error codes
docs.text:
Every BP_* code in the shipped exception hierarchy. A code the error boundary can render but no command produces is marked as such. The code appears as a bracketed suffix on the Error: line (e.g. [BP_INPUT_DATA_INVALID]), usually with a Fix: line giving the remediation.

Code When it's raised Fix BP_CONFIG_DIR_INVALID A configured template directory — the default templates directory (bundled, or overridden by BOILERPLATE_DEFAULT_TEMPLATES_DIR), --templates-dir, or a BOILERPLATE_EXTRA_TEMPLATE_DIRS entry — doesn't exist, isn't a directory, or can't be read. Point the option or environment variable at a directory that exists and is readable. BP_RESOLVE_TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND Defined but not produced by any shipped command; a missing template by name/version surfaces as BP_RESOLVE_DEP_NOT_FOUND. — BP_VERSION_INVALID Reserved for a version string that fails PEP 440 validation. Defined in the exception hierarchy but not yet produced by any shipped command — an invalid version inside a template reference currently surfaces as BP_INPUT_SPECIFIER_INVALID instead. — BP_RENDER_DEST_NOT_EMPTY boilerplate new was given a destination directory that already holds files or folders, hidden ones included, without --force. Nothing is asked or written. Choose a new or empty directory, or add --force to overwrite the files in this one. BP_INPUT_FORCE_REQUIRED Defined but not produced by any shipped command. — BP_INPUT_SPECIFIER_INVALID A name@version template reference is malformed — an invalid name, or a version segment that isn't PEP 440 compliant, including inside an extends reference. Use the format name or name@version. BP_RESOLVE_METADATA_INVALID A template's boilerplate.yml/copier.yml is invalid: schema errors, or a name@version tag that disagrees with the directory's declared metadata. Fix the metadata file; boilerplate validate <template_dir> reports which check failed. BP_INPUT_ANSWERS_MISSING Non-interactive render cannot proceed: a template question has no default: and you supplied no value for it. The error message names the specific fields. In priority order: pass --data key=value (repeatable, never prompted for) or --data-file <path> (a YAML mapping) for the missing answers; or have the template author add a default: (ideally computed, e.g. default: "{{ _folder_name }}" — see template authoring); or drop --ci/--non-interactive and answer the prompts. BP_INPUT_DATA_INVALID --data/--data-file failed to parse ahead of any render attempt: a --data entry with no =; an empty or whitespace-only key; a key starting with _ (Copier's reserved namespace); a --data-file path that doesn't exist or isn't UTF-8; content that isn't valid YAML or isn't a mapping; or a data-file key that isn't a string (YAML reads unquoted on/off/yes/no/bare numbers as non-string values). Fix the flag or file and re-run; nothing is rendered when this error fires. BP_INPUT_TTY_REQUIRED boilerplate new was invoked in interactive mode (the default) but stdin isn't a terminal — typical in CI pipelines, piped input, scripted shells, and < NUL redirection on Windows. Pass --non-interactive (or the global --ci, which precedes the subcommand: boilerplate --ci new …), or set BOILERPLATE_NON_INTERACTIVE/BOILERPLATE_CI once for many call sites; or run from an interactive terminal. --dry-run is exempt — it never prompts. BP_INPUT_DEST_REQUIRED boilerplate new ran with --non-interactive or --ci and no destination argument; the current directory is never assumed. Pass the destination as the second argument: boilerplate new <template> <destination>. Interactively, the CLI prompts for it. BP_RENDER_PROMPT_FAILED Copier's prompt machinery can't display in the current terminal: Git Bash pseudo-TTYs on Windows, Docker entrypoints without -it, editor-embedded shells, or Windows CI runners without a real console buffer. Run from a real terminal (PowerShell, cmd.exe, a Linux tty, or Docker with -it), or pass --ci with values that satisfy every question. BP_RENDER_USER_CANCELLED You pressed Ctrl+C while boilerplate new was showing an interactive prompt; exits 130, the same code every Ctrl+C in the CLI produces. The render stops without printing collected answers or template paths. Re-run boilerplate new, or pass --non-interactive with answers for every question to skip prompting entirely. BP_RESOLVE_DEP_NOT_FOUND An extends reference (or a versioned template reference) names a template that can't be resolved in the catalog. Run boilerplate list and correct the reference. BP_GRAPH_CYCLE The dependency graph formed by extends references contains a cycle, including a template that extends itself. Remove the cyclical extends reference. BP_RESOLVE_VERSION_CONFLICT The same template name resolves to two different versions within one dependency graph. Align all references to a single exact version. BP_RESOLVE_MERGE_CONFLICT Layers provide incompatible values for the same question during merge — mismatched types, or no value/version supplied at all. Reconcile the conflicting question across the layers' copier.yml files. BP_CONFIG_PROFILE_INVALID profile.toml exists but isn't valid TOML, or its [defaults]/[templates.<name>] section isn't a table. Fix the file's TOML syntax or table structure; the error message names the specific section.

docs.title: Customization
docs.text:
Every template — current and future — can be customized three ways, ordered by power. Reach for the least powerful mechanism that works:

You want to… Use Grain Set a value stamped into output (an index URL, a registry, your name) Profile (profile.toml) a value Add or replace whole files, shareably a layer — a template that extends another structure Anything else (edit files a template never anticipated) your own script after boilerplate new behavior

docs.title: Profile (profile.toml)
docs.text:
Create profile.toml in the boilerplate config directory (%APPDATA%\boilerplate\ on Windows; $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/boilerplate/ or ~/.config/boilerplate/ elsewhere):

[defaults]                      # fills a matching question in ANY template
author_name = "Jane Dev"
package_index_url = "https://pkgs.example.com/org/_packaging/feed/pypi/simple/"

[templates.streamlit]           # only for this template; overrides [defaults]
container_registry = "myregistry.azurecr.io"
  • Keys are template question names (see each template's copier.yml). The only reserved names are the two table headers; a key matching no question is ignored.
  • Precedence, high to low: your interactive answer › [templates.<name>] › [defaults] › the template's own default. Defaults pre-fill prompts — you can still override at the prompt; --non-interactive takes them as-is.

docs.title: Questions the first-party templates share
docs.text: Question Templates Effect package_index_url project and everything extending it emits a default [[tool.uv.index]] block in the generated pyproject.toml (empty = public PyPI, no block) sample_module project and everything extending it renders module.py and its test (default on; off renders test_import.py instead; a layer that extends project can default it off) build_backend project and everything extending it build backend in the generated pyproject.toml: uv_build (default) or hatchling, which also renders the [tool.hatch] wheel table — see Choose a build backend container_registry streamlit registry used by the generated push-container.sh; authentication is chosen by registry hostname — see Pushing container images author_name / author_email project and everything extending it project metadata

docs.title: Layers (structure)
docs.text:
Need files a template doesn't ship? Author a template that extends it and add them — composition merges files, questions, and tasks:

# my-org-project/boilerplate.yml
schema_version: "1"
name: org-project
version: 0.1.0
description: Org house style on top of the general-purpose template.
extends: [project]

The folder also needs a copier.yml; template discovery skips a folder that lacks either file.

Point boilerplate at its parent directory with --templates-dir (or set the BOILERPLATE_EXTRA_TEMPLATE_DIRS environment variable — a JSON list of paths, e.g. BOILERPLATE_EXTRA_TEMPLATE_DIRS='["C:/my/templates"]', in the environment or a .env file in the working directory; a bare path string is rejected) and run boilerplate new org-project. The option adds to the search path rather than replacing it, so bundled templates like project stay resolvable for extends. Your layer applies when you create a project; carrying later changes from project into projects you've already made is planned.

docs.title: Your own script (behavior)
docs.text:
For anything neither values nor layers cover — appending to a generated file, registering the project somewhere — run your own script after generation:

boilerplate new project my-app
./my-post-gen.ps1 my-app

Boilerplate deliberately does not manage these scripts.

docs.title: The org pattern
docs.text:
An organization's customization is two plain files delivered by one org-owned script, run once per developer machine after the canonical installer:

  1. uv.toml — points the machine's package resolution at the org feed (plus credential tooling such as keyring). This is uv configuration, not boilerplate's.
  2. profile.toml — the org's generation defaults (above).

A reference script an org can adapt (fictional acme names):

#Requires -Version 7
# acme-setup.ps1 — run AFTER the public boilerplate installer.
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

# 1. Machine package resolution: authenticated org feed for uv.
uv tool install keyring --with artifacts-keyring
$UvDir = Join-Path $env:APPDATA 'uv'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $UvDir | Out-Null
@'
keyring-provider = "subprocess"
publish-url = "https://pkgs.example.com/acme/_packaging/feed/pypi/upload/"
check-url = "https://VssSessionToken@pkgs.example.com/acme/_packaging/feed/pypi/simple/"

[[index]]
name = "acme"
url = "https://VssSessionToken@pkgs.example.com/acme/_packaging/feed/pypi/simple/"
default = true
'@ | Set-Content (Join-Path $UvDir 'uv.toml') -Encoding utf8

# 2. Generation defaults: stamped into every project the developer creates.
$BpDir = Join-Path $env:APPDATA 'boilerplate'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $BpDir | Out-Null
@'
[defaults]
package_index_url = "https://pkgs.example.com/acme/_packaging/feed/pypi/simple/"

[templates.streamlit]
container_registry = "acme.azurecr.io"
'@ | Set-Content (Join-Path $BpDir 'profile.toml') -Encoding utf8

Write-Host "Acme configuration applied."

Hosting, verifying, and updating that script is the org's business — the same trust boundary as the rest of its machine setup. Note the script overwrites any personal profile.toml; on org machines that is usually what you want.

docs.title: What do I need before installing Boilerplate?
docs.text: Nothing — see Before you start for what uv provisions for you and what the Windows installer adds.

docs.title: Do I need administrator rights?
docs.text: Only for the winget (Windows Package Manager) installs on Windows — see Before you start.

docs.title: Is -ExecutionPolicy Bypass in the install command safe?
docs.text: Yes — it is scoped to that one process; see Before you start.

docs.title: What does Boilerplate do?
docs.text: Boilerplate generates a ready-to-code Python project from one or more composed templates in a single command. See Why Boilerplate? for the full picture.

docs.title: How is this different from applying multiple Copier templates to one project?
docs.text: Copier can apply several independent templates to one project (one answers file each), which works when the templates touch disjoint files. Boilerplate adds author-declared composition (extends) on top of Copier: one command, one merged question set, and deterministic precedence when layers overlap the same files. See Why Boilerplate? for the full comparison.

docs.title: How do I get accessible, color-free output?
docs.text: Set BOILERPLATE_ACCESSIBLE=1 (or the standard NO_COLOR) — see Environment variables.

docs.title: How do I report a security vulnerability?
docs.text: Do not open a public GitHub issue. Report vulnerabilities privately by following the Security policy. This keeps details confidential until a fix is available.

docs.title: How do I report a bug, request a feature, or contribute?
docs.text: See the Contributing guide to get started, or Reporting bugs and requesting features for issues.
