first-party templates · core:FirstPartyTemplates Templates Boilerplate publishes as their own git repositories, extracted from the authoring monorepo at release time — the canonical first-party distribution channel (versus user-provided or third-party templates).

  • Kind of: core:Template
  • Related: model:StarterTemplates, trust:TrustLevel, trust:FirstPartyGatingScaffolding, trust:PEPDiscipline, core:PEP
  • Stored in: src/boilerplate/templates/ (the authoring monorepo's copies)
  • See: docs/design/adr-006-template-distribution.md; design 03 §First-Party Templates

Template Specifier · core:TemplateSpecifier A name@version string uniquely identifying a template — the resolved form.

  • Related: core:Template, composition:DependencyGraph
  • Not to be confused with: composition:TemplateReference (the unresolved input form, which may omit the version)
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/types/template_specifier.py
  • See: design 02 §TemplateSpecifier

Question · core:Question A Copier-declared input on a Template, whose answer fills the rendered output; a Template declares zero or more in copier.yml.

  • Part of: core:Template
  • Related: core:Copier, composition:AnswersFile, composition:HiddenQuestion, composition:ScopedView, composition:FullMergedSchema, customization:Profile, customization:AnswerPreset
  • Stored in: the declaring template's copier.yml (owned by Copier; Boilerplate reads it and MUST NOT write to it)
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/integrations/copier_types.py (Copier's Question, imported), src/boilerplate/composition/merging/strategies.py (merge_questions)
  • Avoid: variable, prompt, field
  • Matches: question, in Copier's documentation (exact)

schema v1 · core:SchemaV1 The first generation of this design suite's on-disk contracts (schema_version major 1, e.g. "1" / "boilerplate/lock@1"). Independent of the tool's release version (SemVer 0.x until the first stable 1.0), which tracks implementation maturity, not contract generation.

  • Related: core:Template, composition:LockFile
  • Stored in: the schema_version field of boilerplate.yml and of boilerplate.lock
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/models/template_meta.py, src/boilerplate/models/boilerplate_lock.py
  • See: design 03 §Schema Evolution

PEP · core:PEP Python Enhancement Proposal — the standards process for the Python language. Referenced PEPs: 440 (versioning), 508 (dependency specifiers), 517/518 (build system), 621 (project metadata), 660 (editable installs), 723 (inline script metadata).

  • Related: trust:PEPDiscipline, core:FirstPartyTemplates
  • See: design 01 §Standards compliance in first-party templates

Atomic Staged Write Pattern · core:AtomicStagedWritePattern Boilerplate's stage-then-rename file-emission discipline: stage in an isolated directory, validate, then atomically move into place.

  • Related: composition:SafeUpdate, provisioning:EnvironmentProvisioning
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/project_state/atomic_write.py, src/boilerplate/composition/staging/staging_worktree.py, src/boilerplate/composition/staging/intent_journal.py, src/boilerplate/composition/staging/stale_cleanup.py
  • See: design 07 §Atomic Staged Write Pattern (canonical definition)

Settings · core:Settings Boilerplate's own runtime configuration: one immutable object, loaded once at CLI startup and passed to every application service.

  • Related: customization:Profile
  • Not to be confused with: model:Configuration (the Toolchain's settings in a generated project, not Boilerplate's own)
  • Stored in: compiled-in defaults, overridden by a .env file in the current directory, then by BOILERPLATE_* environment variables
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/settings/settings.py
  • See: design 09 §Settings

docs.title: model
docs.text:
The reference model: what Boilerplate is.

Reference model · model:ReferenceModel The model of what Boilerplate is: Curation picks the Toolchain from the Tool landscape; the Toolchain is a part of the Development Environment, and the Starter templates carry it too; golden paths run on it; Guardrails check the work. Every other statement of what Boilerplate is derives from it.

  • Related: model:Curation
  • See: Developer platform architecture §The model (docs/reference/platform/index.md), which owns it

Environment · model:Environment The problem domain — a developer's setup and its tendency to diverge across machines and time ("environment drift") — and the umbrella over the Development Environment (the thing) and Environment Provisioning (the subsystem). In prose, avoid the bare word where one specific sense is meant.

  • Related: model:DevelopmentEnvironment, provisioning:EnvironmentProvisioning

Tool landscape · model:ToolLandscape The descriptive catalog of the tools, technologies and practices available in a domain, organized by slot, answering what exists?; the Toolchain is curated from it. Boilerplate keeps it as the Development Environment Landscape guide.

  • Part of: model:ReferenceModel
  • Related: model:Slot, model:Curation, model:Toolchain
  • Stored in: docs/design/dev-environment-landscape.md
  • See: Developer platform architecture §The tool landscape (docs/reference/platform/index.md)

slot · model:Slot One recurring role in a development environment (linter, type checker, test runner, …). Each first-party template fills the slots its ecosystem's dev loop uses with one opinionated tool each; the template then fills slots within those slots (each tool's per-project configuration).

  • Part of: model:ToolLandscape
  • Related: model:Toolchain, model:Configuration, model:DevLoop, core:FirstPartyTemplates
  • See: design 01 §What Boilerplate is (the slot model); docs/design/dev-environment-landscape.md, which catalogues the slots

Curation · model:Curation Choosing the Toolchain's picks from the Tool landscape as a set, each for how it works with the others, then configuring them together and maintaining them together. It joins the Development Environment and the Starter templates, which carry the same picks.

  • Related: model:ReferenceModel, model:ToolLandscape, model:Toolchain, model:DevelopmentEnvironment, model:StarterTemplates

Toolchain · model:Toolchain The development tools Boilerplate picks and sets up, one per slot (uv, Ruff, Pyright, pytest, …), chosen by Curation from the Tool landscape, whether or not their versions are pinned; it answers what do we use? and is not an application's own framework stack. Environment Provisioning pins the tools through an EnvironmentProfile, and not every pick is pinned (the editor and git are not).

  • Part of: model:DevelopmentEnvironment
  • Related: model:Slot, model:Curation, model:ToolLandscape, model:Configuration, model:StarterTemplates, provisioning:EnvironmentProvisioning, provisioning:EnvironmentProfile
  • Not to be confused with: model:DevelopmentEnvironment (which contains the Toolchain; not a synonym)
  • See: Developer platform architecture §The toolchain (docs/reference/platform/index.md)
  • Avoid: curated stack, dev stack, tech stack
  • Carve-out: the slogan "Less Yak. More Stack." puns on the toolchain handed to you and templates stacking; outside it, a template layers on another. The reference model page names "curated stack" once, as something the toolchain is sometimes called.
  • Matches: curated stack, in platform engineering per docs/reference/platform/index.md (close)

Development Environment · model:DevelopmentEnvironment The setup a developer works in, on the machine, in the project and in the editor: the Toolchain, its Configuration (pyproject.toml, .vscode/), the Project Layout, and the dev loop. In the reference model the Toolchain is a part of it, and the Starter templates sit beside it.

  • Part of: model:ReferenceModel
  • Related: model:Environment, model:StarterTemplates, model:Configuration, model:ProjectLayout, model:DevLoop
  • Not to be confused with: model:Toolchain (one of its parts, not a synonym), provisioning:EnvironmentProvisioning (the subsystem that installs it and pins the Toolchain's versions)
  • See: the Development Environment guide (docs/environment/index.md)

Configuration · model:Configuration The settings that wire the Toolchain into a project — pyproject.toml and .vscode/.

  • Part of: model:DevelopmentEnvironment
  • Related: model:Toolchain, model:Slot, provisioning:EnvironmentProfile
  • Not to be confused with: core:Settings (Boilerplate's own runtime configuration, not a generated project's)
  • Stored in: a generated project's pyproject.toml and .vscode/, rendered from src/boilerplate/templates/project/pyproject.toml.jinja and src/boilerplate/templates/project/.vscode/
  • See: the Development Environment guide §Configuration (docs/environment/index.md)

Project Layout · model:ProjectLayout The standard project structure — src/, tests/, and their conventions.

  • Part of: model:DevelopmentEnvironment
  • Stored in: src/boilerplate/templates/project/ (its src/ and tests/ scaffold)
  • See: the Development Environment guide §Project layout (docs/environment/index.md)

workflow · model:Workflow The steps taken to get a job done. GitHub Actions workflow files keep their own name.

  • Related: model:GoldenPath

golden path · model:GoldenPath A workflow whose decisions are already thought out for you: the supported, opinionated route through one job, answering how do we work? Golden paths nest: each template is a golden path to a starting point, solving the plumbing so a project starts ready for work, and the dev loop is the golden path for the everyday work that follows.

  • Kind of: model:Workflow
  • Part of: model:ReferenceModel
  • Related: model:DevLoop, model:StarterTemplates, core:Template
  • See: Developer platform architecture §The golden path (docs/reference/platform/index.md)
  • Avoid: paved road, paved path
  • Matches: paved road, in Netflix's vocabulary per docs/reference/platform/index.md (exact)

dev loop · model:DevLoop The cycle you repeat inside a project, which is test-driven development's red-green-refactor: write a failing test (red), make it pass with the least code (green), refactor with the tests still green, then run the checks and commit. Many turns make one pull request, and a release gathers many pull requests.

  • Kind of: model:GoldenPath
  • Part of: model:DevelopmentEnvironment
  • Related: model:Slot
  • Avoid: inner loop, developer workflow, development workflow

Starter templates · model:StarterTemplates The Templates, answering how do we start?: each a golden path to a starting point that carries the Toolchain's project and editor picks. Outside the reference model, say Template.

  • Part of: model:ReferenceModel
  • Related: core:Template, core:FirstPartyTemplates, model:GoldenPath, model:Toolchain, model:DevelopmentEnvironment, model:Curation
  • See: Developer platform architecture §Starter templates (docs/reference/platform/index.md)

Guardrails · model:Guardrails The automated checks that verify a project against the standards its templates configure — dev-time in a Development Environment (format-on-save, live type-checking) and in CI — answering how do we comply?

  • Part of: model:ReferenceModel
  • Related: model:DevelopmentEnvironment, trust:FirstPartyGatingScaffolding, trust:PostRenderValidation, trust:PreconfiguredSubstrate
  • See: Developer platform architecture §Guardrails (docs/reference/platform/index.md)

docs.title: composition
docs.text:
How templates layer into one project, and the lock, answers and update mechanics.

extends-based composition · composition:ExtendsBasedComposition The static extends: mechanism in template metadata that drives composition. Not a runtime feature; resolved at composition time.

  • Related: composition:Layer, composition:DependencyGraph, core:Template
  • Stored in: the extends field of boilerplate.yml
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/models/template_meta.py, src/boilerplate/composition/resolution/resolver.py
  • See: design 03 §extends syntax; design 04 §Stage 1 — Resolver

Layer · composition:Layer One template rendered at a node of the Dependency Graph, each with its own Answers File; a derived Layer (also "derived template" in prose) extends another Template to add or override its files. As a verb, a template layers on the template it extends; in plain prose, templates build on one another.

  • Kind of: core:Template
  • Part of: composition:DependencyGraph
  • Related: composition:ExtendsBasedComposition, composition:AnswersFile, composition:ScopedView, customization:Profile, customization:Task
  • Not to be confused with: trust:Substrate (an enforcement area's mode; PROD-001's enforcement_layers key is not a composition Layer)
  • Stored in: its LockLayer record in boilerplate.lock and its own .copier-answers.<layer>.yml, both in the generated project
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/composition/models/composition_layer.py, src/boilerplate/models/lock_layer.py
  • Avoid: plugin, overlay, mixin
  • Carve-out: "overlay merge" names ADR-011's deep-merge strategy for downstream structured-file customization, not this term.

Non-git layer · composition:NonGitLayer A composition layer whose template source has no git history (a plain filesystem directory or an archive). It records commit: null in the lock; update skips it with a warning — Copier has no built-in fallback merge for it — and copier recopy is the manual refresh.

  • Kind of: composition:Layer
  • Related: composition:LockFile, composition:SafeUpdate, core:Copier
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/project_state/lock_builder.py (records no commit for a folder layer)
  • See: design 06 §Step 4: Three-Way Merge

Dependency Graph · composition:DependencyGraph The directed acyclic graph (DAG) of template specifiers, derived from extends chains.

  • Related: core:TemplateSpecifier, composition:ExtendsBasedComposition
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/composition/models/graph.py (CompositionGraph), src/boilerplate/composition/graph/topology.py, src/boilerplate/composition/resolution/resolver.py
  • See: design 04 §Stage 2 — Dependency Graph and Topological Sort

Template Reference · composition:TemplateReference The input form of a Template Specifier — name or name@version — before resolution.

  • Not to be confused with: core:TemplateSpecifier (the resolved form, always name@version)
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/composition/resolution/resolver.py (the resolver takes it as template_ref)
  • See: design 04 §Template Reference Syntax

Scoped View · composition:ScopedView A Layer's merged questions, secret-question list and Jinja extensions over itself and its ancestors; every render of that Layer, at compose and at update, uses it.

  • Related: composition:Layer, composition:HiddenQuestion, core:Question
  • Not to be confused with: composition:FullMergedSchema (every Layer's questions joined, not one Layer and its ancestors)
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/composition/views/layer_view.py, src/boilerplate/composition/views/layer_view_builder.py, src/boilerplate/composition/views/scope_composition.py
  • See: design 04 §Scoped view

Full Merged Schema · composition:FullMergedSchema Every Layer's questions joined; the questionnaire at compose uses it, and an update step takes each question's definition and default from it.

  • Related: core:Question, composition:SafeUpdate
  • Not to be confused with: composition:ScopedView (one Layer and its ancestors only)
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/composition/merging/merger.py, src/boilerplate/composition/rendering/questionnaire.py
  • See: design 04 §Scoped view and §Safe Update

Hidden Question · composition:HiddenQuestion A Question whose when evaluates false under the recorded answers, the literal when: false derived questions among them; no Answers File records it.

  • Kind of: core:Question
  • Related: composition:AnswersFile, composition:ScopedView
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/composition/rendering/hidden_questions.py
  • See: design 04 §Safe Update

RenderEngine · composition:RenderEngine The proper-noun class that orchestrates Copier across composition layers.

  • Related: core:Copier, composition:Layer, composition:ScopedView
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/composition/rendering/engine.py
  • See: design 04 §Stage 4 — RenderEngine

plural-shape architecture · composition:PluralShapeArchitecture Authoring shape that admits future siblings (e.g., ci-azure-pipelines today, ci-github-actions later) by extending the answer-value enum, not by introducing a breaking schema change.

  • Related: core:Question, core:FirstPartyTemplates, composition:Layer
  • See: docs/intentions/INT-006.yaml

Answers File · composition:AnswersFile Records answers given during render, one file per composition layer. Owned by Copier; Boilerplate MUST NOT write to it.

  • Related: core:Copier, core:Question, composition:Layer, composition:HiddenQuestion, composition:UnmanagedProject
  • Not to be confused with: composition:LockFile (boilerplate.lock, owned by Boilerplate), customization:AnswerPreset (a YAML file of answers passed into a render, not Copier's record of one)
  • Stored in: .copier-answers.<layer>.yml in the generated project, where <layer> is the layer's invariant name (matches LockLayer.name)
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/project_state/answers_file.py
  • See: design 04 §Per-Layer Render Loop (the per-layer _answers_file: contract) and §Render Behavior
  • Matches: answers file, in Copier's documentation (exact)

Lock File · composition:LockFile Records exact versions, commit hashes, and checksums used. Owned by Boilerplate.

  • Related: composition:ManagedProject, composition:Layer, composition:NonGitLayer, trust:TOFU, trust:TrustLevel
  • Not to be confused with: composition:AnswersFile (owned by Copier; records answers, not versions)
  • Stored in: boilerplate.lock in a managed project
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/models/boilerplate_lock.py, src/boilerplate/models/lock_layer.py, src/boilerplate/project_state/lock_file.py, src/boilerplate/project_state/lock_builder.py
  • See: design 02 §Lock File Model; design 06 §Step 4: Lock File Generation

Managed project · composition:ManagedProject A project Boilerplate tracks and can update: it has a boilerplate.lock. adopt transitions an unmanaged project to managed.

  • Related: composition:LockFile
  • Not to be confused with: composition:UnmanagedProject (Copier answers files but no boilerplate.lock)
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/composition/adding/layer_adder.py (the lock-present precondition), src/boilerplate/common/exceptions.py (ProjectNotManagedError)
  • See: design 06 §Part 2.5: Project Adoption

Unmanaged project · composition:UnmanagedProject A project with Copier answers file(s) (.copier-answers.*) but no boilerplate.lock — e.g. a plain copier copy project, or one after eject. adopt transitions it to managed.

  • Related: composition:AnswersFile, composition:LockFile
  • Not to be confused with: composition:ManagedProject (has a boilerplate.lock; Boilerplate tracks and can update it)
  • See: design 06 §Part 2.5: Project Adoption and §Part 2.6: Project Ejection

safe update · composition:SafeUpdate The conflict-detected update workflow Boilerplate provides over Copier's per-layer merge: it runs in a Staging worktree and pauses on conflict.

  • Related: core:Copier, composition:FullMergedSchema, composition:HiddenQuestion, composition:CopyBack, composition:RestoreMarker
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/composition/updating/updater.py, src/boilerplate/composition/staging/staging_worktree.py
  • See: design 04 §Safe Update for the implementation

Staging worktree · composition:StagingWorktree The detached git worktree of the project in which update and add run their per-layer walk, so the user's checkout changes only at the Copy back.

  • Related: composition:SafeUpdate, composition:CopyBack, composition:RestoreMarker
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/composition/staging/staging_worktree.py
  • See: design 06 §Staging worktree

Copy back · composition:CopyBack The step of update and add that reproduces the Staging worktree's result in the user's checkout as uncommitted changes: git restore --source=<commit> --worktree -- :/ from the worktree's last per-layer commit.

  • Related: composition:SafeUpdate, composition:RestoreMarker
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/composition/staging/copy_back.py
  • See: design 06 §Staging worktree

Restore marker · composition:RestoreMarker The file under the project's git directory, paired with the ref refs/worktree/boilerplate/restore, that keeps the state of a copy back cut off midway so a rerun can finish it or the user can set it aside.

  • Related: composition:CopyBack, composition:SafeUpdate
  • Stored in: boilerplate-restore.json in the project's git directory, with the ref refs/worktree/boilerplate/restore
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/composition/staging/restore_marker_file.py, src/boilerplate/models/restore_marker.py
  • See: design 06 §Interrupted copy back and §Setting a partial update aside

docs.title: customization
docs.text:
How a user changes what templates produce.

Profile · customization:Profile A user's default answers for Template Questions, read from profile.toml and merged into the render — global [defaults] plus per-Template [templates.<name>].

  • Related: core:Question, core:Template
  • Not to be confused with: provisioning:EnvironmentProfile (boilerplate-env.yml, pinned tool versions; unrelated despite the shared word), customization:AnswerPreset (a YAML file of answers passed to one render, not a user's standing defaults)
  • Stored in: profile.toml at the Boilerplate config root
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/settings/profile.py, src/boilerplate/settings/paths.py
  • See: docs/design/adr-010-profile.md
  • Avoid: typed Profile model, org profile, config

Answer Preset · customization:AnswerPreset A YAML file of answers passed with --data-file to new, update or add, which forces those answers for one run — for CI/CD use or to repeat a project.

  • Related: core:Question
  • Not to be confused with: customization:Profile (a user's standing defaults in profile.toml, not a file passed to one render), composition:AnswersFile (Copier's per-layer record of answers already given; the template's answers file from a finished new can be passed as a preset)
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/cli/commands/new.py (loads a YAML mapping of answers from --data-file)
  • See: design 05 §Answer Presets; design 10 §Answer Preset Safety

Task · customization:Task A command declared in a Template's _tasks that runs after rendering — the escape hatch for arbitrary edits.

  • Part of: core:Template
  • Related: core:Copier, composition:Layer
  • Stored in: _tasks in the declaring template's copier.yml
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/composition/tasks.py
  • See: design 04 §Task Execution Order; docs/design/adr-014-deferred-task-execution.md
  • Avoid: hook, script, post-gen step
  • Matches: task, in Copier's documentation (exact)

docs.title: provisioning
docs.text:
Installing and pinning the Toolchain.

Environment Provisioning · provisioning:EnvironmentProvisioning The subsystem that installs and version-pins a Development Environment — the env apply flow, providers, and the EnvironmentProfile.

  • Related: provisioning:EnvironmentProfile, provisioning:EnvironmentProvisionRecord, provisioning:WASM, model:Environment, model:Toolchain, core:AtomicStagedWritePattern
  • Not to be confused with: model:DevelopmentEnvironment (the setup itself, which this subsystem installs)
  • See: design 08
  • Avoid: Environment Pillar, Environments Pillar

EnvironmentProfile · provisioning:EnvironmentProfile The declarative input to Environment Provisioning: tool versions and configuration.

  • Related: provisioning:EnvironmentProvisioning, provisioning:EnvironmentProvisionRecord, model:Toolchain, core:Template
  • Not to be confused with: customization:Profile (profile.toml, a user's default answers to template questions, see ADR-010; the two are unrelated despite the shared word)
  • Stored in: boilerplate-env.yml
  • See: design 02 §EnvironmentProfile; design 08

EnvironmentProvisionRecord · provisioning:EnvironmentProvisionRecord The schema for the env-state record that Environment Provisioning writes. Use this name when discussing structure, and .boilerplate/environment.yml when discussing the file.

  • Related: provisioning:EnvironmentProvisioning, provisioning:EnvironmentProfile
  • Stored in: .boilerplate/environment.yml in the project
  • See: design 02 §EnvironmentProvisionRecord; design 08 §State Files

WASM · provisioning:WASM WebAssembly — the plugin architecture used by proto for cross-platform tool installation.

  • Related: provisioning:EnvironmentProvisioning
  • See: docs/design/adr-001-build-vs-adopt.md; design 10 §Trust Boundaries

docs.title: trust
docs.text:
What Boilerplate enforces and what it trusts.

substrate · trust:Substrate The enforcement mode PROD-001 assigns to each area of the product it lists under enforcement_layers (the runtime, templates, tool configurations, environments, scaffolded projects) — enforced (Boilerplate's own runtime gates and rejects on violation, with no opt-out) or preconfigured (defaults are shipped; user-runnable first-party gating scaffolding executes the check in third-party venues; the user MAY opt out).

  • Related: trust:PostRenderValidation, trust:PEPDiscipline
  • Not to be confused with: composition:Layer (a rendered template; PROD-001's enforcement_layers key uses the word for an enforcement area, not a template)
  • Stored in: docs/products/PROD-001.yaml (the substrate key of each enforcement_layers entry)
  • See: design 01 §What Boilerplate is

enforced substrate · trust:EnforcedSubstrate The enforced value of substrate: coerce-at-touch-points within Boilerplate's own runtime — schema/parse validation, path-safety (TOCTOU) re-validation, consent/task gating, and lock/checksum verification. Boilerplate rejects on violation with a BP_* code; there is no opt-out.

  • Kind of: trust:Substrate
  • Related: trust:TrustLevel, trust:FirstPartyGatingScaffolding, composition:LockFile
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/common/exceptions.py (BP_* codes), src/boilerplate/models/boilerplate_lock.py (lock schema_version validation), src/boilerplate/repository/template_checksum.py (computes the checksum the lock records)
  • See: docs/products/PROD-001.yaml enforcement_layers.product

preconfigured substrate · trust:PreconfiguredSubstrate The preconfigured value of substrate: Boilerplate ships the defaults, and user-runnable first-party gating scaffolding executes the check in third-party tools' native venues (CI runners, hook runners); the user MAY opt out.

  • Kind of: trust:Substrate
  • Related: trust:FirstPartyGatingScaffolding, model:Guardrails, trust:PostRenderValidation
  • See: docs/products/PROD-001.yaml enforcement_layers.templates and enforcement_layers.tool_configurations

first-party gating scaffolding · trust:FirstPartyGatingScaffolding The CI pipelines, lint configs, and bundled EnvironmentProfile files shipped beside templates as user-runnable parts of the preconfigured substrate. The user opts in; gates execute in third-party tools' native venues (CI runners, hook runners).

  • Part of: trust:PreconfiguredSubstrate
  • Related: core:FirstPartyTemplates, model:Guardrails, trust:EnforcedSubstrate, provisioning:EnvironmentProfile
  • See: docs/products/PROD-001.yaml shipped_gating_scaffolding

post-render validation · trust:PostRenderValidation Out-of-scope content verdicts performed against generated projects after Boilerplate hands off (detecting drift between shipped defaults and user-edited config). Not enforced; structurally outside Boilerplate's reach.

  • Related: trust:Substrate, model:Guardrails
  • See: docs/products/PROD-001.yaml enforcement_layers.tool_configurations; docs/intentions/INT-006.yaml (not_included)

PEP discipline · trust:PEPDiscipline The convention that when a PEP defines the canonical way, first-party templates use it — no custom conventions that duplicate or contradict a PEP.

  • Related: core:PEP, core:FirstPartyTemplates, trust:Substrate
  • See: design 01 §Standards compliance in first-party templates; docs/products/PROD-001.yaml enforcement_layers.templates

Trust Level · trust:TrustLevel Binary classification for a template's origin: trusted or untrusted. Untrusted code is default-deny and requires explicit consent.

  • Related: trust:TOFU, core:FirstPartyTemplates, customization:Task, composition:LockFile
  • Stored in: the trust_level field of each source entry in boilerplate-sources.yml in the user's data directory (the implicit first-party source is trusted); each lock layer's optional free-form trust_tier is a separate field, reserved for richer tiers
  • Defined in: src/boilerplate/models/lock_layer.py (the trust_tier field)
  • See: design 03 §Trust and Verification Levels; design 09 §Catalog Source Configuration File

TOFU · trust:TOFU Trust-on-first-use — a security model where the first interaction with a remote source is trusted, and subsequent interactions are verified against the initial state.

  • Related: trust:TrustLevel, composition:LockFile
  • Stored in: boilerplate.lock (the commit hash and checksum captured after the first fetch); the optional pin expected_commit on a source entry in boilerplate-sources.yml
  • See: design 03 §Git Source; design 02 §CatalogSource (expected_commit)

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines every domain entity in the Boilerplate system: its fields, types, validation rules, and relationships.

All models are immutable once constructed unless otherwise noted. Validation MUST fail fast: reject invalid input at construction time, not lazily during use.

See Product overview for the glossary.

docs.title: Version
docs.text:
A PEP 440-compliant version string. All versions in this system MUST conform to PEP 440 (see PEP 440 for the full grammar and ordering rules).

Non-Python implementations: PEP 440 endorses SemVer clauses 1–8 — every plain X.Y.Z is valid in both grammars and orders identically. Implementations targeting non-Python ecosystems MAY use SemVer only on the X.Y.Z release subset. Pre-releases, build metadata, and post-releases MUST use PEP 440 syntax (1.0a1, 1.0.post1, 1.0.dev1, 1!2.0), not SemVer (1.0.0-alpha.1, 1.0.0+abc) — the orderings disagree (SemVer's lexicographic pre-release order conflicts with PEP 440's aN < bN < rcN). Lock file version fields MUST serialize as PEP 440 strings.

  • Examples: "1.0.0", "2.0.0b1", "0.0.1.post1", "1.2", "0.1.dev3"
  • Comparison: standard PEP 440 ordering (pre-releases sort before releases)
  • Serialization: always a string
  • Validation: MUST reject strings that are not valid PEP 440 versions

Key ordering rules (summary for implementers): - Canonical form: N[.N]+[{a|b|rc}N][.postN][.devN]; 1.0 and 1.0.0 are equal - Epoch: E!N.N sorts above all non-epoch versions - Pre-release order: aN < bN < rcN < release - Post-release: 1.0 < 1.0.post1 - Dev release: 1.0.dev1 < 1.0a1 < 1.0 - When comparing, normalize by treating missing numeric segments as 0 (e.g., 1.0 == 1.0.0)

docs.title: JSON
docs.text:
The JSON type represents any value that can appear in a JSON or YAML document:

JSON = string | integer | float | boolean | null | map[string, JSON] | list[JSON]

All fields of type map[string, JSON] MUST be serializable to both YAML and JSON without loss.

docs.title: TemplateSpecifier
docs.text:
A compound identifier uniquely addressing one version of one template.

Field Type Constraints name string Alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores only version Version MUST be a valid PEP 440 version

String form: {name}@{version} (e.g., project@2.1.0, streamlit@1.0.0b2)

Parsing: Split on the first @ — left side is name, right side is version. Both MUST pass their respective validation.

Ordering: Compare by name lexicographically first; if equal, compare version by PEP 440 ordering.

Equality: Two specifiers are equal iff name and version are both equal.

Errors: - InvalidTemplateSpecifierError — name fails pattern or string is not in name@version form - InvalidVersionError — version is not PEP 440 compliant

docs.title: TemplateMeta
docs.text:
The contents of a template's boilerplate.yml file. Represents Boilerplate-specific metadata about one template.

Field Type Required Default Constraints schema_version string No "1" Schema major version. MUST have major version 1 (i.e., "1", "1.1", etc. are all valid within the 1.x series). See §03 Schema Evolution for forward-compatibility rules. Boilerplate MUST reject templates with an unrecognized major version and SHOULD silently ignore unknown fields within a recognized version. name string Yes — Non-empty; identifies the template logically description string No "" Human-readable summary version Version Yes — Semantic version of this template extends list of string No [] Ordered list of parent template references post_create_message list of string No [] Lines printed after successful project creation; MAY contain Jinja2 variable references. When a composition spans multiple layers, post_create_message from ALL layers in the dependency chain MUST be accumulated and displayed in topological order (base templates first, root template last). Each layer's message is displayed with a header identifying the template source. lifecycle_state string No "published" Template lifecycle state. One of: draft, published, deprecated, archived. successor string or null No null Template name to recommend when this template is deprecated. requires_profile object or null No null Environment profile required by this template; see requires_profile semantics. checksum_excludes list of string No [] Path prefixes to exclude from rendered output checksum computation, in addition to the built-in exclusions (.git/, __pycache__/, .boilerplate/). Template authors MAY use this to exclude generated artifacts (e.g., .venv/, node_modules/). allowed_extensions list of string No [] Per-template Jinja2 extension allowlist; declarative and narrowing, never consent. See allowed_extensions semantics.

Each entry in extends is a template reference in the form name or name@version. Unversioned references resolve to the latest available version at resolution time.

Serialization format (YAML): 

schema_version: "1"
name: project
description: A general-purpose Python project, with its tools configured.
version: "2.1.0"
extends:
  - base@1.0.0
  - standards

Validation rules: - name MUST be non-empty - version MUST be a valid PEP 440 version - schema_version MUST be a recognized major version string - extends entries MUST be non-empty strings; they are not validated for existence at parse time

Load behavior: Given a path, if the path is a directory, load {path}/boilerplate.yml. If it is a file, load that file directly. Raise FileNotFoundError if the file does not exist.

docs.title: requires_profile semantics
docs.text:
When non-null, requires_profile MUST be an object with two fields:

  • name (string, required) — the profile's logical name.
  • version (string, optional) — a PEP 440 version constraint against the profile's own version, used to require a specific profile lineage.

The constraint targets the profile version, not the underlying tool versions. Tool-version requirements are expressed via the profile's own version lineage: profile authors bump the profile version when tool constraints change. Templates do not override individual tools.

See Template system and discovery for the full sub-field specification.

docs.title: allowed_extensions semantics
docs.text:
allowed_extensions lists the import paths of Jinja2 extensions a template intends to load. The list is declarative and narrowing, not a consent grant: it scopes the consent prompt to exactly the listed extensions (rather than to anything the system-wide allowlist permits) and surfaces the requirement to the user before installation.

Consent is still required. An extension loads only when both conditions hold:

  1. Its package appears in the system-wide allowed_extension_packages setting, AND
  2. The user has consented via --allow-extensions, --allow-untrusted, or interactive confirmation per §03 Jinja2 Extension Safety.

Per-template allowed_extensions does NOT waive the user-consent requirement — template-author metadata cannot grant consent on the user's behalf. See Template system and discovery for the full Jinja2 extension safety model.

docs.title: TemplateInfo
docs.text:
A resolved template: metadata paired with its filesystem location.

Field Type Notes name string Template's logical name meta TemplateMeta Parsed boilerplate.yml location path Absolute filesystem path to the template root scaffolding_template opaque handle An opaque reference passed to the render engine. Its internal structure is implementation-defined. Boilerplate treats it as a value object — it MUST NOT modify it after construction.

Computed: - specifier → derived from name and meta.version

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
The output of the Resolver. An immutable snapshot of the dependency traversal result.

Field Type Notes deps DependencyMap Maps each specifier string to its direct dependency specifier strings templates map of string → TemplateInfo Maps specifier string to the resolved TemplateInfo

DependencyMap is a map where: - Key: canonical specifier string (e.g., "project@2.1.0") - Value: ordered list of direct dependency specifier strings

Computed: - execution_sequence → topologically sorted specifier strings, dependencies first

Invariant: Every specifier referenced as a dependency MUST also appear as a key in deps. The Resolver guarantees this.

docs.title: CompositionGraph
docs.text:
The dependency graph artifact within a CompositionArtifact.

Field Type Notes nodes map of string → GraphNode All nodes keyed by specifier string edges map of string → list[string] Adjacency list (specifier → its dependency specifiers), each list in declaration order, deduplicated sequence list[string] Deterministic topological render sequence (dependencies first)

GraphNode:

Field Type Notes name string Template name version string Template version string path path Filesystem path to template root

Operations: - sequence_payload() → map — structured representation for serialization

docs.title: CompositionLayer
docs.text:
A layer is a template participating in a composition. Each layer contributes files and configuration; the composition engine merges them in topological order.

One template's contribution to a composition.

Field Type Required Notes name string Yes Template name version string Yes Template version string path path Yes Filesystem path to template root values map[string, JSON] Yes Question values contributed by this layer state_after map[string, JSON] or null No Cumulative merged state after this layer is applied (null if not tracked) delta map[string, JSON] or null No Keys added or changed by this layer vs previous state (null if not tracked)

Computed views: - state → state_after if present, else empty - delta_view → delta if present, else empty

docs.title: CompositionArtifact
docs.text:
The complete, immutable artifact produced by the Composer. Contains everything needed to render a project.

Field Type Notes graph CompositionGraph The dependency graph (carries the topological sequence) layers list[CompositionLayer] One entry per template, in execution order final map[string, JSON] Fully merged Copier configuration (questions + directives) schema_version string "1" — schema major version

Computed properties: - merged_questions_schema → final with all internal keys (prefixed _) removed — the canonical user questionnaire - stats → CompositionStats (see below) - requires_unsafe → true if final contains Jinja2 extensions requiring Copier's unsafe=true mode

docs.title: CompositionStats
docs.text:
Aggregate metrics derived from a CompositionArtifact. Used by the compose --stats command for debugging and introspection.

Required fields (all implementations MUST include):

Field Type Description layers_count integer Number of template layers in the composition question_count integer Number of user-facing questions in the merged questionnaire task_count integer Number of tasks in the merged _tasks list template_names list[string] Template names in execution order

Additional fields are permitted and encouraged but not required.

docs.title: TemplateCatalog
docs.text:
An in-memory index of all available templates. Not a persistent store.

Lookup strategy: templates are indexed by two keys: 1. Canonical tag: "{name}@{version}" — for exact-version lookup 2. Name + version map: for latest-version resolution

Registration policy: "first one wins" — if two templates share the same canonical tag, the first registered is kept and subsequent duplicates are ignored; a DEBUG-level log message MUST be emitted recording the duplicate tag and the skipped source path.

Operations:

Method Input Output Notes register(template) TemplateInfo void First-wins deduplication register_many(templates) list[TemplateInfo] void Calls register for each get_by_tag(tag) string TemplateInfo or null Exact tag lookup resolve(name, version?) name + optional version TemplateInfo or null Null version returns the entry with the highest version by PEP 440 ordering (same as resolve_latest) resolve_latest(name) name TemplateInfo or null Returns the entry with the highest version by PEP 440 ordering; first-registered wins if versions compare equal list_all() — list[TemplateInfo] All registered templates list_tags() — list[string] All canonical tags len() — integer Count of registered templates

docs.title: TemplateRepository (interface)
docs.text:
An abstract source of templates. Implementations discover and load templates from a specific origin (local directory, remote index, etc.) and return TemplateInfo records.

Required operation: - load_templates() → list[TemplateInfo]

The repository does not register templates; the caller is responsible for populating a catalog.

docs.title: DirectoryTemplateRepository
docs.text:
A TemplateRepository implementation that scans local filesystem directories.

Discovery algorithm: 1. Given a list of directories, scan each directory for subdirectories containing both boilerplate.yml and copier.yml. 2. For each valid template directory: parse boilerplate.yml → TemplateMeta, construct a TemplateInfo. 3. Skip directories that fail validation (log a warning, continue). 4. Per template name, keep only the highest-versioned template found (PEP 440 ordering). If two directories provide the same template at the same version, the template from the lexicographically earlier directory path wins (first-encountered). Multiple versions of the same template in a single directory are not simultaneously available from one repository instance; only the highest is kept.

Validation: A template directory is valid iff: - It contains boilerplate.yml - It contains copier.yml - boilerplate.yml parses without error

docs.title: CatalogEntry
docs.text:
A display and ranking model constructed on demand from a TemplateInfo + CatalogSource pair. Not stored in the catalog — the catalog stores TemplateInfo internally; CatalogEntry is computed when the list command or ranking algorithm needs source-aware metadata.

Field Type Source name string TemplateInfo.name version Version TemplateInfo.meta.version description string TemplateInfo.meta.description tags list[string] Registry metadata; [] for filesystem sources category string Registry metadata; "" for filesystem sources source string CatalogSource.name source_priority integer CatalogSource.priority classification enum boilerplate-enabled or copier-only (determined by file presence) trust_level enum CatalogSource.trust_level; binary trusted/untrusted. Local filesystem sources are untrusted by default; first-party git sources — the published per-template repositories (ADR-006) — are trusted by default, as is any other git source explicitly configured trust_level: trusted. The deferred wheel_bundle source type would be trusted when built. See Template system and discovery. lifecycle_state enum Registry metadata; published for filesystem sources last_updated ISO 8601 datetime Registry metadata; filesystem mtime for filesystem sources dependencies list[string] TemplateInfo.meta.extends successor string or null Registry metadata; null for filesystem sources

docs.title: CatalogSource
docs.text:
A configured origin from which the catalog discovers templates.

Field Type Notes name string Human-readable source identifier (e.g., official, community) type enum Source type (filesystem, git, archive, wheel_bundle, http, github, oci). Implementable types: filesystem, git, and archive (.zip/.tar.gz/.tgz extraction; renamed from the legacy bundle type). wheel_bundle (Git bundle packaged inside the Boilerplate wheel) is deferred as a seed cache pending demonstrated demand (ADR-006). The http, github, and oci types are reserved for future versions. location string URI or path to the source credentials reference Reserved for Phase 4 (remote / third-party sources). Credential reference (env var name, vault path, etc.) for authenticated remote sources. Until Phase 4, sources are local and ignore this field. priority integer Lower number = higher priority; ties broken by registration order trust_level enum Binary trusted/untrusted — the trust level this source can grant. Trusted by default for first-party git sources — the published per-template repositories (ADR-006) — and for any other git source explicitly configured trust_level: trusted; filesystem and archive sources are untrusted by default. The deferred wheel_bundle type would be trusted when built. See Template system and discovery. (The richer tiered model is reserved for Phase 4.) expected_commit string or null TOFU (trust-on-first-use) pinning for git sources: the expected commit hash on first clone. When set, Boilerplate records the commit on first use and rejects later fetches whose tip does not descend from it. Ignored for filesystem and archive types. See Settings and configuration files.

docs.title: ArchiveSource
docs.text:
A catalog source backed by a compressed archive containing template directories. Enables offline distribution and air-gapped environments.

Field Type Required Default Description type "archive" Yes — Source type discriminator location string Yes — Local file path or HTTPS URL to the archive name string Yes — Display name for this source priority integer No 100 Lower = higher priority trust_level enum No untrusted Binary trusted/untrusted trust ceiling. An archive source is untrusted by default; its tamper-evidence comes from checksum, not from a trust tier. See Template system and discovery. checksum string or null No null Expected SHA-256 hex digest of the archive; validated before extraction credentials CredentialRef or null No null Reserved for Phase 4 (remote / third-party sources). Credential reference for HTTPS downloads.

Supported formats: .zip, .tar.gz, .tgz. The archive MUST contain template directories as immediate children of the archive root. An optional boilerplate-archive.yml manifest at the root MAY declare archive metadata (name, version, created_at). Archives are extracted to {user_data_dir}/boilerplate/archives/{name}/ on first use; re-extracted when checksum changes or --refresh is passed. When present, the manifest's name and version are used for display in boilerplate cache output and diagnostic messages. They do not affect catalog registration or template resolution.

docs.title: BoilerplateLock
docs.text:
The boilerplate.lock file written into a project root after a successful creation or update.

Field Type Notes schema_version string "boilerplate/lock@1" — namespaced schema version identifier boilerplate_version string Version of the Boilerplate tool that wrote the file copier_version string Version of Copier used for rendering created_at ISO 8601 datetime UTC timestamp of creation updated_at ISO 8601 datetime UTC timestamp of last update root_template string Specifier of the template used to create the project copier_answers_file_hashes map[string, string] or null Per-layer SHA-256 hex digests, one entry per template layer that has an answers file. Key = template name (matches LockLayer.name); value = SHA-256 hex digest of that layer's .copier-answers.<layer>.yml. This is the sole answers-integrity mechanism lock verify consults for tamper detection on update. Optional; omitted when no answers files exist. layers list[LockLayer] One entry per template layer, in execution order; at least one layer joined through extends, the root

Hash format convention: Hash fields that are fixed to SHA-256 by definition (copier_answers_file_hashes values, proto_lock_hash) use bare hex strings. Checksum fields that may support alternative algorithms in the future (LockLayer.checksum) use the algorithm:hex prefix format (e.g., "sha256:{hex_digest}"). This allows future algorithm migration for content checksums without a schema change.

LockLayer:

Field Type Notes name string Template name version string Exact version used (PEP 440) joined_via enum How the layer joined the project: extends for the root template and every layer its extends closure reaches, as new and adopt write them and as update writes a layer the closure newly reaches; add for a layer boilerplate add introduced. The value is fixed once written: a layer add introduced keeps add when a later root target reaches it through extends, and the extends constraint still bounds its version. update reads it to tell which layers the root's target governs (06 §Step 3). source string URI or filesystem path of the template commit string or null Git commit hash of the template at render time checksum string SHA-256 hex digest of the template source directory content (excluding .git/, __pycache__/, .mypy_cache/, .pytest_cache/, .ruff_cache/, node_modules/), prefixed with algorithm identifier (e.g., "sha256:{hex}"). Files are sorted lexicographically by relative path (forward slashes on all platforms), then path and content are concatenated and hashed. This is the authoritative definition of the checksum exclusion list. The source directory is a git checkout, so comparisons must be stated in git's content sense (line endings normalized), not raw bytes — Copier's git-based checkout rewrites line endings under core.autocrlf=true (ADR-015 §Verification). See Project lifecycle for computation details. subdirectory string or null Deferred, conditional on the wheel_bundle seed cache (ADR-006): when built, would hold the value of the layer's _subdirectory: Copier directive for a layer sourced from a shared Git bundle. Published per-template repositories carry no _subdirectory: — one repository, one template — so null for every layer today. source_bundle string or null Deferred, conditional on the wheel_bundle seed cache (ADR-006): when built, would hold the bundle's relative path within the wheel (e.g., boilerplate/_template_bundles/templates.bundle), used for cache invalidation and audit. null for every layer today — first-party layers render from the published Git repositories, not a wheel-packaged bundle. trust_tier string or null Optional. The trust level of the layer's source at resolution time, recorded when the source declares one; null otherwise. With local sources the recorded value is null or "local". Never consulted; reserved for the Phase 4 trust model. bundle_uri string or null Optional; reserved. The external URI from which the layer's source bundle can be restored (populated by external/enterprise catalog infrastructure for air-gap restoration). null until that infrastructure populates it; never consulted. bundle_checksum string or null Optional; reserved. Expected checksum of the bundle referenced by bundle_uri, used to verify a restored bundle (populated by external/enterprise catalog infrastructure for air-gap restoration). null until that infrastructure populates it; never consulted.

Invariants: - A lock file MUST hold at least one layers entry. A lock with an empty layers list does not match the schema, so reading it fails with BP_LOCK_READ_FAILED. - The lock file MUST be written atomically: write to a temp file in the same directory as the target, then rename. - The lock file MUST NOT exist in a partial state. - The lock file MUST be written only after Copier has successfully committed the render. - Boilerplate MUST be the exclusive writer of boilerplate.lock. External tools MUST NOT be expected to write it. - Keys MUST be sorted deterministically (stable key order enables clean diffs).

Schema version format: Schemas for files that Boilerplate writes as runtime state — boilerplate.lock ("boilerplate/lock@1") and .boilerplate/environment.yml ("boilerplate/environment@1") — use the namespaced format namespace/schema@major. Boilerplate MUST parse any such file sharing the same namespace and major version. Schemas for files that template or profile authors write — boilerplate.yml (TemplateMeta) and boilerplate-env.yml (EnvironmentProfile) — use a bare-major form ("1", "1.1") for authoring ergonomics; in those cases the namespace is implicit in the filename. The two formats are not interchangeable; each schema's schema_version row in this document is authoritative for that schema.

docs.title: UpdatePlan
docs.text:
The plan artifact produced by the update pipeline. Summarizes what will change if the update is applied.

Field Type Notes current_root string Current root template specifier target_root string Target root template specifier layer_changes list[LayerChange] Per-layer version changes classification enum PATCH, MINOR, or MAJOR (highest wins) migrations_required list[string] Populated when any of the trigger conditions in 06 §Migration trigger conditions hold; MUST be empty otherwise. 06 owns the authoritative trigger list and the MAJOR-update confirmation gate that consumes this field.

LayerChange:

Field Type Notes name string Template name from_version string Current version to_version string Target version bump enum PATCH, MINOR, or MAJOR

docs.title: MigrationRecord
docs.text:
An entry in .boilerplate/migrations.yml recording one finished operation.

Field Type Notes id string Sequential integer starting at "1" (stored as string). The created record (when present) is always id: "1". from_version string or null Root template specifier before the operation (e.g., "streamlit@0.1.0"). null for created records (no prior state), add records (the added layer had no prior state) and adopted records (no prior Boilerplate state — the project existed under Copier but not under Boilerplate). to_version string Root template specifier after the operation (e.g., "streamlit@0.2.0"). For created and adopted records, this is the template specifier the project is now bound to; for an add record, it is the specifier of the added layer. timestamp ISO 8601 datetime UTC timestamp status enum One of success, failed, conflict, adopted, created; see MigrationRecord status state machine for the exit-code mapping and when each value is written. error string or null Error message if status is not success (or created/adopted, both of which are success-shaped terminal values) classification enum or null PATCH, MINOR, or MAJOR for update records; null for created, adopted and add records (no prior-version comparison applies). targets map[string, string] or null On a conflict record, each layer of the paused walk keyed by LockLayer.name with the version the walk was updating it to. null on every other record. finished list[string] or null On a conflict record, the names of the layers whose steps the paused walk completed, in walk order; the layer whose merge left conflict markers is among them. The run builds it from the RestoreMarker: the marker's finished followed by its paused_layer (06 §Interrupted copy back). null on every other record.

Invariants: Entries MUST be append-only, and an existing entry MUST NOT be modified. A conflict record MUST be appended when a conflict pauses an update, and a failed record when a task fails after the copy back.

docs.title: MigrationRecord status state machine
docs.text:
status carries five values, each written once when the operation ends. They map to CLI exit codes:

Status Exit code Meaning success 0 Normal completion of an update. conflict 4 (ACTION_REQUIRED) Merge conflicts requiring user resolution. The record names each layer's target version and the layers the paused walk finished, which is what update resumes from (04 §Safe Update). failed 1 A task failed after the copy back of an update or an add and the files were kept, under --non-interactive or by a terminal user's choice. A failure before the copy back leaves the checkout unchanged and appends no record. adopted 0 Written by the adoption pipeline to distinguish adopted projects from created or updated projects in the audit trail. See §06 Part 2.5. created 0 Written by boilerplate new as the first record on successful project creation. See §06 Part 1 Step 5.

Single write when the operation ends: Every operation appends its record once, with its final status, when the operation ends, and never modifies an entry afterwards. update and add append a success record after the lock file has been written. An operation that leaves the checkout unchanged, such as one that fails before the copy back or whose copy back fails and is undone, appends no record. The state of a copy back cut off midway is kept in the RestoreMarker, not in the log. adopt and create write only Boilerplate-owned state files and have no merge-conflict path.

docs.title: IntentJournal
docs.text:
An intent journal records the in-progress state of a mutating operation for crash recovery. Written before the operation begins and deleted on successful completion.

Field Type Description operation enum One of: create, update, add, adopt, env_apply. Identifies which mutating operation owns the journal so crash-recovery logic can dispatch to the operation-specific handler. The set MUST cover every command that participates in journal-based recovery. phase string Current phase. Free-form string at the schema level; valid identifiers are operation-specific. See IntentJournal phase vocabularies. started_at ISO 8601 When the operation began staging_dir string Path to the staging directory destination string Path to the target project or environment template_ref string or null Template reference (for create/update/add) profile_ref string or null Profile reference (for env_apply)

File locations: Project operations use .boilerplate-commit-intent.json in the staging directory. For update and add, the staging directory is the uniquely named temp folder that holds the worktree, and the journal sits beside the worktree so git add -A in the worktree never picks it up. Environment operations use .boilerplate-env-intent.json in the staging directory.

docs.title: IntentJournal phase vocabularies
docs.text:
phase is a free-form string at the schema level so each operation's recovery handler can interpret its own phases. Per-operation vocabularies:

Operation Phase identifiers Phase semantics create, adopt staging, committing, locking locking corresponds to writing boilerplate.lock. env_apply staging, committing, locking Same three identifiers as project operations, but locking names the Record Write stage (Stage 6) — environment.yml is a provenance record, not a lock file. See EnvironmentProvisionRecord and §08 Stage 6.

Recovery behavior: See Project lifecycle and Environment provisioning for how each operation dispatches on the phase identifiers above. update and add have no phase vocabulary of their own: the journal identifies the staging folder for stale cleanup only, and recovery of a cut-off copy back reads the RestoreMarker, whose phase is their one recovery vocabulary.

docs.title: RestoreMarker
docs.text:
A restore marker keeps the state of an update or add run that is copying its result back, so a run cut off there can be finished or set aside (06 §Interrupted copy back). Written before the copy back changes a file and removed after the run appends its record.

Field Type Description operation enum update or add kind enum complete when the walk finished every layer, paused when a conflict paused it phase enum copy_back until the copy back ends, then tasks (a complete run's tasks run), then recording (the lock and the record remain). update and add pass the same phases. start_commit string The commit HEAD pointed at when the run began result_commit string The staging worktree's last per-layer commit, start_commit when no layer finished targets map[string, string] Each layer of the walk keyed by LockLayer.name with the version the walk was updating it to, as in a conflict record finished list[string] The names of the layers whose steps the walk finished, in walk order, the paused layer excluded. Empty when kind is complete. paused_layer string The name of the layer whose merge left conflict markers, which no commit holds and which follows the finished layers in walk order. Absent when kind is complete. started_at ISO 8601 When the run began

File location: git rev-parse --git-path boilerplate-restore.json, which resolves under the git directory of the worktree the command runs in.

Ref: refs/worktree/boilerplate/restore, set with git update-ref to result_commit and removed with git update-ref -d. A refs/worktree/ ref is per worktree, keeps the commit reachable after the stale-staging cleanup removes the staging folder, and is not shared with other worktrees. The ref is set before the marker is written and removed after the marker is removed. The marker is written with the same tmp-then-rename recipe as the other single-file state (07 §Atomic Staged Write Pattern); a marker that does not parse stops the command with BP_UPDATE_INTERRUPTED.

The marker differs from the IntentJournal: the journal sits in the staging folder, which the stale cleanup removes, and the marker sits in the git directory so it outlives that folder.

docs.title: EnvironmentProfile
docs.text:
A declarative specification of the development toolchain required by a project or team. Profiles use proto's .prototools schema for tool version declarations and add Boilerplate-specific composition via extends.

Field Type Required Default Constraints name string Yes — Non-empty; identifies the profile logically version Version Yes — Semantic version of this profile schema_version string No "1" Schema major version. MUST be "1" for the current schema. Boilerplate MUST reject profiles with an unrecognized major version and SHOULD silently ignore unknown fields within a recognized version. extends list of string No [] Ordered list of parent profile references tools map[string, string] No {} Tool name → version constraint (proto-compatible) packages map[string, list[PackageRequirement]] No {} Platform-keyed package requirements allowed_proto_plugins list of string No [] Allowlist of proto tool/plugin identifiers permitted for this profile. When non-empty, proto MUST only install tools whose identifiers appear in this list. An empty list means no restriction. Plugin identifiers use proto's canonical tool names (e.g., node, go, rust, python). Violation raises BP_ENV_PLUGIN_NOT_ALLOWED.

Computed: - specifier → {name}@{version}, derived from the name and version fields

Enterprise deployments SHOULD define an explicit allowed_proto_plugins list in their base environment profile to prevent unauthorized WASM plugin execution.

tools entries follow proto's version constraint syntax and are written to .prototools during provisioning. Example: {"python": ">=3.11", "node": ">=18"}.

packages entries are keyed by platform (windows, wsl2, linux, macos) and list platform-specific package requirements.

PackageRequirement:

Field Type Required Notes name string Yes Human-readable package name source string Yes Package manager (winget, scoop, apt, brew, dnf) id string No Package manager-specific identifier (e.g., Git.Git for winget) version string No Version constraint

docs.title: Environment Lock Strategy
docs.text:
Tool-level version locking and checksum verification are delegated to proto via its native .protolock file. Boilerplate enables this by setting settings.unstable-lockfile = true in the generated .prototools. Proto's lock file records exact resolved versions, checksums, and platform (OS/arch) for each tool — this is the reproducibility mechanism for Environment Provisioning.

Boilerplate does NOT maintain a separate environment.lock file for tool versions. Doing so would duplicate what proto already provides and violate "orchestrate, don't replace." Instead, Boilerplate records only what proto does not know: which profile was applied and how the extends chain was resolved.

docs.title: EnvironmentProvisionRecord
docs.text:
Written to .boilerplate/environment.yml after successful provisioning. Records the profile resolution and provisioning provenance. Tool-level version locking and checksums are in .protolock (owned by proto). See 08-environment-provisioning.md Part 5 for the full operational specification.

Field Type Notes schema_version string "boilerplate/environment@1" — namespaced schema version (same convention as boilerplate/lock@1) boilerplate_version string Version of the Boilerplate tool that performed provisioning profile_name string The root profile's name (e.g., python-dev) profile_version string The root profile's version, PEP 440 (e.g., 1.2.0) extends_chain list[string] Ordered list of profile specifiers in topological order (base first, root last) applied_at ISO 8601 datetime UTC timestamp of when provisioning completed tools map[string, string] {tool_name: exact_version} for all installed tools proto_lock_hash string or null SHA-256 hex digest of .protolock at time of apply; null if proto did not write .protolock

Invariants:

  • Written atomically (same pattern as boilerplate.lock).
  • Written only after proto has successfully provisioned all tools and .protolock exists.
  • Keys MUST be sorted deterministically.

Ownership boundary: Boilerplate owns .boilerplate/environment.yml (profile provenance). Proto owns .protolock (tool versions and checksums). The boilerplate env status command reads both to report the full environment state.

State, not audit: .boilerplate/environment.yml is the single env-domain state file — a current-state projection holding the most recently applied state. EnvironmentProvisionRecord is overwritten in place on each successful env apply, not appended; the recovery story is "run env apply again". The env domain MUST NOT add a migrations-style append-only audit log: provisioning is idempotent and re-runnable, so it needs only the current-state record.

docs.title: Profile File
docs.text:
An environment profile is declared in a standalone YAML file named boilerplate-env.yml. This file is the profile definition; the .prototools file is the generated output written during provisioning.

File locations:

  • Profile definitions (reusable, versioned): Stored in template directories alongside templates, discovered by a dedicated profile scanner that follows the same directory traversal pattern as DirectoryTemplateRepository. A directory containing boilerplate-env.yml is a profile source, analogous to a directory containing boilerplate.yml being a template source.
  • Project-local profile: A boilerplate-env.yml in the project root applies to that project. Created by boilerplate env apply or manually by the developer.

Discovery: Profiles are discovered and registered in a ProfileCatalog (analogous to TemplateCatalog) using the same directory scan and "first one wins" registration policy. The env apply <profile-spec> command resolves a profile by name or name@version from this catalog.

Relationship to .prototools and .protolock: During env apply, Boilerplate reads the profile's tools section, merges any extends chain, and writes the resolved tool versions to .prototools in proto's native format. Boilerplate also sets settings.unstable-lockfile = true in the generated .prototools to enable proto's native .protolock file, which records exact resolved versions and checksums for reproducibility. .prototools and .protolock are generated artifacts — Boilerplate owns their lifecycle during provisioning, but proto owns their schema and reads them at runtime.

ProfileCatalog operations: The ProfileCatalog follows the same interface pattern as TemplateCatalog:

Method Input Output Notes register(profile) EnvironmentProfile void First-wins deduplication by name@version resolve(name, version?) name + optional version EnvironmentProfile or null Null version returns highest by PEP 440 list_all() — list[EnvironmentProfile] All registered profiles

docs.title: Error Hierarchy
docs.text:
All errors inherit from BoilerplateError (the base class). Each exception type maps to one or more BP_* error codes (see Operational quality). The exception hierarchy is the implementation mechanism; the error codes are the stable public contract.

Error Exit code Raised When BoilerplateError — Base; never raised directly DirectoryValidationError 2 A required directory path is missing, not a directory, or otherwise invalid TemplateNotFoundError 1 A requested template cannot be located in the catalog InvalidVersionError 3 A version string is not PEP 440 compliant InvalidTemplateSpecifierError 3 A specifier string fails name/version validation MetadataValidationError 3 boilerplate.yml is malformed or missing required fields ProfileError 1 profile.toml exists but is not valid TOML, or a reserved section is not a table (BP_CONFIG_PROFILE_INVALID) DestinationRequiredError 3 A non-interactive render names no destination, and the current directory is never assumed (BP_INPUT_DEST_REQUIRED) DestinationNotEmptyError 3 The render destination exists and is non-empty, and --force was not provided NonInteractiveRequiresForceError 3 A multi-layer render in non-interactive mode requires --force MissingRequiredAnswersError 3 Non-interactive render cannot proceed because required answers are missing (no default, and not hidden by its when) InteractiveModeRequiresTtyError 3 Interactive render requested but stdin is not a TTY, so prompts can never be answered InvalidDataError 3 --data/--data-file input cannot be parsed: a --data entry has no =, the file cannot be read, or its YAML is not a mapping InteractiveRenderFailedError 1 Copier's prompt machinery failed because the environment cannot host interactive prompts UserCancelledError 130 The user cancelled an interactive prompt (e.g. Ctrl+C); translated from Copier's CopierAnswersInterrupt before its (AnswersMap, Question, Template) payload can reach the generic exception handler DependencyError — Intermediate base for dependency resolution errors; never raised directly DependencyNotFoundError 1 (extends DependencyError) A template referenced in extends cannot be found in the catalog DependencyCycleError 1 (extends DependencyError) The dependency graph contains a cycle VersionConflictError 1 (extends DependencyError) The same template resolves to incompatible versions in the graph (BP_RESOLVE_VERSION_CONFLICT) LockReadFailedError 1 boilerplate.lock cannot be read as a lock file: unparseable YAML, a truncated write or a body that does not match the schema (BP_LOCK_READ_FAILED) LockSchemaUnsupportedError 1 The lock file's schema_version major exceeds the major the running tool supports, so the tool neither reads nor mutates it (BP_LOCK_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED) RecordedAnswerRejectedError 3 A recorded answer fails the target view's question type, choices or validator inside a layer's update step, after the layer's migrations; translated from Copier's ValueError AnswersFileIncompleteError 3 Before any layer runs, a question of a layer's scoped view at the recorded versions that is neither secret nor hidden (04 §Safe Update defines hidden) is recorded in neither the layer's own answers file nor its declaring layer's file; the error lists the layer and the keys UpdateLayerDriftError 3 Before any layer runs, a layer and one of its ancestors both disagree with boilerplate.lock, with no pending conflict record to resume UpdateTargetMismatchError 3 An explicit --target-version differs from the targets a pending conflict record names UpdateUnknownLayerError 3 update was given a target for a layer the project's lock does not list; nothing is staged (BP_UPDATE_LAYER_UNKNOWN) ActionRequiredError — Base for a recoverable pause that needs user action; never raised directly, exits 4 through its subclasses UpdateTargetExcludedError 3 An explicit --target-version <layer>@<version> names a version that the extends constraint of another lock layer excludes; nothing is staged (BP_UPDATE_TARGET_EXCLUDED) UpdateConflictPausedError 4 (extends ActionRequiredError) A layer's update left merge conflicts and the walk stopped (BP_UPDATE_CONFLICT_PAUSED) UpdateDowngradeError 3 Before any layer runs, a target is older than the version a layer's answers file records in _commit, or a recorded _commit yields no version (BP_UPDATE_DOWNGRADE_REJECTED) UpdateProjectNotReadyError 3 The project is not a git repository root with at least one commit, or its working tree has uncommitted changes, untracked files included (BP_UPDATE_PROJECT_NOT_READY) UpdatePathObstructedError 3 Before the copy back, a path the walk added already exists in the checkout as an ignored file or directory (BP_UPDATE_PATH_OBSTRUCTED) UpdateInterruptedError 3 The restore marker shows an earlier run cut off while restoring its result into the working tree, and the rerun cannot finish it: another command, a moved HEAD, a working tree that differs from the run's result, a run a conflict had paused, or a marker file that does not parse (BP_UPDATE_INTERRUPTED) UpdateCopyBackFailedError 1 Copying the staging worktree back failed partway; the copy back was undone (06 §Undo), the staging worktree is kept, the restore marker and its ref are removed and no record is appended (BP_UPDATE_COPY_BACK_FAILED) ProjectNotManagedError 3 add found no boilerplate.lock in the project (BP_UPDATE_PROJECT_NOT_MANAGED) LayerAlreadyAddedError 3 add named a template the lock already lists (BP_UPDATE_LAYER_ALREADY_ADDED) AddAncestorsMissingError 3 A template the new layer extends is not in the lock (BP_UPDATE_ANCESTORS_MISSING) AddAncestorVersionError 3 An ancestor's recorded version fails the new layer's extends reference (BP_UPDATE_ANCESTOR_VERSION_MISMATCH) UpdateTaskFailedError 1 A task failed after the update's files were copied back; the update keeps the files and writes the lock under --non-interactive UpdateSubmodulesUnsupportedError 3 update or add finds a .gitmodules file in the project, so the staging worktree cannot be created safely (BP_UPDATE_SUBMODULES_UNSUPPORTED) UpdateCheckoutChangedError 3 The user's checkout changed while an update or add worked in the staging worktree, so the worktree is discarded before the copy back (BP_UPDATE_CHECKOUT_CHANGED) ConcurrencyContentionError 1 Another Boilerplate operation still holds the project's advisory lock when the wait times out (BP_CONCURRENCY_CONTENTION) MergeConflictError 1 Two layers declare incompatible values for the same configuration key

Unrecognized exceptions outside this hierarchy MUST exit with code 1 (FAILURE). Exit-code semantics (what each code means) are specified in §Exit Codes below.

docs.title: Settings and Configuration Files
docs.text: Runtime settings (the Settings object) and the boilerplate-sources.yml catalog-source configuration file are operator-authored configuration — a different artifact class than the domain schemas defined in this document. Their full specification (fields, env vars, defaults, validation rules, read protocols) lives in Settings and configuration files. The revoked-templates.yml revocation file is reserved for Phase 4 (revocation is deferred); it is not a live operator-authored file.

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text:
Code Name Meaning 0 SUCCESS Command completed successfully 1 FAILURE General runtime failure 2 CONFIG_ERROR Configuration or settings could not be loaded 3 VALIDATION_ERROR Input validation failed 4 ACTION_REQUIRED The operation requires user intervention before it can complete (e.g., merge conflicts during update that the user resolves and commits before rerunning boilerplate update). Distinguishes recoverable workflow pauses from hard failures (exit 1). Commands: update (merge conflicts). env apply does not produce exit 4 — per §08 Part 4, all provisioning failures roll back fully to exit 1; a partial-install resume path is a candidate future enhancement, not part of the contract. 130 USER_CANCELLED The user cancelled an interactive prompt (Ctrl+C). Matches the POSIX 128 + SIGINT convention Typer's own KeyboardInterrupt handler already uses, so every Ctrl+C in the CLI — inside a prompt or not — exits with the same code.

Command-line usage errors — an unknown option, a missing argument, a rejected flag value — are input validation and exit 3, overriding Click's own default of 2, which this taxonomy reserves for CONFIG_ERROR.

Documented validation example: Passing --verbose and --quiet together is mutually exclusive and exits with code 3 (VALIDATION_ERROR).

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document specifies the structure of Boilerplate templates, the boilerplate.yml metadata schema, how Copier is configured, how templates are discovered, classified, ranked, and presented to the user, and how the catalog is built from one or more federated sources. Templates are structured so Copier can render them natively; boilerplate.yml adds only what Copier doesn't provide — composition, versioning, and dependency metadata. Catalog discovery extends "orchestrate, don't replace" to the template ecosystem — Boilerplate federates sources without owning them.

See Data models for entity definitions (TemplateMeta, TemplateInfo, TemplateCatalog, CatalogEntry, etc.).

docs.title: Template Directory Layout
docs.text:
A Boilerplate-compatible template is a directory on the filesystem with the following required structure:

{template-name}/
├── boilerplate.yml          # REQUIRED — Boilerplate metadata
├── copier.yml               # REQUIRED — Copier questionnaire and tasks
└── {template content}/      # Files rendered into the destination project

Additional files and directories are permitted. Copier renders files according to its own conventions (e.g., Jinja2 templating, exclusion rules).

docs.title: Path Safety
docs.text:
Boilerplate MUST verify, after staging, that all rendered file paths are contained within the staging root. Absolute output paths and .. components that resolve outside the staging root MUST be rejected with a clear error. Symlinks in rendered output that point outside the staging directory MUST be rejected with a clear error. Templates containing absolute output paths MUST be rejected at validate time.

Symlinks in template source directories: Template source directories MAY contain symlinks. During per-layer rendering (see Composition engine), symlinks within a template's tree MUST be resolved (copied as regular files) rather than preserved when the source is materialized for Copier. This ensures consistent output across platforms regardless of symlink support. Symlinks pointing outside the template directory MUST be rejected during boilerplate validate.

docs.title: Required files
docs.text:
File Owner Purpose boilerplate.yml Boilerplate Declares name, version, description, and parent templates copier.yml Copier Declares questions (variables), tasks, exclusions, and other Copier directives
