Both files MUST exist. A directory containing only one of the two is not a valid Boilerplate template (though a directory with only copier.yml MAY be classified as a Copier-only template for catalog purposes; see Template Classification).

docs.title: YAML Parsing Rules
docs.text:
Both boilerplate.yml and copier.yml MUST be parsed as YAML 1.2 using the Core Schema (see YAML 1.2 specification). The following constraints apply to Boilerplate-owned files (boilerplate.yml and boilerplate.lock); copier.yml parsing is delegated to Copier:

  • Character encoding: UTF-8 only
  • Anchors and aliases: Permitted, but implementations MUST limit total alias expansion to prevent entity expansion attacks (e.g., "billion laughs"). A maximum of 1,000 resolved alias nodes is RECOMMENDED. If expansion exceeds the implementation's limit, parsing MUST fail with a clear error.
  • Custom YAML tags (e.g., !!python/object): MUST NOT appear; if encountered, parsing MUST fail with a clear error
  • Duplicate keys: MUST be treated as an error; if two keys at the same mapping level are identical, parsing MUST fail
  • Schema validation: Load the full document first, then validate against the schema; do not validate field-by-field during parsing
  • Unrecognized fields: MUST be silently ignored (forward-compatibility)

docs.title: boilerplate.yml Schema
docs.text: The complete field reference for boilerplate.yml is defined in 02-data-models.md §TemplateMeta. This section covers authoring guidance and behavioral details for template authors.

docs.title: extends syntax
docs.text:
Each entry in extends is a template reference (name or name@version). See 02-data-models.md §TemplateSpecifier for syntax and resolution rules.

Version Ranges: The current extends syntax supports exact version pins (name@1.0.0) and unversioned references (name). Version range specifiers (e.g., name@>=1.0,<2.0) are reserved for a future release.

Order matters: in the extends list, later-declared entries take file precedence over earlier entries when conflicts occur. The composition execution order is determined by topological sort of the dependency graph; within the sort, declaration order in extends determines edge priority and therefore file precedence when diamond dependencies exist. See Composition engine for the full precedence rules.

docs.title: post_create_message
docs.text: When post_create_message is present and non-empty, the CLI MUST print each line to the user's terminal after a successful project creation. Lines are printed in order, separated by newlines. Lines MAY contain Jinja2 variable references. Boilerplate MUST render these through Copier's Jinja2 environment using the same variable context available during template rendering. Values from secret questions (secret: true in copier.yml) MUST be excluded from the rendering context for post_create_message to prevent accidental secret leakage in terminal output or logs.

docs.title: requires_profile
docs.text:
When requires_profile is non-null, it MUST be an object with the following fields:

Field Type Required Description name string Yes Profile identifier (e.g., "python-dev", "node") version string No PEP 440 version constraint against the profile's own version (e.g., ">=1.2", "~=2.0"). Validates against published profile versions in the catalog.

Tool-version requirements come from the profile's lineage, not from the template. Profiles declare tool version constraints in their own tools map; profile authors bump the profile version when those constraints change (the profile version is the contract). A template that needs Python ≥ 3.12 requires a profile version whose tool map satisfies that — not a per-template tool override. This keeps the profile as the single source of truth for tool versions and prevents the same profile from producing different effective constraints depending on which template invokes it. A template that needs more than one toolchain requires a profile that composes them via extends — illustratively, a python-containers profile extending python-dev — not a list of profiles.

When the required profile is not present in the project's environment state (no .boilerplate/environment.yml, or its profile_name does not match) or its profile_version does not satisfy the version constraint, the outcome depends on whether the command mutates the project:

  • Mutating commands (boilerplate new, boilerplate update, boilerplate add, boilerplate adopt) MUST fail closed with BP_RESOLVE_PROFILE_MISSING and exit code 3 (VALIDATION_ERROR). The error message MUST name the required profile, the failing constraint, and the actual environment state (or its absence).
  • Read-only / inspection commands (compose, graph, validate, --render-to, test) MUST emit a WARNING naming the same details but MUST NOT fail on this basis alone, so authors can inspect a template before its profile is provisioned.

This keeps the profile contract a hard precondition exactly where it affects on-disk state, while letting inspection remain usable on a not-yet-provisioned environment.

docs.title: Schema Evolution
docs.text:
Boilerplate MUST support all boilerplate.yml schema versions within the 1.x series. Any valid 1.x document — whether "1", "1.1", or a future "1.9" — MUST be loadable by any Boilerplate implementation that supports schema version 1. New 1.x versions MAY add optional fields but MUST NOT remove or change the semantics of existing fields. Unrecognized fields MUST be silently ignored, ensuring that a template authored against a newer 1.x schema still loads on an older Boilerplate version (forward-compatibility).

When Boilerplate encounters a schema_version with an unknown major version (e.g., "2"), it MUST reject the document with a clear error message indicating that the schema version is not supported and suggesting the user upgrade Boilerplate. This prevents silent misinterpretation of a fundamentally incompatible schema. Implementations MUST NOT attempt to partially parse or guess the semantics of an unknown major version.

docs.title: Example boilerplate.yml files
docs.text:
A base template (no parent): 

schema_version: "1"
name: project
version: "2.1.0"
description: A general-purpose Python project, with its tools configured.
post_create_message:
  - "Run 'cd {{ project_slug }}' to enter your project."
  - "Run 'uv run pytest' to run the tests."

A derived template (extends project): 

schema_version: "1"
name: streamlit
version: "1.0.0"
description: A Streamlit app, built on the general-purpose template.
extends:
  - project@2.1.0
requires_profile:
  name: python-containers   # illustrative profile name, extending python-dev
  version: ">=1.0"          # profile-version constraint (profile lineage is the tool-version contract)

A deeply layered template (extends multiple parents): 

schema_version: "1"
name: ml-api
version: "3.0.0"
description: ML inference API template.
extends:
  - fastapi@2.0.0
  - ml-base@1.5.0

docs.title: Copier Configuration
docs.text: The Copier configuration file (copier.yml) declares the information that the composition engine and Copier need to render a template. Boilerplate treats this file as Copier-owned; the composition engine merges it across layers using the strategies defined in Composition engine.

docs.title: Configuration Concepts
docs.text:
The copier.yml file contains four categories of configuration that Boilerplate's composition engine understands:

Concept Description Composition behavior Questions User-facing prompts that collect variable values (name, type, default, help text, conditional visibility, constrained choices) Derived template questions override base template questions of the same key; new questions are appended Tasks Commands executed after rendering (post-generation hooks) Accumulated from all layers; executed after final rendering Extensions Jinja2 extensions (custom filters) Union across all layers, deduplicated Directives Copier-specific configuration (minimum Copier version, exclusion patterns, subdirectory settings) Layer-local by default; specific directives have explicit merge strategies

docs.title: Copier YAML Schema
docs.text:
Copier uses the following YAML schema in copier.yml:

Questions — Any key in copier.yml not starting with _ is a user question. Questions are dictionaries with the following fields:

Sub-field Purpose type Data type: str, bool, int, float, json, yaml help Prompt text shown to the user default Default value (supports Jinja2 expressions) when Boolean expression; if false, the question is skipped choices List of allowed values (optional)

Directives — Underscore-prefixed keys configure Copier's own behavior. Each Copier directive key is assigned a merge strategy. See 04-composition-engine.md §Merge Rules for the complete key-to-strategy mapping.

docs.title: Task Execution Safety
docs.text:
Task execution is default-deny: tasks never run without explicit operator consent. Before executing any accumulated tasks, Boilerplate MUST display the full list of tasks that will run (template layer name + command) and prompt the user for confirmation unless --yes is passed. A --no-tasks flag (canonical name) MUST be supported to suppress all task execution without prompting. All executed tasks MUST be logged at INFO level including: task command string, source template layer, execution order index, exit code, and duration. Task stdout and stderr MUST be captured and logged at DEBUG level. This audit trail enables post-incident investigation of what tasks ran and what they produced.

Under the current binary trust model, the consent requirement splits into two rows:

Template trust Requirement to run tasks trusted User confirmation (or --yes) untrusted User confirmation AND --allow-tasks (or --allow-untrusted)

If an untrusted template's tasks are not authorized by --allow-tasks (or --allow-untrusted), those tasks MUST be skipped with a warning listing the skipped commands.

Security warning: Template tasks execute shell commands with the invoking user's full privileges. Boilerplate provides no sandboxing or isolation for task execution. Users SHOULD review task commands before confirming.

docs.title: Jinja2 Extension Safety
docs.text:
When any composition layer declares _jinja_extensions, Boilerplate MUST display which extensions will be loaded and from which template layer, and prompt the user for confirmation unless --allow-extensions (or --allow-untrusted) is explicitly passed on the CLI. The --allow-extensions flag is required to enable extension loading in non-interactive mode; auto-escalating to allow_extensions=true without user consent is not permitted. Extensions MUST be logged at INFO level (extension name, source template) when loaded.

The user consent prompt for Jinja2 extensions MUST be displayed BEFORE any extension module is imported. Extension modules may execute arbitrary code at import time (__init__ side effects), so consent must precede loading.

Boilerplate MUST reject extension module paths that resolve to standard library modules (os, sys, subprocess, importlib, shutil, pathlib) or any module outside the template's own directory tree and explicitly allowed extension packages.

Extension allowlist: Two lists govern whether an extension loads. They serve different purposes and are not interchangeable:

List Where declared Role Gating? allowed_extensions Template's boilerplate.yml (per-template) Declarative: names what the template intends to load; narrows the consent prompt and surfaces the requirement to the user. No — does not grant consent and does not relax the package-allowlist check. allowed_extension_packages Global Boilerplate configuration (system-wide) Package-level allowlist: the set of packages whose extensions may be loaded at all. Yes.

An extension module loads only when ALL three of the following hold:

  1. Its import path is NOT in the standard library blocklist (os, sys, subprocess, importlib, shutil, pathlib, etc.).
  2. It resolves to a file within the template's own directory tree, OR its package name appears in the system-wide allowed_extension_packages list.
  3. The user has consented to extension loading (via --allow-extensions, --allow-untrusted, or interactive confirmation).

Extensions from packages not on the allowlist MUST be rejected with BP_RENDER_UNSAFE_EXTENSION and a remediation message listing the package name and how to add it to the allowlist.

docs.title: Jinja2 Sandbox
docs.text:
Boilerplate MUST use Jinja2's SandboxedEnvironment (not the standard Environment) for all template rendering. The SandboxedEnvironment restricts attribute access on objects, preventing common Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) techniques such as traversing __class__.__mro__ or __subclasses__() to reach dangerous built-in functions.

The module import blocklist (above) and the SandboxedEnvironment are complementary controls: the blocklist prevents loading dangerous modules as Jinja2 extensions at import time; the sandbox prevents template expressions from reaching dangerous functionality at render time via Python's object model.

The system-wide extension allowlist plus explicit user consent is the enforced policy boundary for what code may run; SandboxedEnvironment is defense-in-depth that hardens execution within that boundary, not a control relied upon as the security boundary itself.

The sandbox MUST also cover post_create_message rendering, regardless of whether Copier's own environment is sandboxed. This makes the security guarantee unconditional across every Jinja2 rendering path Boilerplate touches.

docs.title: Example copier.yml
docs.text:
project_name:
  type: str
  help: "Human-readable name of the project (e.g. My Project)"
  default: "{{ _folder_name }}"

project_slug:
  default: "{{ project_name | slugify }}"
  when: false

description:
  type: str
  help: "Brief description of the project."
  default: "A new Python project."

dependencies:
  type: json
  default: []
  help: "Runtime dependencies"

dev_dependencies:
  type: json
  default:
    - pytest
    - ruff
  help: "Development dependencies"

_tasks:
  - ["python", "_scripts/post_generation.py"]

Overriding a question in a derived template: A derived template's copier.yml declares its own questions and MAY declare a parent question to override or extend it; it MUST NOT declare a parent question unchanged, because the layer's scoped view already hands every ancestor's question to every render of the layer (ADR-015); boilerplate validate warns on an unchanged redeclaration (05 §validate, check V17). When layers are merged, the derived template's value overrides the base for scalar and dict types (see merge strategy in Composition engine).

# streamlit/copier.yml — overrides the default for 'dependencies'
dependencies:
  default: ["streamlit", "pydantic>=2"]

docs.title: Copier Integration Contract
docs.text: Boilerplate orchestrates Copier; Copier renders. This section specifies the boundary contract — what each side does, what each side never does, and the invariants that hold across the boundary.

docs.title: Ownership boundaries
docs.text: Artifact / state Owner Mutability Notes .copier-answers.<layer>.yml (one per layer) Copier Mutable (Copier only) Boilerplate reads; never writes. See 04 §Render Behavior for the _answers_file: contract. boilerplate.lock Boilerplate Mutable (regenerated on update) Full dependency graph + integrity Template submodules Git Initialized by Boilerplate before render MUST exist before YAML parsing Merged copier.yml Boilerplate composition engine Derived !include directives processed before Copier sees the file Rendered project files Copier Written to staging during render Atomically moved on success MigrationRecord entries Boilerplate Append-only Written post-update, post-add or post-adopt

docs.title: Preconditions (before invoking Copier)
docs.text:
All of the following MUST hold before Boilerplate invokes Copier for a render or update operation. A precondition violation MUST fail fast with a Boilerplate-attributed error, not an opaque downstream Copier or YAML parse error:

  • All template dependencies resolved and locked (DependencyGraph built and validated).
  • Template artifacts fetched; git submodule update --init --recursive completed for every layer referenced as a submodule.
  • YAML !include paths validated for existence (parse-time check).
  • Destination path validated (empty or --force explicitly passed).
  • Answers payload prepared (initial user-supplied answers for new; existing answers + new resolution for update).

docs.title: Postconditions
docs.text:
On render success: each layer's .copier-answers.<layer>.yml written by Copier with _commit and _src_path; boilerplate.lock written by Boilerplate after Copier returns successfully; all rendered files present in destination; no conflict markers.

On render failure: no partial .copier-answers.<layer>.yml files in destination; no partial boilerplate.lock; staging directory removed; error raised with attribution Copier and phase render.

On update success: each affected layer's .copier-answers.<layer>.yml updated by Copier with new _commit (if that layer's version changed); boilerplate.lock regenerated; MigrationRecord appended (per §06); staging worktree removed.

On update failure before the copy back: staging worktree removed; the project is unchanged; no new MigrationRecord written.

docs.title: Non-responsibilities
docs.text:
Boilerplate explicitly does NOT:

  • Mutate any .copier-answers.<layer>.yml contents (Copier exclusivity, per the per-layer pattern).
  • Execute Jinja2 rendering logic or template-specific tasks (Copier owns rendering; Boilerplate orchestrates task confirmation gates per §Task Execution Safety above).
  • Process YAML !include directives (the YAML parser handles include resolution before Copier is invoked).
  • Implement three-way merge mechanics (delegated fully to Copier on update).

Copier explicitly does NOT:

  • Resolve template dependency graphs.
  • Generate or validate boilerplate.lock.
  • Initialize git submodules.

docs.title: Boundary invariants
docs.text:
These invariants MUST hold across the Boilerplate ↔ Copier boundary; violation of any is a contract bug, not a feature interaction:

  • Every submodule reachable from the root template's extends chain MUST be initialized before Copier is invoked.
  • Boilerplate MUST never write any layer's .copier-answers.<layer>.yml; only Copier does.
  • Render MUST leave no partial destination state on failure (staging-then-move, per §07 Atomic Staged Write Pattern).
  • boilerplate.lock MUST be written only after Copier returns success.
  • On update, the staging worktree MUST exist from the start of the walk until the run ends or a failure removes it, and the user's checkout MUST stay unchanged until the copy back.

Failure attribution for boundary violations follows the §07 Error Attribution table: infrastructure failures (missing submodule, invalid YAML include) attribute to Git or YAML; render conflicts attribute to Copier; lock or migration record failures attribute to Boilerplate.

docs.title: Submodule Federation and Tool Ownership
docs.text: This subsection explains how a template's extends parents are made available on disk before render, and draws the broader ownership lines across the full toolchain (Copier, Boilerplate, uv, the quality tools, and Git). It complements the per-artifact Ownership boundaries table above, which scopes specifically to the Boilerplate ↔ Copier render boundary.

docs.title: Fetching extends parents
docs.text:
When a template's extends parents live in separate repositories, a template repository MAY reference them as Git submodules (.gitmodules maps each parent to a submodule path). Boilerplate initializes those submodules recursively before parsing YAML or invoking Copier, so the full template source is present on disk (the submodule-initialization-before-render rule above). Each parent template owns its own semantic versioning and Git tags; on update, each layer's own copier update -a .copier-answers.<layer>.yml reads that layer's per-layer answers file, finds its recorded _commit, fetches from the original template repository, and uses the tag as the baseline for that layer's three-way merge (ADR-015 point 2) — there is no single shared answers file to read.

Reserved for Phase 4 (remote / third-party sources). A catalog monorepo that aggregates many independently versioned template repositories into a single federated source — the broader "submodule federation" organization convention — is deferred. Today, Boilerplate fetches a template and its extends parents directly (filesystem, a single git source, or archive; the deferred wheel_bundle seed cache would also apply here once built); the per-template submodule initialization above is the current mechanism and remains in scope.

docs.title: Tool ownership boundaries
docs.text:
The wider toolchain divides responsibilities as follows. Each tool owns a distinct slice of the workflow and explicitly does not own the others':

Component Owns Does NOT own Copier Template input validation, variable interpolation, answers file Dependency resolution, rendering orchestration Boilerplate Composition orchestration, lock file, atomic rendering, quality gates Package management, linting, type checking uv Dependency resolution, lock file, Python environment Template selection, composition logic ruff/pyright/pytest Linting, type checking, testing Quality gate orchestration Git Version control, artifact storage Rendering decisions, composition logic

Key boundaries:

  • Migrations may transform rendered outputs AFTER composition; outputs ≠ answers.

docs.title: Template Authoring Lifecycle
docs.text: This section describes the recommended workflow for creating, testing, and publishing templates.

docs.title: Authoring workflow
docs.text: The typical lifecycle is: scaffold a skeleton (boilerplate init-template), add template content and questions, validate (boilerplate validate), test locally (boilerplate new --dry-run), iterate, and publish to a Git repository or catalog source directory.

docs.title: Validation Surface
docs.text:
boilerplate validate verifies template invariants before publication. The authoritative check registry — stable check IDs, severities, and output format — lives in 05 §validate; IDs are stable once assigned and may be cited in error messages and CI output.

Validation is idempotent and read-only: it MUST NOT modify the template directory or perform any installation work.

docs.title: Template Testing
docs.text:
The boilerplate test command provides automated regression testing for templates. See CLI reference for the full CLI specification (flags, output formats, exit codes). A template test consists of a fixture: pre-seeded answers and an expected rendered output snapshot.

Fixture layout: Place fixtures in a tests/ subdirectory within the template:

{template-name}/
├── boilerplate.yml
├── copier.yml
└── tests/
    ├── defaults/               # fixture name
    │   ├── answers.yml         # pre-seeded answers
    │   └── expected/           # expected rendered output tree
    │       ├── pyproject.toml
    │       └── src/
    └── with-extras/            # another fixture
        ├── answers.yml
        └── expected/

Test execution: boilerplate test renders the template to a temp directory using each fixture's answers.yml, then diffs the output against expected/. Mismatches are reported per-file with unified diffs.

Snapshot update: Run boilerplate test --update-snapshots to regenerate all expected/ directories from current render output. Use this to create initial fixtures or update them after intentional template changes.

Template authors SHOULD maintain at least one fixture per template. Fixtures SHOULD cover the common-case answer set and any conditional branches in the template.

docs.title: Version Management
docs.text:
Template authors manage versions by editing the version field in boilerplate.yml. Boilerplate does not auto-increment versions or infer them from external sources.

To bump a version, update the version field in boilerplate.yml, validate, run snapshot tests, and tag the commit.

Git tag integration: For git catalog sources, Boilerplate discovers template versions from git tags matching v{version} or {name}@{version}. The version in boilerplate.yml SHOULD match the git tag version. If they disagree, the git tag version takes precedence for catalog discovery, and boilerplate validate MUST emit a warning.

For filesystem catalog sources, only the boilerplate.yml version is used — there is no git tag integration.

Downstream discovery: When a template author publishes a new version (by pushing a git tag or updating the filesystem directory), downstream projects discover it via:

  • boilerplate status — shows "Updates: template 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0 available"
  • boilerplate update --dry-run — shows the update plan without applying
  • boilerplate list --all-versions — shows all available versions

Version deprecation: To deprecate an old version, set lifecycle_state: deprecated and optionally successor: template-name@2.0.0 in the old version's boilerplate.yml. Users who reference the deprecated version will see a warning.

docs.title: Composition rules quick reference
docs.text: See 04-composition-engine.md §Merge Rules for the merge-strategy mapping, §Topological Sort for diamond-dependency file precedence, §Render Behavior for file-overlay semantics, and §Task Execution Order for deferred, once-only task execution.

docs.title: Shared File Authoring Guide
docs.text: See 04-composition-engine.md §Managing Shared Files Across Layers for the single-owner and post-render-task patterns for a file multiple layers need to contribute to.

docs.title: Template Classification
docs.text:
Every template in the catalog MUST be classified into one of two types:

Classification Criteria Boilerplate-enabled Contains both boilerplate.yml and copier.yml; supports composition, versioning, and lock files Copier-only Contains copier.yml but no boilerplate.yml; can be scaffolded but does not support composition or lock files

Classification MUST be deterministic and based solely on file presence. A template's classification MUST NOT change without a change to its files.

docs.title: Classification Algorithm
docs.text: At sync time, each template directory or remote entry MUST be classified based on file presence: directories with both boilerplate.yml and copier.yml are Boilerplate-enabled; directories with only copier.yml are Copier-only; all others are skipped. Classification is deterministic: same files produce the same classification across all runs.

docs.title: Copier-Only Template Behavior
docs.text:
When boilerplate new is invoked with a Copier-only template:

  1. The template is rendered using Copier directly (single invocation, no composition)
  2. No boilerplate.lock is written (no composition metadata to record)
  3. No extends resolution occurs (Copier-only templates cannot participate in composition)
  4. Post-creation guidance is limited to default guidance (cd {destination})
  5. The list command MUST show Copier-only templates with a Copier type indicator, clearly distinguishing them from Boilerplate-enabled templates

This allows Boilerplate to serve as a unified entry point for both composed and simple templates without requiring every template to adopt the full Boilerplate metadata format.

docs.title: Trust and Verification Levels
docs.text:
Trust is binary: a template is either trusted or untrusted. Trust reflects confidence in a template's origin — whether it came from a source the operator configured as authoritative.

Level Description Who grants trusted Came from a trusted source — a first-party git source (the published per-template repositories, ADR-006), or a git source with trust_level: trusted explicitly configured Source configuration untrusted Default for any source not configured as trusted, including local filesystem and archive templates Implicit

The binary model is the current enforcement surface. The richer multi-tier taxonomy (Official / Verified / Community / Local) is reserved for Phase 4 (remote / third-party sources). The lock's trust_tier field is an OPTIONAL free-form string field so Phase 4 can reintroduce richer tiers without a schema change; its absence MUST NOT fail resolution (see the lock provenance and integrity rule in Security model). Source URL and commit-or-checksum remain mandatory regardless of trust.

Invariants:

  • A template's trust is inherited from its source: a template is trusted only when its source is trusted (a first-party published-repo git source, or any git source configured as trusted).
  • Local filesystem and archive templates are untrusted by default.

docs.title: Trust ceiling per source type
docs.text:
Under binary trust, first-party git sources — the published per-template repositories (ADR-006) — are trusted by default; any other git source MAY be configured as trusted; filesystem and archive sources are untrusted. The deferred wheel_bundle source type would be trusted when built.

Source type Maximum trust git (first-party, published per-template repository) trusted git (third-party, with trust_level: trusted configured) trusted git (third-party, default) untrusted filesystem untrusted archive untrusted wheel_bundle (deferred seed cache) trusted (when built)

These ceilings are enforced during catalog registration. A source configured with trust_level: trusted on a filesystem or archive type is rejected at validation time. The CLI only reads trust values; it cannot modify them.

docs.title: Emergency Revocation
docs.text: Reserved for Phase 4 (remote / third-party sources). An out-of-band revocation mechanism — a system-wide revoked-templates list (revoked_templates_path), its read protocol, the BP_RESOLVE_TEMPLATE_REVOKED rejection, and the matching status / update / lock verify / new --force behaviors — is deferred until Boilerplate consumes remote third-party sources. For first-party and operator-configured sources, incident response is handled by removing or replacing the offending source and re-resolving; there is no separate revocation list. The concept is retained here so Phase 4 can reintroduce it without redesigning the trust model.

docs.title: Content Verification
docs.text:
The trust model verifies template origin (which source provided it) but not template content (tamper detection between publication and use). The expected_commit field on CatalogSource plus per-layer commit and checksum fields in boilerplate.lock provide a post-creation integrity chain; pre-use signature verification is not yet supported.

boilerplate lock verify SHOULD be included as a CI gate step to detect template content drift between catalog refreshes. See §07 Operational Quality for the CI/CD Quick Reference.

docs.title: Filesystem Source Defaults
docs.text:
When templates are discovered from filesystem sources (the DirectoryTemplateRepository), CatalogEntry fields that are only available from remote registries receive the following defaults:

Field Default Rationale trust_level untrusted Filesystem templates have no external trust attestation lifecycle_state published (when absent from boilerplate.yml) See note below tags [] No tagging metadata available from filesystem category "" No category metadata available from filesystem last_updated Filesystem mtime of boilerplate.yml Best available proxy for modification time successor null No deprecation metadata available from filesystem

The DirectoryTemplateRepository MUST respect the lifecycle_state declared in boilerplate.yml. The default value of published is applied only when the field is absent from the file, not when it is present with any value. Templates with lifecycle_state: draft are excluded from boilerplate list output by default but remain renderable via direct path reference (boilerplate new ./path/to/template).

These defaults ensure that filesystem templates appear in list output and participate in ranking without requiring registry metadata. The list command SHOULD suppress empty columns (e.g., Tags) when all results have default values.

docs.title: .copier-answers.<layer>.yml Integrity
docs.text:
Boilerplate MUST record the SHA-256 hex digest of each layer's .copier-answers.<layer>.yml file contents in the copier_answers_file_hashes mapping of boilerplate.lock (key = template name, value = digest). This per-layer mapping captures the literal answers-file contents and is the sole answers-integrity mechanism that lock verify uses. Each first-party template's copier.yml declares its own answers file via Copier's _answers_file: directive (see 04-composition-engine.md §Render Behavior). Boilerplate MUST NOT write or mutate any .copier-answers.<layer>.yml; those files are read-only from Boilerplate's perspective and are written exclusively by Copier. On update, if any layer's hash does not match, Boilerplate MUST warn the user that answer state for that layer may have been externally modified.

For reusing an answers file as an answer preset, see 05 §Answer Presets.

docs.title: Lifecycle States
docs.text:
State Description Visible by default draft Not yet published; under development No published Stable and recommended for use Yes deprecated Still works but superseded; users are warned Yes (with warning indicator) archived No longer maintained; not suitable for new use No (requires --include-archived)

Deprecation successor: When a template enters the deprecated state, it SHOULD declare a successor field in its catalog metadata — a template reference (e.g., "new-template@2.0.0" or "new-template") pointing to the recommended replacement. When the CLI displays a deprecated template (in list or during new), it MUST include the successor reference in the warning if one is declared:

!  template 'old-api' is deprecated. Use 'new-api@2.0.0' instead.

Deprecation triggers. A template version SHOULD enter the deprecated state when ANY of:

  • A security vulnerability cannot be fixed via PATCH release.
  • A breaking semantic change is required for future capabilities.
  • The version has been superseded by a major release with improved architecture or contracts.
  • Integrity or provenance concerns surface that warrant warning users away from the version.

Removal policy (deprecated → archived):

  • A version SHOULD remain deprecated long enough for downstream projects to migrate before it is marked archived; the template author chooses the interval. Critical security issues MAY transition deprecated → archived immediately, and the catalog entry MUST document the rationale at the same time.

Lifecycle state is advisory: deprecated templates warn but remain usable, and archived templates are hidden by default. (Hard out-of-band blocking via revocation is reserved for Phase 4; see §Emergency Revocation.)

docs.title: Template Discovery and Catalog Sources
docs.text: The catalog is federated: it is built from one or more catalog sources. Each source has a type, location, and priority.

docs.title: Supported Source Types
docs.text:
Type Description filesystem Local directory git Git repository, local or remote (see Git Source) archive Compressed archive (.zip, .tar.gz); enables offline and air-gapped distribution (see Archive Source) wheel_bundle Git bundle (.bundle) packaged inside a Python wheel; first-party-only; carries Git history (see Wheel Bundle Source)

The source type enum is extensible. Additional types (e.g., http, github, oci) are specified when built. Implementations encountering an unknown source type SHOULD log a warning and skip the source gracefully.

docs.title: CatalogSource
docs.text:
See Data models for the full CatalogSource schema. Key fields: name, type, location, priority, trust_level, expected_commit (optional — when set, the initial Git clone is validated against this commit hash; see TOFU warning). Authentication is delegated to Git's credential helper system (see §Authentication); a per-source credentials field is reserved for Phase 4 (remote / third-party sources).

Priority determines conflict resolution: lower number = higher priority. If two sources share the same priority value, the one registered first (earlier in the configuration list) takes precedence.

docs.title: CatalogEntry
docs.text: See Data models for the full CatalogEntry schema. A CatalogEntry is the catalog's record for one template from one source, including classification, trust level, lifecycle state, and dependency information.

docs.title: Discovery Algorithm (DirectoryTemplateRepository)
docs.text:
The DirectoryTemplateRepository scans each configured directory for immediate subdirectories containing both boilerplate.yml and copier.yml. Each valid candidate is parsed into a TemplateInfo record. Candidates are processed in lexicographic order by absolute path for determinism. Invalid candidates (unparseable metadata, invalid specifiers) are skipped with a warning.

Per template name, the highest PEP 440 version wins. If two directories provide identical name@version, the first encountered (lexicographically earlier path) wins. The TemplateCatalog enforces first-wins deduplication across multiple repositories.

Important limitation: The DirectoryTemplateRepository keeps only one version per name when scanning unversioned subdirectories. Teams managing multiple template versions on the filesystem SHOULD use versioned subdirectories (see below).

docs.title: Versioned Subdirectory Convention
docs.text:
A directory source MAY provide multiple versions of the same template using the versioned subdirectory naming convention: a subdirectory named {name}@{version} (e.g., base@1.0.0/) is treated as a specific version of template {name}. The name portion must be alphanumeric with hyphens and underscores; the version must be valid PEP 440. When versioned subdirectories are present, all discovered versions are registered in the catalog (not just the highest).

This allows pinned extends references (e.g., extends: [base@1.0.0]) to resolve correctly within a filesystem source. The catalog's first-wins deduplication still applies for identical name@version pairs across multiple sources.

Resolution determinism: A Resolver instance caches resolved templates by specifier string. A specifier that has been resolved once always returns the same TemplateInfo for the lifetime of that Resolver instance. All transitive references to the same name@version resolve to the same object within a single resolution run.

docs.title: Template Directory Resolution Order
docs.text:
When building the catalog, directories are searched in this order:

  1. --templates-dir (CLI override, if provided — highest priority)
  2. default_templates_dir (the user's default template directory)
  3. Each path in extra_template_dirs in declaration order
  4. First-party templates (the published per-template git repositories, per ADR-006; implicit source, lowest priority — org-local clones or mirrors of those repositories, or the deferred wheel-bundled seed cache (see Wheel Bundle Source), serve as the offline path)

The first template registered for a given canonical tag wins. User-provided templates via --templates-dir or extra_template_dirs can shadow built-in templates of the same name and version.

docs.title: Catalog Build Process
docs.text: The catalog is built by iterating directories in resolution order (see above), loading templates from each via DirectoryTemplateRepository, and registering them in the catalog. First-wins deduplication ensures that higher-priority sources shadow lower-priority ones for the same name@version.

docs.title: Environment Profile Discovery
docs.text:
Environment profile discovery follows the same directory scan pattern as template discovery (see Discovery Algorithm above). Where template discovery looks for boilerplate.yml, profile discovery looks for boilerplate-env.yml:

  • A directory containing boilerplate-env.yml is a profile source. The DirectoryProfileRepository scans configured directories for immediate subdirectories containing boilerplate-env.yml, parses each into an EnvironmentProfile record (see Data models for the ProfileCatalog schema), and registers them in the ProfileCatalog.
  • Registration policy: The same first-wins deduplication policy applies. Per profile name, the first registered entry wins across repositories. Within a single directory source, the highest-versioned record is kept (identical to template behavior).
  • Versioned subdirectories: The {name}@{version}/ naming convention is supported for profiles, enabling multiple profile versions to coexist in a single directory source.
  • Search order: Profile directories are searched in the same order as template directories: --templates-dir (CLI override) → default_templates_dir → extra_template_dirs → bundled profiles.
  • Validation: Each discovered boilerplate-env.yml MUST be parsed and validated. Invalid files are skipped with a warning log.

See Data models for ProfileCatalog operations and Environment provisioning for profile resolution and activation.

docs.title: Git Source
docs.text: Templates MAY be sourced from any Git repository — remote or local. Git treats local paths and remote URLs identically (git clone works with both), so a single git source type covers all Git-based template distribution.

docs.title: Fetch Behavior
docs.text:
Boilerplate clones the repository at a specific version tag using a shallow clone (depth 1). If no tag is specified, the default branch is cloned and the latest version tag is used. After clone, the local directory is treated as a standard filesystem source for discovery.

For local paths, boilerplate doctor MUST verify the path is a valid git repository and warn if it is not.

Trust-on-first-use (TOFU) warning: The first clone of a remote template source trusts whatever the Git server returns. No out-of-band verification of repository content occurs on initial fetch. After the first successful fetch, the lock file captures the commit hash and content checksum, providing integrity verification for subsequent operations. To mitigate TOFU risk:

  • Prefer HTTPS URLs over SSH for auditability
  • Use expected_commit in CatalogSource configuration to pin the initial fetch to a known-good commit
  • Review template content after first fetch before running --allow-untrusted operations

docs.title: Supported URL Formats
docs.text:
Format Example HTTPS https://github.com/user/repo.git SSH git@github.com:user/repo.git Local path /home/user/my-template-repo Shorthand (gh:) gh:user/repo (expanded to GitHub HTTPS) Shorthand (gl:) gl:user/repo (expanded to GitLab HTTPS) Shorthand (ado:) ado:org/project/repo (expanded to Azure DevOps HTTPS)

Implementations MUST support HTTPS, SSH, and local paths. Shorthands are expanded to HTTPS before cloning. Additional shorthands MAY be added in future versions.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Boilerplate delegates all credential handling to Git's credential helper system. See 10-security.md §Credential Handling for credential safety requirements.

If authentication fails, the CLI MUST report the failure with remediation guidance and the error code BP_GIT_AUTH_FAILED.

docs.title: Version Tag Convention
docs.text:
Version tags MUST follow one of these patterns:

  • v<version> — e.g., v1.2.0 (single-template repositories)
  • <template-name>@<version> — e.g., project@2.1.0 (multi-template repositories)

Version discovery enumerates tags matching these patterns, parses them as PEP 440 versions, and selects the best match for the requested constraint.

docs.title: Archive Source
docs.text: Templates MAY be distributed as compressed archives. The archive source type extracts a .zip, .tar.gz, or .tgz archive and treats the extracted contents as a filesystem source.

docs.title: Use cases
docs.text:
• Air-gapped environments where neither network access nor local git repos are available
  • Simple distribution: share a set of templates as a single file without requiring a git server
  • Checksum-verified snapshots: a checksum-protected archive provides tamper-evident template distribution

docs.title: Archive structure
docs.text:
The archive MUST contain template directories as immediate children of the archive root:

my-catalog.zip
├── project/
│   ├── boilerplate.yml
│   └── copier.yml
├── streamlit/
│   ├── boilerplate.yml
│   └── copier.yml
└── boilerplate-archive.yml   # optional manifest

An optional boilerplate-archive.yml manifest at the root MAY declare:

  • name: archive display name
  • version: archive version
  • created_at: ISO 8601 creation timestamp
  • template_checksums: map of template name → SHA-256 checksum of template directory contents

docs.title: Extraction and caching
docs.text: Archives are extracted to {user_data_dir}/boilerplate/archives/{source-name}/ on first use. Re-extraction occurs when the archive checksum changes or --refresh is passed. HTTPS archive downloads use the same Git credential helper mechanism as remote git sources.

docs.title: Checksum verification
docs.text: If checksum is configured in the archive source, it MUST be validated against the archive file before extraction. Mismatch raises BP_BUNDLE_CHECKSUM_FAILED.

docs.title: Example configuration
docs.text:
sources:
  - name: airgapped-catalog
    type: archive
    location: /mnt/shared/boilerplate-catalog-2026-03-20.zip
    checksum: sha256:abc123...

Currently an archive source is untrusted (only git sources may be configured as trusted; see Trust ceiling per source type). Its tamper-evidence comes from the checksum, not from a trust tier.

docs.title: Wheel Bundle Source
docs.text:
Deferred. Per ADR-006, the canonical first-party channel is the published per-template git repositories — ordinary git sources with vX.Y.Z tags, extracted from the authoring monorepo at release time. The wheel_bundle source type below is retained in the taxonomy as a deferred offline seed-cache option, built only on demonstrated demand.

A Git bundle file (.bundle) packaged inside the Boilerplate Python wheel as binary asset data — one bundle per first-party template, carrying that template's full extracted Git history and tags. Distinct from the archive source type (which extracts compressed archives without Git history). If built: the build pipeline produces per-template bundles from the extracted repos, the wheel ships them as package data, and first use clones each to a per-user cache directory ({user_data_dir}/boilerplate/cache/templates/<bundle-version>/) that Copier sees as a normal local Git repository (no _subdirectory: — each bundle is a single template at its root). The cache is invalidated when the installed Boilerplate version changes, since the bundles ship with the wheel. The cache is a seed, not a source of record: Copier records the source it actually used, and per ADR-015 Boilerplate MUST NOT rewrite an answers file to mask that — so a cache-seeded layer's answers file records the cache path itself, which is machine-local and does not resolve on another machine. Rehoming to the published repository is a deliberate one-line _src_path edit the user makes; the seed cache trades portability for offline capability, and that is the honest trade. LockLayer.source_bundle records the bundle's wheel-relative path for cache invalidation and audit.

Trust: trusted — first-party templates shipped inside the Boilerplate wheel. (The richer multi-tier taxonomy is reserved for Phase 4; see Trust and Verification Levels.)

Distinct from:

  • archive — .zip/.tar.gz/.tgz extraction; no Git history; not Copier-update-friendly for multi-layer projects.
  • git — remote Git URL; requires network on first use; the canonical first-party channel.
  • filesystem — local directory; may or may not have .git/.

docs.title: Local Catalog Cache
docs.text:
Remote sources are cached locally so that discovery operations do not require network access on every invocation.

Invariants:

  • Discovery MUST default to cached data. Remote sync MUST require explicit --refresh.
  • Stale caches (older than 24 hours) SHOULD warn the user but MUST NOT block operations.
  • Sync operations MUST be idempotent and safe to retry.
  • Cache storage format is implementation-defined (YAML, JSON, or SQLite are all acceptable).
  • Cached template artifacts MUST match their recorded checksum. A cached artifact whose recomputed checksum does not match its lock-file checksum MUST be treated as missing (re-fetched on next access); stale or corrupt cache entries MUST NOT be reused silently.

The cache directory ({user_data_dir}/boilerplate/) is a security-sensitive location. On POSIX systems, implementations MUST set directory permissions to 0700 (owner-only access). On Windows, implementations SHOULD restrict access to the current user via ACLs. Cache poisoning by other users or processes could lead to execution of malicious template content.

For local sources (filesystem and local git paths), discovery re-scans the source directory on each invocation; the scan is cheap at the catalog sizes targeted, so no separate mtime-based index is maintained.

docs.title: First-Party Templates
docs.text: Boilerplate ships with first-party templates. These serve as the authoritative reference for what valid templates look like.

docs.title: First-Run Experience
docs.text: On a fresh installation, boilerplate list MUST display first-party templates with a clear header (e.g., "First-party templates"). When no remote sources are configured, the output MUST include guidance: "Configure additional template sources in boilerplate-sources.yml or use --templates-dir to add template directories." When boilerplate new is invoked without a template argument and no template can be resolved, the CLI MUST list the available first-party templates and the same guidance rather than presenting an empty list with a diagnostic dead-end.

docs.title: project template
docs.text: A general-purpose Python project, with its tools configured. The template collects standard project metadata (name, description, author, dependencies) and runs a post-generation script. See the template's copier.yml for the full question set.

docs.title: streamlit template
docs.text: A Streamlit app, built on the general-purpose template: it extends project and overrides dependency defaults to include Streamlit-specific packages. All other questions are inherited from project via composition and reach the layer through its scoped view at every render, compose and update alike (ADR-015). See the template's copier.yml for details.

docs.title: boilerplate list
docs.text:
The list command is the primary interface for template discovery. Its full specification — arguments, options, output formats, ranking, and behavior — is in CLI reference.

This section documents the result-ordering and template classification logic that the list command depends on.

docs.title: Result Ordering
docs.text:
List and search results MUST use a plain deterministic ordering: source priority (lower priority number first), then name, then version (descending). The same catalog state always produces the same order; there is no weighted relevance score. Trust state MUST NOT participate in result ordering; it is a displayed and filterable property only.

Query filtering: When a query string is provided, it acts as a case-insensitive substring filter — a template is included when the query is a substring of its name, description, or any tags entry. Filtering decides inclusion only; it does not reorder results. The deterministic ordering above still applies to the filtered set.

Duplicate resolution: When two sources provide the same template name and version, the entry from the higher-priority source (lower priority number) is shown. The duplicate is suppressed.

docs.title: Selection and Handoff to Project Creation
docs.text: When the user selects a template (via boilerplate new), the discovery system resolves the template reference to a TemplateSpecifier (see Data models) and passes it to the project creation workflow (see Project lifecycle). If the user specified a version constraint rather than an exact version, the catalog resolves it to the highest matching version before constructing the specifier.

docs.title: Template Authoring Constraints
docs.text:
An implementation MUST enforce the following when loading templates:

  1. boilerplate.yml MUST be present. If absent, the directory is not a valid Boilerplate template.
  2. copier.yml MUST be present. If absent, the directory is not a valid Boilerplate template.
  3. name in boilerplate.yml MUST contain only alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores.
  4. version MUST be a valid PEP 440 version.
  5. extends is a list. The list MAY be empty ([]). If non-empty, each entry MUST be a non-empty string. Existence of referenced templates is validated at resolution time, not at load time.
  6. Circular dependencies (A → B → A) MUST be detected during resolution and reported as DependencyCycleError. They are not validated at load time.
  7. First-party (official) templates MUST include a .gitattributes declaring * text=auto eol=lf; third-party templates SHOULD. One file does two jobs: inside the template repository it keeps the template's own sources LF on every checkout, so files copied verbatim render identically on every platform; rendered into the project it keeps the project's shell scripts LF, because a script that checks out CRLF fails in bash on the carriage return in its shebang. * text=auto alone achieves neither — it normalizes what git stores and leaves the working tree platform-native, so a Windows checkout still yields CRLF. Checksum comparison normalizes line endings on its own (ADR-015) and is not a substitute for the file.
  8. The validate command SHOULD report file path collisions when validating a template with extends dependencies: files that exist in multiple layers, noting which layer's version will take precedence. This is a warning, not an error — file overlay is by design, but unintentional collisions are a common authoring mistake.

docs.title: Constraints and Invariants
docs.text:
1. Classification MUST be based solely on file presence, not content.
  2. Archived templates MUST be excluded from default results.
  3. Duplicate templates (same name+version from multiple sources) MUST resolve to the highest-priority source.
  4. Source priority MUST be configured explicitly; no implicit ordering.
  5. Search results MUST be stable for the same query, filters, and catalog state.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The composition engine takes a template reference, resolves its dependency graph, merges configuration from all layers, and produces a CompositionArtifact ready for rendering. The engine orchestrates Copier without replacing it — it resolves dependencies and merges configuration, then delegates actual file rendering to Copier.

The engine is composed of four sequentially-invoked stages:

Stage 1: Resolver
Stage 2: Dependency Graph & Topological Sort
Stage 3: Composer (uses CopierConfigMerger)
Stage 4: RenderEngine

The four-stage decomposition and the worker interfaces below are a reference implementation structure; a conforming implementation MAY organize this differently. The normative requirements are the MUST/MUST NOT statements.

docs.title: Responsibility
docs.text:
The Resolver takes a template reference and a populated catalog, performs a depth-first traversal of the extends chain, and returns a Resolution containing: - deps: a DependencyMap (specifier → list of direct dependency specifiers) - templates: a map from specifier string → TemplateInfo

The Resolver does not detect or report cycles — that is the graph layer's responsibility. The visited set in the resolution algorithm prevents redundant traversal of diamond dependencies (e.g., A → B, A → C, B → C visits C only once) but preserves all dependency edges so the graph layer can detect cycles. The Resolver MUST NOT mutate any catalog state. It MUST be pure with respect to its inputs.

docs.title: Template Reference Syntax
docs.text: A template reference is either "name" (resolves to latest) or "name@version" (exact). See 02-data-models.md §TemplateSpecifier.

docs.title: Resolution Behavior
docs.text:
The Resolver performs a depth-first traversal of the extends chain starting from the root template. For each template encountered, it records the template's information and its direct dependencies (as declared in meta.extends), then recurses into each dependency. A visited set prevents redundant traversal of shared dependencies (diamond patterns), but dependency edges are always recorded — even when the target has already been visited — so that the full edge set is available for cycle detection in the graph layer. After traversal completes, the Resolver checks for version conflicts: if the same template name appears at different versions anywhere in the graph, it raises BP_RESOLVE_VERSION_CONFLICT.

Key invariants:

  • Each specifier is visited at most once, but all dependency edges are preserved.
  • Direct dependencies preserve the declaration order from meta.extends.
  • All referenced templates MUST exist in the catalog; if any are missing, raise DependencyNotFoundError.
  • Template references are resolved via the catalog: unversioned references (name) resolve to the latest version; versioned references (name@version) resolve to the exact version.

docs.title: Version conflict resolution
docs.text:
When the same template name is encountered at different versions during dependency traversal (diamond dependency with version disagreement), the Resolver MUST reject the composition with BP_RESOLVE_VERSION_CONFLICT:

BP_RESOLVE_VERSION_CONFLICT
What: Template 'base' required at version 1.0.0 (by 'layer-a') and 2.0.0 (by 'layer-b')
Why: Diamond dependency with incompatible version constraints
Remediation: Align all references to 'base' to a single version, or use version ranges that resolve to a common version
Attribution: Template Author

The Resolver MUST NOT silently pick one version over another; version conflicts are always an error, because silent resolution could yield different results for different traversal orders.

Future: Version range specifiers (e.g., name@>=1.0,<2.0) are reserved for a future release. The current extends syntax accepts exact version pins and unversioned references only.

docs.title: Graph size limits
docs.text:
To prevent pathological compositions and protect against accidental infinite recursion:

  • Maximum dependency chain depth: 20 templates. Exceeded → BP_GRAPH_DEPTH_EXCEEDED.
  • Maximum total nodes in the resolved graph: 50 templates. Exceeded → BP_GRAPH_SIZE_EXCEEDED.

The defaults MUST be enforced.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Error Condition DependencyNotFoundError A template reference cannot be resolved in the catalog InvalidTemplateSpecifierError A versioned reference fails specifier parsing

docs.title: Stage 2 — Dependency Graph and Topological Sort
docs.text: Between the Resolver output and the Composer, the dependency map is normalized and sorted.

docs.title: Normalization
docs.text: Normalization prepares the raw dependency map for topological sorting. It deduplicates each node's dependency list while preserving declaration order from extends, ensures every referenced node appears as a key (with an empty list if it has no dependencies of its own), and detects self-cycles immediately (raising DependencyCycleError).

docs.title: Topological Sort
docs.text:
After normalization, the dependency map is sorted into a dependency-first ordered list. Any topological sort that produces a deterministic, dependency-first sequence satisfies the contract — the invariant is the ordering guarantee, not the specific algorithm. If a cycle is detected, DependencyCycleError is raised.

Invariant: Given A extends [B, C], B and C MUST appear before A in the sequence.

Tie-breaking rule: When multiple nodes have zero in-degree simultaneously (independent subgraphs or branches), the sort MUST break ties by lexicographic ordering of the normalized template specifier string (name@version). This ensures deterministic output regardless of hash-map iteration order or platform differences. Lexicographic tie-breaking applies only across independent roots (nodes no other node depends on); within a root's reachable subgraph, extends declaration order governs (per the diamond dependencies rule below), and a dependency shared across roots is emitted at its first occurrence.

Example (linear chain):

Input:  { "A": ["B"], "B": ["C"], "C": [] }
Output: ["C", "B", "A"]

Diamond dependencies: When a diamond dependency is detected, Boilerplate resolves file precedence by declaration order in the extends list. Dependencies declared later in extends are rendered later and their files take precedence. For example, given extends: [base-lib, utility-lib], utility-lib is rendered after base-lib and its files win on conflict. This rule applies recursively: if both base-lib and utility-lib themselves extend a shared dependency, the shared dependency is rendered once, and the extending template that appears later in the original extends declaration takes precedence. Determinism is guaranteed by the normalization step, which preserves declaration order from extends.

// Diamond: C extends [A, B], A extends [Base], B extends [Base]
Input:  { "C": ["A", "B"], "A": ["Base"], "B": ["Base"], "Base": [] }
Output: ["Base", "A", "B", "C"]  // B declared after A in extends; B's files override A's at same paths

File precedence follows the topological render order: templates rendered later overwrite files from templates rendered earlier at the same path. For direct children listed in extends, this means later-declared entries take precedence. For deeper dependency graphs, the topological sort determines the authoritative order — use boilerplate graph to verify the actual render sequence.

CLI visibility: When boilerplate graph detects a diamond dependency pattern (a node reachable via two or more paths), the output MUST annotate affected nodes with a [diamond] indicator and note which parent's files take precedence. Example:

#   Layer          Version   Path                      Notes
1   base           1.0.0     /path/to/base
2   parent-a       1.0.0     /path/to/parent-a
3   parent-b       1.0.0     /path/to/parent-b         [diamond: files override parent-a]
4   my-template    1.0.0     /path/to/my-template

Errors:

Error Condition DependencyCycleError A cycle exists in the dependency graph (e.g., A → B → A)

docs.title: Responsibility
docs.text: The Composer takes a Resolution and produces an immutable CompositionArtifact. It: 1. Extracts and merges Copier configuration from all template layers 2. Builds the CompositionGraph 3. Produces a CompositionLayer for each template in topological order 4. Optionally computes per-layer states and deltas (for debugging and introspection)

docs.title: Composition Behavior
docs.text:
The Composer processes templates in topological order. For each template in the sequence, it reads the template's copier.yml configuration and builds a CompositionLayer containing the template's name, version, path, and user-facing question values (non-underscore keys). All layer configurations are then merged using the CopierConfigMerger to produce the final merged schema.

When introspection is requested (include_states or include_deltas), the Composer additionally tracks the cumulative configuration state after each layer and/or the delta each layer contributes. These are attached to the corresponding CompositionLayer for use by inspection commands.

The Composer also builds a CompositionGraph from the resolution data, recording each template as a graph node (with name, version, and path) and preserving the dependency edges in declaration order.

The final output is a CompositionArtifact containing the graph (with its topological sequence), the per-layer details, and the fully merged configuration schema.

docs.title: Responsibility
docs.text: The CopierConfigMerger merges a list of copier.yml configuration dictionaries (one per layer, in topological order) into a single unified configuration.

docs.title: Merge Rules
docs.text:
The strategy applied to each key is determined by the following lookup, in priority order:

Key pattern Strategy Notes _min_copier_version intersect_versions Highest declared minimum version wins _tasks accumulate All tasks from all layers concatenated _secret_questions accumulate All secret question names concatenated _jinja_extensions union Extensions deduplicated, first-seen order, joined within each scoped view Any key not starting with _ merge_questions All user question keys Any other _-prefixed key layer-local (excluded from merge) Last layer's value is used; not propagated. Examples: _exclude, _templates_suffix, _subdirectory

Fallback rule: any _-prefixed key not explicitly listed above is treated as layer-local and excluded from the merged output. This is a closed-world assumption: only the keys listed above participate in merging.

docs.title: Merge Strategies
docs.text: The four merge strategies used by the configuration merger are defined below. Each strategy corresponds to one or more key patterns in the key-to-strategy mapping table above.

docs.title: accumulate
docs.text:
Concatenates lists in order; wraps scalars in a single-element list.

accumulate([["task_a"], ["task_b", "task_c"]]) → ["task_a", "task_b", "task_c"]

Used for: _tasks, _secret_questions.

docs.title: union
docs.text:
Concatenates lists preserving first-seen order, removing duplicates.

union([["ext_a", "ext_b"], ["ext_b", "ext_c"]]) → ["ext_a", "ext_b", "ext_c"]

Used for: _jinja_extensions.

docs.title: intersect_versions (highest wins)
docs.text:
Given a list of PEP 440 version strings, returns the maximum.

intersect_versions(["1.0", "2.0", "1.5"]) → "2.0"

Used for: _min_copier_version.

docs.title: merge_questions
docs.text:
Merges user question values: - Dict + Dict → shallow merge (later layer's keys override earlier; only the top level is merged, nested dicts are replaced wholesale) - List + List → deduplicated concatenation (items from earlier layers first, then later layers; items compared by value equality; insertion order of first appearance is preserved) - Scalar + Scalar (same type) → override (later value wins) - Type mismatch → raise MergeConflictError

Detection timing: Type mismatches MUST be detected during the compose stage (when configurations are merged), not during the render stage (when the end user runs the template). This ensures template authors catch conflicts during boilerplate compose or boilerplate validate, not end users during boilerplate new. Implementations MUST invoke the merger during validation when extends dependencies are resolvable.

merge_questions([{"type": "str", "default": "a"}, {"default": "b"}])
→ {"type": "str", "default": "b"}

Nested structure behavior:

// Base layer:  {db: {host: "localhost", port: 5432}}
// Derived layer: {db: {host: "prod.example.com"}}
// Result:      {db: {host: "prod.example.com"}}
// Note: 'port' is GONE — the entire nested dict was replaced, not merged.

Template authors who need to preserve base keys in nested structures should use flat question keys (db_host, db_port) instead of nested defaults.

Used for: all user questions (non-_ keys).

Template authoring note: Because merge_questions uses shallow merge (nested dicts are replaced wholesale by the later layer), a derived template that needs to add one key to a base template's nested default must redeclare the entire nested structure. To minimize maintenance burden when base templates evolve:

  • Prefer flat question keys over deeply nested defaults (e.g., db_host, db_port instead of db: {host: ..., port: ...})
  • When nesting is necessary, keep nested structures small and document them as extension points in the base template
  • Use Jinja2 defaults in template files rather than question defaults for values that derived templates commonly override

docs.title: Key ordering
docs.text: The merged output preserves the order keys were first encountered across all configurations (left-to-right across layers).

docs.title: Scoped view
docs.text:
The merger runs over two layer sets. Over every layer of the composition it produces the full merged schema, which the questionnaire asks once (Render Behavior). Over one layer and its ancestors, an ancestor being any layer the layer's extends chain reaches, directly or transitively, taken in topological order, it produces that layer's scoped view: the merged questions, the accumulated _secret_questions and the merged _jinja_extensions of those layers only, which is the flattened template the layer and its ancestors would make if merged by hand, and the Composer's output with that layer as the root. Every render of a layer, at compose and at update, renders under the layer's scoped view. Copier records in a layer's answers file the answers to the questions its template declares (Copier: the answers file), so a layer's answers file records its own and its ancestors' answers and nothing of a sibling or a descendant. A layer's files and questions MAY use only questions its own layer or an ancestor declares. A question's declaring layer is the first layer of the view, in topological order, to hold it; a later layer that only overrides the question does not become its declaring layer.

No render of a layer sees a descendant's or a sibling's questions or extensions, because a descendant's context hook or same-named filter in an ancestor's render would change the ancestor's files (ADR-015 §Verification (2026-10-06)).

An update step takes each question's definition from the full merged schema, so an ancestor's step can receive a descendant's override of the ancestor's question. The override's default, when, validator and choices expressions MUST reference only questions in the scoped view of the layer that declares the overridden question, because a question only the descendant declares is undefined in the ancestor's step. boilerplate validate MUST check this (05 §validate, check V16).

docs.title: Responsibility
docs.text: The RenderEngine takes a CompositionArtifact and an ExecutionContext and orchestrates the actual file generation for each layer using Copier.

docs.title: Copier Worker Interface
docs.text:
The RenderEngine delegates actual file generation to Copier via the run_worker call. This interface abstracts Copier's internal API behind a stable contract owned by Boilerplate. Implementations MUST isolate all Copier API usage behind this interface so that Copier version upgrades require changes only in the worker implementation, not in the composition engine. The supported Copier version range MUST be declared in Boilerplate's package metadata and validated at startup; incompatible versions MUST fail with BP_COPIER_COMPAT_FAILED before any rendering begins.

One Worker subclass serves compose and update. The worker implementation MUST hand Copier the layer's scoped view through a Worker subclass that holds, in its dataclass fields, two scoped views of the layer for each update step, each with its questions and its _jinja_extensions union: the view joined from the versions recorded for the layer and its ancestors, which the old copy renders under, and the view joined from their target versions, which the in-place render and the new copy render under. The subclass builds template from the view that matches the render Copier is making, together with the src_path: the old copy renders the layer's recorded source at its recorded _commit under the recorded-versions view, and the in-place render and the new copy render under the target-versions view. The subclass MUST tell the old copy from the other two renders by the render's destination and never by vcs_ref, because the three renders can carry one ref: when only an ancestor moves, as with project v1 to v2 under streamlit v1 to v1, the old copy, the new copy and the in-place worker, which keeps the walk's ref, all carry v1, yet the recorded-versions view (streamlit@v1 joined with project@v1) and the target-versions view (streamlit@v1 joined with project@v2) differ. Copier creates the old copy's and the new copy's destinations under temporary directories with their own name prefixes, and the in-place render's destination is the project. Reading that prefix is a dependency on Copier's internals that ADR-002 lists among the audited internals. Compose renders every layer through that subclass, and the update walk (Safe Update) runs Copier's update for every layer through it, so every worker Copier builds from it with dataclasses.replace (the old copy, the in-place render and the new copy of an update included) exposes both scoped views of the layer.

run_worker(source_path, destination_path, scoped_view, answers, overwrite, interactive, unsafe, run_tasks) → WorkerResult

Parameter Type Description source_path path Path to the template directory being rendered destination_path path Path to the destination project directory scoped_view map[string, JSON] The layer's scoped view: the merged question schema of the layer and its ancestors answers map[string, JSON] Pre-seeded answers; these override defaults and suppress prompts for matched keys overwrite boolean Whether to overwrite existing files in the destination interactive boolean Whether to prompt the user for unanswered questions unsafe boolean Whether to allow Jinja2 extensions and task execution (required when the _jinja_extensions union of the layer's scoped view is non-empty, or when the operation runs the layer's tasks or migrations; an update step needs it when either the recorded or the target scoped view needs it) run_tasks boolean Whether to execute _tasks after rendering

WorkerResult contains:

Field Type Description user_answers map[string, JSON] Answers explicitly provided by the user or resolved from defaults metadata_answers map[string, JSON] Copier-internal values (e.g., tool version, internal counters)

Behavioral contracts:

  • When interactive=false, the worker MUST NOT prompt; it MUST use answers or question defaults for all values.
  • When run_tasks=false, the worker MUST skip task execution.
  • When unsafe=true, Copier permits Jinja2 extensions and task execution. Because a layer's Worker holds the _jinja_extensions union of its scoped view (see merge strategies), Boilerplate MUST set unsafe=true on a layer's Worker whenever that union is non-empty, and additionally on a layer whose tasks or migrations the operation runs (ADR-003 records this permissive posture). An update step reads two scoped views, the recorded release's and the target's, and MUST set the flag when either view's union is non-empty. A layer whose scoped view declares no extension keeps unsafe=false when the operation runs none of its tasks or migrations.
  • The worker MUST NOT modify source_path in any way.

Assumed Copier behavior: The run_worker contract assumes Copier operates synchronously and single-threaded — it blocks until rendering is complete and does not spawn background processes. If Copier's concurrency model changes in a future version, the worker interface MUST serialize invocations to preserve the sequential layer-rendering guarantee. Copier is also assumed to be non-interactive when interactive=false — it MUST NOT prompt on stdin.
