docs.title: Render Behavior
docs.text:
The RenderEngine asks the questions of the full merged schema (no underscore-prefixed keys) once, across all layers, so the user is prompted only once, and then renders each layer under its scoped view via its own Copier Worker invocation against the same destination directory; per-layer rendering consumes the resolved answers without re-prompting.

Why per-layer rendering: A single Copier invocation for a multi-template composition breaks copier update, which assumes "1 template = 1 Git repository". Boilerplate invokes Copier once per layer and lets each layer own its own answers file, preserving Copier's three-way update flow per layer.

Per-layer rendering and file overlay:

  • Each layer is rendered via its own Copier Worker invocation against the same destination directory; the RenderEngine loops in topological order.
  • Each layer produces its own .copier-answers.<layer>.yml — Copier renders the template's answers-file stub at the path its _answers_file: directive names, and both halves are required (the contract is specified at Per-Layer Render Loop below). Each layer's answers file records the answers to its scoped view's questions, which the layer's later copier update starts from (see Safe Update and 06-project-lifecycle.md §Step 4: Three-Way Merge).
  • Layer N+1 overwrites Layer N's file collisions at the same path (file-level composition; see Composition is file-level, not content-level).
  • Layer-local directives (e.g., _exclude, _skip_if_exists, _subdirectory) are applied per-layer from each layer's own copier.yml; they do not propagate across layers. One exception: _jinja_extensions merges by union within each scoped view (see merge strategies above), so a layer's declared extensions reach its own Worker and every descendant's Worker, and no ancestor's or sibling's. For the rule on _skip_if_exists, see Per-Layer Render Loop below.
  • The unsafe=true flag is passed to a layer's worker whenever the _jinja_extensions union of its scoped view is non-empty, and additionally to a layer whose tasks or migrations the operation runs; an update step passes it when either the recorded or the target scoped view needs it (see Copier Worker Interface).
  • The render operation MUST be aborted with BP_RENDER_TIMEOUT if the wall-clock time exceeds the configured render_timeout setting (default: 300 seconds). See 09-settings-and-configuration.md §Settings for the BOILERPLATE_RENDER_TIMEOUT environment variable.

Single-prompt answer reuse:

  • The full merged schema is computed once from all layers' configurations before rendering begins. All questions from all layers are collected into a single questionnaire, ordered by first appearance in topological order.
  • If interactive mode is enabled, the user is prompted for all questions from the full merged schema in a single interactive session. Conditional visibility (when expressions) is evaluated during prompting. If non-interactive, defaults and pre-seeded answers are used.
  • Each layer's Copier Worker invocation then receives as pre-seeded answers the resolved answers to its scoped view's questions; subsequent layers do NOT re-prompt for previously-answered questions.
  • Tasks are deferred: the accumulated list, in topological order, runs once after the last layer renders (see Task Execution Order).
  • Overwrite: The overwrite flag is passed from the ExecutionContext. When rendering into an empty staging directory (the standard creation path), overwrite does not trigger conflicts because no files pre-exist. When --force is active, files are overwritten freely, including any a layer lists in its own _skip_if_exists (Per-Layer Render Loop). The "full-file replacement" overlay semantics described in Project lifecycle are achieved naturally by per-layer rendering in topological order: later layers' files replace earlier layers' files at the same path.

Composition is file-level, not content-level. When two layers contribute a file at the same path, the later layer's file completely replaces the earlier layer's. There is no line-by-line or AST-level merge of file contents across layers. Template authors building layered compositions should structure templates to avoid file conflicts — for example, by organizing layer-specific content into separate files, by designating a single layer as the owner of a shared file, or by using post-render _tasks to merge content programmatically when the format supports it.

docs.title: Managing Shared Files Across Layers
docs.text:
When multiple layers need to contribute to the same file (e.g., pyproject.toml), full-file replacement means only the last layer's version survives. Template authors SHOULD use one of these patterns:

  1. Single-owner pattern (recommended): Designate one layer as the owner of the shared file. That layer's template renders the complete file under its scoped view, so the file MAY use any question its own layer or an ancestor declares; other layers contribute their values via questions with merge_questions but do not include the shared file in their own template content. The owning layer MUST be, or descend from, every layer that declares a question the shared file uses; the last layer of the composition, the root template, always qualifies, because its extends chain reaches every other layer.

  2. Post-render task: Use a _tasks entry in the final layer to programmatically merge content (e.g., merge TOML sections). This approach is flexible but couples the template to specific tooling. The task runs once against the finished project with the merged answers in scope (ADR-014).

Boilerplate does not perform content-level merging of individual files. This is a deliberate design choice: content merge semantics are format-dependent and would introduce significant complexity.

Note on Jinja2 cross-layer inheritance: Because each layer is rendered by its own Copier invocation (see Render Behavior), {% extends %} directives within a derived layer's templates cannot reach into a different layer's template directory. Cross-layer template inheritance via Jinja2 is NOT supported by the per-layer rendering shape; use the single-owner or post-render-task pattern instead.

docs.title: Per-Layer Render Loop
docs.text:
The RenderEngine iterates layers in topological order. For each layer:

  1. Resolve the layer's source path (filesystem directory, or a Git working tree — the published first-party repository, an org-local clone or mirror, or, once the deferred seed cache exists, a wheel-bundle cache directory). A cache path MUST NEVER be recorded as _src_path in the answers file: Copier records the source it actually used, and masking a local cache path behind a canonical URL would mean rewriting Copier's own answers file, which ADR-015 forbids (ADR-006).
  2. Invoke run_worker against the destination directory through the Worker subclass of the Copier Worker Interface, with the layer's scoped view as the questionnaire, the resolved answers to that view's questions as pre-seeded answers, and the layer's own copier.yml as the source of its layer-local directives.
  3. Copier writes the rendered files into the destination directory and produces the layer's .copier-answers.<layer>.yml (by rendering the layer's answers-file stub at the path named by its _answers_file: directive).

The source template directories on disk are never modified. The destination directory is the same across all layer invocations — file collisions are resolved by overwrite (later layers win), implementing file-level composition.

Compose asks the merged questionnaire once and every layer renders with the same answers, each under its own scoped view, so a layer's answers file records the questions of that view and nothing more. In a composition of project and streamlit, streamlit extends project:

flowchart LR
    accTitle: Merged questionnaire to per-layer answers files
    accDescr: The merged questionnaire is asked once and yields the resolved answers, which feed two renders, project under its own scoped view and streamlit under the project plus streamlit scoped view. The project render writes the project answers file with the project's questions, and the streamlit render writes the streamlit answers file with the project's and streamlit's questions.
    Q["Merged questionnaire<br>asked once"] --> A["Resolved answers"]
    A --> P["Render project<br>scoped view: project"]
    A --> S["Render streamlit<br>scoped view: project + streamlit"]
    P --> PF[".copier-answers.project.yml<br>project's questions"]
    S --> SF[".copier-answers.streamlit.yml<br>project's and streamlit's questions"]
Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom

Layer-local Copier directives — _exclude, _skip_if_exists, _subdirectory, _templates_suffix, _envops — are scoped to the layer that declares them in its own copier.yml. They do NOT propagate across layers; each layer's invocation reads them only from its own copier.yml. _jinja_extensions is merged instead — see the merge strategies table — so every layer's Worker receives the union of the extensions its own layer and its ancestors declare.

_skip_if_exists applies to a layer rendered on its own (update, add), not to a composed render. In a composed render no layer's _skip_if_exists applies: new writes every layer's files, and a later layer overlays this render's own output regardless of what it declares (Composition is file-level, not content-level). A layer rendered on its own applies its own declared list to the files already in the project, because Copier checks _skip_if_exists before overwrite: that is the layer's copier update and the render of a layer add writes into an existing tree (06 §Adding a layer). In the layer's copier update it is Copier's own directive: it stops a merge into a listed file that already exists, and Copier still recreates a listed file the project deleted.

Extensions follow the scoped view. A layer's render receives the _jinja_extensions its own layer and its ancestors declare, and a layer's files and questions MAY use only extensions its own layer or an ancestor declares. When two layers in one scoped view define the same filter or extension name, the later layer in topological order wins; the render MUST warn when a later layer's extension replaces a filter, test or global an earlier layer's extension already registered in the same view, and validate warns on the static case (05 §validate, check V15). An extension declared as a file path inside a template, in the copier-templates-extensions syntax that resolves the path against the template root, MUST be registered by Boilerplate as an importable module loaded from the declaring layer's source at the version the render's scoped view joins, under a module name unique to that layer and version, and handed to the renders that need it. Boilerplate MUST NOT register such an extension once, from one source at the target versions, for every render, because the old copy then renders with the target version's code and the update silently keeps the old output (ADR-015 §Verification (2026-10-06)).

_answers_file: directive and answers-file stub (both mandatory for first-party layers): Each first-party template's copier.yml MUST declare _answers_file: .copier-answers.<layer>.yml, and the template MUST ship an answers-file stub — a template file literally named {{ _copier_conf.answers_file }}.jinja rendering _copier_answers (the project template's stub is the reference pattern). The directive alone is inert: Copier writes an answers file only by rendering the stub; a template lacking one composes cleanly but silently produces no answers file, exit 0, no warning — verified against Copier 9.15.0 (ADR-015 §Verification). Together they are the contract that makes per-layer copier update -a .copier-answers.<layer>.yml work at update time (see 06-project-lifecycle.md §Step 4: Three-Way Merge). validate SHOULD warn when a template declares extends or is offered for composition without a stub, since such a layer is copy-only.

Implementations MUST:

  1. Isolate all Copier API usage behind the Copier Worker Interface.
  2. Include integration tests that verify the per-layer render loop produces the correct destination tree against the declared Copier version.
  3. Treat Copier version upgrades as requiring explicit validation, not automatic adoption.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
If staging directory creation fails, Boilerplate MUST emit BP_RENDER_STAGING_FAILED with the specific error. If a per-layer Copier invocation fails, Boilerplate MUST emit BP_RENDER_TEMPLATE_FAILURE with the specific error and the layer name. The doctor command SHOULD verify that the process has write access to the system temp directory before rendering is attempted.

The supported Copier version range MUST be declared in Boilerplate's package metadata and documented in the CLI --version output.

docs.title: Task Execution Order
docs.text:
See also: 03-template-system.md §Task Execution Safety for trust-level controls and confirmation behavior.

Task execution is deferred: every layer renders with task execution suppressed, and the full accumulated task list runs exactly once, as part of the final layer's Worker invocation, after the composed project's files are complete (ADR-014). At update, the walk runs the same list once after the last layer's update (Safe Update). Deferral preserves Copier's contract — tasks run against a generated project — when the project is the composed whole; running a base layer's tasks mid-composition would execute them against files later layers have not finished writing. The accumulated list preserves topological order across layers (dependencies first, root template last) and declaration order within each layer, so the effective order is the same one per-layer execution would produce. Entries keep Copier's native shapes end-to-end (string = shell, argv list = no shell, mapping = command with optional when/working_directory); conditions evaluate against the merged answers in the final layer's context.

Example: Given app extends [base, middleware]:

base/copier.yml:        _tasks: ["echo base-setup"]
middleware/copier.yml:   _tasks: ["echo middleware-init", "echo middleware-check"]
app/copier.yml:          _tasks: ["echo app-finalize"]

Execution order:
1. echo base-setup          (from base)
2. echo middleware-init      (from middleware)
3. echo middleware-check     (from middleware)
4. echo app-finalize         (from app)

This ordering guarantees that infrastructure tasks (base) run before application tasks (derived), which is the natural dependency order.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text: After all layers complete, return a TemplateInfo describing the final layer (the root template). If the final layer's metadata cannot be loaded, Boilerplate MUST fail with BP_RENDER_METADATA_FAILED — a synthetic "0.0.0" version MUST NOT be silently coined.

docs.title: Safe Update
docs.text:
The boilerplate update pipeline does not re-render the old composition itself. Three-way merge for each layer is performed by Copier's per-template update mechanism, which reconstructs that layer's base internally from the template's Git history. Boilerplate's role is to orchestrate Copier's update per layer in lock order and to own the staging worktree the walk runs in and the copy back of its result (06 §Staging worktree). copier update -a .copier-answers.<layer>.yml names that per-layer operation throughout the design docs; the walk performs it through the same Worker subclass compose uses (Copier Worker Interface; ADR-002) so the layer's scoped view reaches every render, and a hand-run invocation of that command is the escape hatch (ADR-015).

Each layer's old copy uses the versions the descendant was last rendered against. The old copy of a layer's step renders the layer's own template at the _commit its own answers file records and each ancestor at the version boilerplate.lock records for it. The lock records the last complete update, so its versions match what the layer's files were last rendered against, which an ancestor's own _commit no longer does once the ancestor has updated ahead of its descendant.

The walk covers every layer the lock lists, in lock order. The lock lists the root's extends closure in topological order, followed by each layer add introduced, in the order it was added, so every layer follows its ancestors. Each lock entry records how the layer joined the project (LockLayer.joined_via, 02 §BoilerplateLock). Each layer resolves its own target. How targets are named and resolved is 06 §Step 2, and which layers the plan reports as ADDED or REMOVED is 06 §Step 3.

A paused update resumes from its own record. When the last record in .boilerplate/migrations.yml is a conflict MigrationRecord (02 §MigrationRecord), update MUST resume that update, not plan a new one. The record names each layer's target version (targets) and the layers the paused walk finished (finished), the layer whose merge left conflict markers among them. The resumed walk skips the finished layers and runs the remaining layers to the recorded targets, never to the latest release, so a release an unpinned ancestor publishes after the pause does not move the targets. Comparing versions cannot tell a finished layer from an unfinished one: with project v1 to v2, streamlit v1 to v1 and app v1 to v2, streamlit has run under project v2 in the paused walk, but its own _commit equals the lock, so a version comparison would run it again with an old copy at project v1 from the lock, a stale base. A remaining layer's old copy uses its own _commit and the lock's ancestor versions, as in any update. An explicit target (--target-version, bare or <layer>@<version>) that differs from the recorded targets MUST be refused with BP_UPDATE_TARGET_MISMATCH (07 §Error Code Registry), whose message tells the user to set the partial update aside first. A conflict record binds only while the finished layers' answers files still record the recorded targets; once the partial update is set aside, the record no longer binds and update plans afresh.

Without a pending conflict record, drift rules apply. Each layer's old copy uses its own _commit and the lock's ancestor versions, and every layer runs, so a changed answer reaches a layer that is already at its target version. When a layer and one of its ancestors both disagree with the lock, as after a hand-run update of each, the update MUST stop before any layer runs with BP_UPDATE_LAYER_DRIFT (07 §Error Code Registry), naming each layer's _commit and the lock's version and the remediation: undo the hand-run updates with git revert of the commits that hold them, then run update again. Any other disagreement, such as a hand-run update of one layer, MUST warn and proceed, and boilerplate doctor MUST report every disagreement.

A layer's own answers come from its own answers file, and its ancestors' answers arrive as data. Copier reads a layer's own questions from that layer's answers file, after the layer's before-migrations run and Copier clears its cache and re-reads the file (Copier: updating a project), so Boilerplate MUST NOT pass a layer's own recorded answers as data: data outranks the answers file in Copier's answer precedence (AnswersMap.combined), so a recorded value passed before the migrations ran would override what the migrations wrote. For each question an ancestor declares, Boilerplate MUST pass as data, for the in-place render and the new copy, the answer recorded in that declaring ancestor's answers file, read when the layer's step starts. Ancestors update first, so their migrations have run by then. Passed data outranks the layer's own copy of those answers, and Copier rewrites that copy from the layer's target view when the step finishes (Copier: configuration sources). A later layer overrides an earlier one only in the merged template, meaning question definitions and defaults, at compose and at update; it never overrides recorded answers, because a descendant's stale copy of an ancestor's answer would otherwise shadow the ancestor's migrated value.

Prompting happens inside each layer's step, after its migrations. Update prompting is Copier's own: each layer asks its own questions with the recorded answer as the default, as copier update does; update --skip-answered asks only the questions no answers file records; and --non-interactive takes every default, as Copier's defaults does. Prompting is TTY-gated per ADR-013. Each question's definition and default come from the full merged schema at the target versions, while the set of questions a layer asks follows the layer's scoped view, so a descendant's override sets the default of a new ancestor question when the ancestor's step asks it. An ancestor's questions arrive as data in a descendant's step and are not asked again, so each question is asked once, in the layer that declares it. A secret question is asked at the first layer whose scoped view holds it, held in memory for the rest of the update and never recorded, and MUST declare a default, or no render of its layer can run non-interactively. A hidden question is one whose when evaluates false under the layer's own answers file plus, for each question an ancestor declares, the answer recorded in that declaring ancestor's answers file, the same data the walk passes at each step, read in the scoped view at the recorded versions, the literal when: false derived questions among them; a when that reads a key no file records leaves the question not hidden, so the completeness check reports that question's key; Boilerplate computes hidden questions per scoped view and no answers file records them. Compose keeps its single unified pass over the full merged schema (Per-Layer Render Loop), because nothing is recorded and no migration runs at compose.

Each render Copier makes during a layer's update renders under the layer's scoped view at the versions it renders: the old copy renders under the scoped view joined from the recorded versions of the layer and its ancestors, and the in-place render that writes the layer's files and its answers file and the new copy render under the scoped view joined from their target versions. This matches Copier's own single-template behavior that the old copy renders exactly as it did when it was last rendered, which Copier's documentation does not state and ADR-015's 2026-10-06 verification observed, so a target version MAY add a question without a default or retype a question, as with vanilla Copier, subject to the recorded-answer check below. A question the target version removes is still a question in the scoped view at the recorded versions, and its answer comes from the layer's own answers file, so the old copy renders the same as it did when the answer was recorded. A renamed question is a removal plus an addition; carrying the recorded value to the new name is the template's own job, through Copier _migrations. A layer's answers file therefore records, after every update, the answers to the questions of its scoped view at the target versions: its own and its ancestors' answers, and nothing of a sibling or a descendant. The copies exist because Copier builds a layer's merge base, the old copy, from that one file, and a hand-run copier update of the layer reads it too; plain Copier also records a shared question in every template that asks it. Each update rewrites the copy from the declaring layer.

The old copy reads the layer's own answers file, and the walk fills the keys it lacks. Copier builds the old copy with data=self.subproject.last_answers (the old copy's replace call in Worker._apply_update, read at Copier 9.18.1), so the old copy reads the layer's own answers file, and data the walk passes for the update, meaning supplied values and the ancestors' answers read when the step starts, never reaches it. For a question of the scoped view at the recorded versions that the layer's own file does not record, the Worker subclass MUST supply the answer the question's declaring layer recorded when the walk began, before any layer's step ran. A key the layer's own file records keeps its own value. Compose gives every layer the same values and each update rewrites the copy from the declaring layer, so the declaring layer's record at the start of the walk is what the layer was last rendered with; reading it when the walk begins, not when the step starts, keeps a change an ancestor's step makes in the same walk out of the merge base, so the change reaches the layer's files.

In two cases the merge base renders an ancestor's new value, so the layer's lines that use it keep their old rendering, as under plain Copier:

  • Hand-run update. An inherited answer was changed outside Boilerplate after the layer's last render, such as a hand-run update of the ancestor with new data at the same version.
  • Rerun after a conflict. The walk resumes with the finished ancestors already updated, so "when the walk began" means when the rerun begins, and for a layer whose own file is trimmed the fill reads the ancestor's post-update record.

A layer whose own file records its keys, as every file the walk's Copier writes does, is unaffected.

For the in-place render and the new copy, the walk passes as data the answer each question's declaring ancestor recorded, read when the step starts. The diagram follows one step, streamlit over project, and shows which file feeds each of the three renders:

flowchart LR
    accTitle: Files that feed each render of one layer update
    accDescr: Streamlit's own file feeds the old copy with its own keys and feeds the in-place render with its own questions, read after migrations, while the project file as read when the walk began feeds the old copy only with the keys streamlit's file lacks. The project file as read when the step starts feeds the in-place render and the new copy as data, the in-place render writes streamlit's files and answers file, and the old copy and the new copy both go into the three-way merge.
    SF["streamlit's own file"]
    PW["project's file<br>as read when the walk began"]
    PS["project's file<br>as read when the step starts"]
    OLD["Old copy"]
    INP["In-place render"]
    NEW["New copy"]
    OUT["streamlit's files<br>and answers file"]
    MERGE["Three-way merge"]
    SF -->|"own keys"| OLD
    PW -->|"only keys streamlit's file lacks"| OLD
    SF -->|"own questions, read after migrations"| INP
    PS -->|"as data"| INP
    PS -->|"as data"| NEW
    INP --> OUT
    OLD --> MERGE
    NEW --> MERGE
Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom

A trimmed answers file is filled for the old copy, and the in-place render records it again. Without the fill, the old copy reads only the layer's own answers file, so a file that lacks an ancestor's answers renders the ancestor's questions at their defaults, which for project_name (default {{ _folder_name }}) is the old copy's temporary-directory name (_folder_name in Worker._render_context, read at Copier 9.18.1), or fails with Question "x" is required where the question has no default (the ValueError in Worker._ask). A hand-run vanilla update of a child layer trims the file to the layer's own keys (ADR-015). The walk fills a trimmed file's keys for the old copy as above, and the in-place render records the full scoped view's answers again, so Copier restores the file; Boilerplate MUST NOT write it (ADR-015). Before any layer runs, update MUST check that every question of each layer's scoped view at the recorded versions that is neither secret nor hidden, has an answer in the layer's own file or in its declaring layer's file. Where neither records one, update MUST stop with BP_UPDATE_ANSWERS_INCOMPLETE (07 §Error Code Registry), whose message names the layer and the keys and the remediation: undo the hand-run update that trimmed the file, with git revert of the commit that holds it, then run boilerplate update again. boilerplate doctor MUST report a trimmed file and any key no layer records.

The walk runs ancestors first. The walk MUST always run the layers' updates in the order boilerplate.lock lists, which is topological because the lock lists the root's closure in topological order and add appends a layer only after its ancestors, so every ancestor updates before its descendants. A layer's migration that renames a question therefore rewrites that layer's answers file before any descendant's update reads the file as data; a descendant updated first, shipping no migration of its own, finds the question under neither name and records its default with no error (ADR-015 §Verification (2026-10-06)). The walk MUST warn when a layer declares a question that was an ancestor's question in the recorded-version view and is no ancestor's in the target-version view, an orphaned override: a renamed or removed ancestor question leaves the override as a stray question of the layer's own.

Changed questions fail closed. The walk checks each recorded answer against the layer's target view inside the layer's step:

  • When it runs: after the layer's migrations and Copier's re-read of the answers file, and before the in-place render, so a migration that repairs a recorded answer clears it before the check sees it.
  • What it rejects: a recorded answer the target view rejects, by type, choices or validator. The update MUST stop with BP_INPUT_ANSWER_REJECTED (07 §Error Code Registry), and the error names the layer, the question, the recorded value and the remediation --data <question>=<value>. A recorded answer the target's type casts, such as the string "8080" under an int question, passes.
  • How a supplied value replaces it: a value for that question supplied by --data or --data-file replaces the recorded answer, and Copier validates the supplied value instead, so the check applies only to a recorded answer nothing replaces. A supplied value is user input, not a recorded answer, so it does not contradict the rule that a layer's own recorded answers are never passed as data.
  • In a terminal: that question's prompt shows why the recorded answer is rejected and asks for a valid one.
  • Why the check exists: Copier's own update path drops a recorded answer the target rejects and, when the new default passes, records the new default with no warning (ADR-015 §Verification (2026-10-06)).

Tasks run once, after the walk. The walk MUST skip tasks in every render Copier makes during a layer's update; Copier otherwise runs the layer's own _tasks in its old-copy temporary directory, in place and in its new-copy temporary directory (ADR-015 §Verification (2026-10-06)). After the last layer's update completes, including the rerun that finishes an update paused on a conflict, the walk MUST run once, against the finished project, the merged task list of every layer the lock lists, in lock order, the way compose runs the merged list of all its layers (Task Execution Order; ADR-014); --no-tasks skips that run. Skipping tasks leaves a layer's _migrations running in that layer's own update (ADR-007). The run goes through the same Worker subclass, at the target versions with each layer's recorded answers after its update, under Copier's update operation, so a task's when: sees _copier_operation == "update" and a template MAY guard a creation-only task. _copier_operation comes from Copier's private _operation ContextVar (copier._main._operation, read at Copier 9.18.1), which only run_copy, run_recopy and run_update set (through the as_operation decorator; Worker._execute_tasks reads it), so the post-walk run MUST set that ContextVar to "update" around the task run through the shim, and ADR-002 lists it among the audited internals. If a task fails after the files are copied back, a terminal offers to keep the files or undo the run. Keeping the files, whether the terminal user chooses it or --non-interactive does, MUST write the lock, append a failed record, name the failed task and how to rerun it, and exit with 1; undoing the run, as 06 §Undo defines it, appends no record. add handles a failed task the same way (06 §Adding a layer) (FAILURE, ADR-004); exit 4 stays the conflict pause.

See Project lifecycle for the full update workflow, including Copier version management and non-git source fallback.

docs.title: Composition Inspection
docs.text: The CompositionArtifact supports several inspection operations for the CLI compose command.

docs.title: Sections
Error Reference
docs.text: Composition-related errors use the BP_RESOLVE_*, BP_GRAPH_*, BP_RENDER_*, and BP_LOCK_* code families. See Operational quality for the authoritative error code registry and 02-data-models.md §Error Hierarchy for the exception class hierarchy.

docs.title: Invariants
docs.text:
1. Every specifier in sequence MUST appear in nodes, edges, and layers.
  2. sequence MUST be in dependency-first order: for any edge A → B, B MUST appear before A.
  3. final MUST be the result of merging ALL layer configurations; no layer is skipped.
  4. merged_questions_schema MUST contain no underscore-prefixed keys.
  5. The accumulated _tasks list MUST run exactly once, as part of the final layer's Copier invocation, after all layers' files are rendered; non-final layers MUST render with task execution suppressed. At update, every render of the walk MUST suppress task execution, and the merged list of every layer the lock lists MUST run exactly once after the last layer's update, in lock order. The list preserves topological order across layers and declaration order within each layer (see ADR-014).
  6. All questions from all layers MUST be collected into a single questionnaire and prompted once; no re-prompting occurs across per-layer Copier invocations.
  7. Version resolution MUST be deterministic: identical inputs (catalog state, version constraints, source priority ordering) MUST produce identical resolved versions. The resolver MUST NOT consult the system clock, random number generators, or environment variables that vary between invocations.
  8. Once DependencyGraphBuilder returns a graph, its nodes, edges, and sequence MUST NOT be mutated. Stages downstream of the resolver consume the graph as a read-only structure; this guarantees the resolution space is reproducible.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document specifies the Boilerplate CLI surface: every command, flag, argument, output contract, and behavioral invariant. The CLI is an opinionated entry point, but it does not create lock-in — every underlying tool (Copier, Git, uv) remains directly invocable.

This document also specifies the developer experience contracts (pipeline narration, confirmation prompts, post-action guidance, answer presets, interactive prompting) that apply across all commands.

docs.title: Invocation
docs.text:
boilerplate [global-options] <command> [command-options]

The CLI binary name is boilerplate. When invoked with no subcommand, the CLI MUST print the top-level help text and exit with code 0. When boilerplate is invoked with no arguments, the help output MUST include a "Getting started" section at the top: Get started: boilerplate list | boilerplate new <template> <destination>.

docs.title: Global Options
docs.text:
These options apply to all commands and MUST be processed before any subcommand.

Option Short Type Default Description --verbose -v flag false Enable debug-level logging --quiet -q flag false Suppress non-error output --help -h flag — Print help text and exit --version — flag — Print version and exit --templates-dir — path null Override the template search directory for the command --format — enum varies Output format (command-dependent: text, table, json, yaml, tree, wide) --ci flag false Convenience flag equivalent to --non-interactive --yes. Default: false. See --ci behavior below. Component flags inapplicable to a given command (e.g. --non-interactive on eject and adopt) are no-ops for that command. --color — enum auto Color output mode: auto, always, never. Default: auto. --offline — flag false Use only the local cache; do not attempt any network access for remote catalog sources. Default: false.

Task execution truth table: The following table defines the complete behavior of task execution flags across the two trust states. This is the authoritative reference for resolving flag interactions. For a dedicated explanation, see boilerplate help trust.

Trust State Default --yes --no-tasks --allow-tasks --allow-tasks --yes trusted prompt execute skip execute execute untrusted skip + warn skip + warn skip prompt execute
  • prompt: The CLI asks the user to confirm before executing tasks.
  • execute: Tasks run without prompting.
  • skip: Tasks are silently skipped (no warning).
  • skip + warn: Tasks are skipped and a warning lists the skipped commands with the flag needed to enable them.

Flag naming: The canonical flag names are --allow-tasks and --allow-extensions. The convenience alias --allow-untrusted is equivalent to --allow-tasks --allow-extensions.

docs.title: Trust Flags
docs.text:
The following flags govern execution of untrusted template content and are accepted by boilerplate new, boilerplate update, and boilerplate add. They are defined here once; per-command sections reference this definition.

  • --allow-extensions — Allow Jinja2 extensions declared by templates. Required when any template layer uses _jinja_extensions. Default: false.
  • --allow-tasks — Allow task execution for untrusted templates. Default: false. See the Task execution truth table above for trust-state rules.
  • --allow-untrusted — Convenience alias equivalent to --allow-extensions --allow-tasks. Default: false.

--verbose and --quiet are mutually exclusive. If both are provided, the CLI MUST exit with code 3 and a clear error message.

--version: Prints the version string (e.g., boilerplate 0.2.0) and exits with code 0.

--ci behavior: Designed for CI/CD pipelines where no human is present. --ci desugars to --non-interactive --yes: every question takes its default or forced answer, and task execution resolves under the truth table's --yes column, so trusted sources execute and untrusted sources skip with a warning. To execute tasks from an untrusted source in CI, pass --ci --allow-tasks, which resolves under the --allow-tasks --yes column (execute for both trust states).

Environment variable equivalents: BOILERPLATE_CI mirrors --ci; BOILERPLATE_NON_INTERACTIVE mirrors new's --non-interactive (see below). Each is a tool-scoped opt-in following the PIP_NO_INPUT convention: the value is trimmed of surrounding whitespace, then enabled when the trimmed value is non-empty and not 0 or false (case-insensitive) — an explicit 0/false, and empty or whitespace-only, all behave as unset. An explicit CLI flag always wins; the env var can only turn a behavior on, never veto a flag that is present. Both compose with the non-TTY guard (see new command below) exactly as the flags do. The generic CI environment variable is never inspected — see ADR-013.

--color modes: auto uses TTY detection and NO_COLOR. always forces color on (useful when piping to less -R). never forces color off. Follows the convention established by git, cargo, and ripgrep.

--offline behavior: Operations requiring templates not present in the local cache will fail with BP_RESOLVE_TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND (the template cannot be found in any available source). Local filesystem sources are always available regardless of this flag. Use boilerplate cache warm to pre-populate the cache for offline use.

--templates-dir: When provided, it is added to the catalog build before the configured extra_template_dirs. Resolution order (highest to lowest priority): --templates-dir (if provided) → default_templates_dir (the user's default template directory) → extra_template_dirs → first-party templates (the published per-template git repositories, ADR-006; implicit source) — authoritative definition in 03 §Template Directory Resolution Order. The --templates-dir flag takes highest priority, allowing users to override all configured directories. This ensures explicit CLI arguments always win over configuration.

--format per-command support: Every command MUST support --format json. Additional formats are command-specific:

Command Supported Formats new text (default), json update, add, status, doctor, validate, init-template, env table (default), json list table (default), json, wide compose yaml (default), json graph table (default), json, tree

When --format json is active, the command MUST output exactly one JSON object to stdout. No progress output, no human-readable messages. Errors are included in the JSON object's error field, not printed separately.

docs.title: Template Argument Resolution
docs.text:
All commands that accept a template reference use the <template-spec> argument name for consistency. Several commands (compose, graph, validate) accept a <template-spec> argument that may be either a template name/reference or a filesystem path. The CLI MUST resolve this argument using the following rule:

  1. If the argument contains a path separator (/ or \) or starts with ., treat it as a filesystem path. Load the template directly from the directory.
  2. Otherwise, treat it as a template reference (name or name@version) and resolve via the catalog.

This means boilerplate compose ./project is always a path, and boilerplate compose project is always a catalog lookup. To force path resolution for a directory in the current working directory whose name matches a template, use ./name.

docs.title: Help Text Structure
docs.text:
The --help output MUST use visual grouping to organize commands by domain. A Get started: block MUST appear before command groups to give new users an immediate entry point. Global options MUST appear at the bottom (lowest priority for new users). On a terminal that can show it, the top-level help opens with the banner:

Usage: boilerplate [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]

  Less yak. More stack.

  Pairs a Python development environment, one tool for each job, with templates that build on one another to stamp out projects.

  Get started:
    boilerplate list                    Browse available templates
    boilerplate new <template> <dest>   Create a new project

Project commands:
  new            Create a new project from a template
  update         Update project to newer template version
  add            Add a template layer to a managed project
  adopt          Import an existing Copier project into Boilerplate
  eject          Stop Boilerplate management of a project
  status         Show project and environment state

Template commands:
  list           List and search available templates
  compose        Show template composition and merged config
  graph          Show template dependency graph
  validate       Validate a template directory
  init-template  Create a new template skeleton
  test           Run template regression tests

System commands:
  doctor         Run health checks
  env            Manage environment profiles
  cache          Pre-populate template cache
  lock           Lock file operations (verify)

Global options:
  -v, --verbose       Enable debug logging
  -q, --quiet         Suppress non-error output
      --format FMT    Output format (text, json, table, yaml, tree, wide)
      --templates-dir Override template search directory
      --ci            CI mode (non-interactive, --yes)
      --color MODE    Color output (auto, always, never)
      --offline       Use local cache only
  -h, --help          Show this message and exit
      --version       Show version and exit

docs.title: Banner
docs.text:
The banner is the CLI logo drawn in braille dots beside the name boilerplate in ASCII art. It prints in one place: above the top-level help (boilerplate, boilerplate --help, and boilerplate -h). Subcommand help, --version, and every command MUST NOT print it; new is the command people run most, so its first prompt opens the run. A blank line MUST come before the banner, setting it apart from the command line above; when no banner prints, neither does that line.

Look: the logo is docs/assets/boilerplate-cli-logo.svg drawn in braille at 11 rows, its braces and bars in brand blue (#40B4E5) and its >_ prompt in the terminal's default text color, so the prompt follows the theme. The name is FIGlet's standard font in bold, 49 columns by 6 rows, centered vertically 3 columns to the logo's right. Both ship as text that scripts/render_cli_banner.py generates from the SVG ahead of time; the CLI reads no image at runtime. At every width, the art MUST keep the logo's shapes clean at braille resolution:

  • Each bar is exactly two dot rows tall in every column it lights, with equal gaps between bars.
  • Where the logo shows a bar's end past the chevron, the art shows it too: the long bars all end in one column unless a prompt cell covers it.
  • The chevron is mirror-symmetric about its tip.
  • The prompt is painted over the bars. A character cell prints in one color, so a cell holding any prompt dot drops its blue dots, and the braces end on the cell row above the underscore's so the two never share a cell.
  • No stray dots: only a bar's end showing past the prompt forms a cluster of four dots or fewer.

Layout: the CLI MUST print the first layout below that fits. A layout fits when the terminal is at least as wide as the layout, so no row wraps, and tall enough for the layout and the blank line before it, so the whole banner can be on screen at once. More height buys nothing: the help that follows scrolls the banner away regardless. When neither fits, no banner prints.

Layout Fits when the terminal has at least Also requires Logo beside name logo width + 3 + 49 columns (74–81), and 12 lines Braille output Name alone 49 columns and 7 lines —

Braille output requires a UTF-8 stdout, a TERM other than linux (the Linux text console, whose fonts lack braille), and output that is not ASCII-only. When color is off (--color never, or NO_COLOR without --color always, per Terminal Accessibility rules 1 and 4), the banner MUST contain only printable ASCII, so the name prints alone, without color or bold.

Logo width: the source image is square, so the logo's width in columns MUST follow the terminal's cell shape (cell height divided by cell width). The default shape is 2.25, which gives 25 columns. On POSIX, when the terminal reports its window size in pixels (TIOCGWINSZ) and the report is plausible (at least 2 pixels per column and 4 per row), the CLI MUST derive the shape from it and use the generated width nearest to 11 × shape, from 22 to 29 columns. The CLI MUST NOT ask the terminal for its cell size with escape sequences: the reply needs raw mode and a timeout, and Windows Terminal answers with a fixed virtual cell.

Suppression: the banner MUST NOT print when any of these holds:

  • stdout is not a terminal, or TERM is dumb or unknown
  • BOILERPLATE_ACCESSIBLE is enabled (Terminal Accessibility rule 5)
  • on Windows, the system reports a running screen reader (SPI_GETSCREENREADER), which could read each braille cell aloud
  • BOILERPLATE_NO_BANNER is enabled, by the truthiness rule of the other BOILERPLATE_* boolean env vars (see the environment variable equivalents note in Global Options)
  • --quiet is active (Quiet Mode)

docs.title: "Did You Mean?" for Unknown Commands
docs.text:
If the user types an unknown command, the CLI MUST suggest the closest match based on edit distance. Example:

$ boilerplate nw streamlit
Error: Unknown command 'nw'. Did you mean 'new'?

docs.title: Help Topics
docs.text:
The CLI MUST support boilerplate help <topic> for extended documentation on cross-cutting concerns. Help topics are distinct from command help (--help) — they provide conceptual explanations rather than flag references.

boilerplate help trust: Displays the trust model documentation: the binary trusted/untrusted states and how they are assigned, the task execution truth table (from Global Options above), flag interactions, and examples of common flag combinations. See 03-template-system.md §Trust and Verification for the canonical trust model.

If boilerplate help is invoked without a topic, it MUST list available topics. If an unknown topic is provided, it MUST suggest the closest match.

docs.title: Command Examples
docs.text:
Every command's --help output MUST include an Examples: section showing at least two representative invocations. Examples MUST use realistic values, not placeholder strings like <foo>. They appear after the options table and before the exit codes.

Example for new:

Examples:
  boilerplate new project my-service
  boilerplate new streamlit@1.0.0 ./my-dashboard --no-git-init
  boilerplate new streamlit my-app --data-file ci/answers.yml --non-interactive

docs.title: new
docs.text:
Usage: boilerplate new <template-spec> <destination> [options]

Resolve, compose, and render a template into a destination directory. This is the primary project creation command.

Arguments:

Argument Required Description template-spec Yes Template reference: name or name@version destination Conditional Target directory path. MUST be provided as an argument OR prompted interactively.

Version syntax: The CLI accepts name (resolves to latest) or name@version (exact version). Version ranges (e.g., name@>=2.0) are NOT supported at the CLI level — they are resolved internally within extends chains.

If <template-spec> is omitted and the terminal is interactive, Boilerplate presents a simple numbered selection prompt listing available templates (name, version, one-line description) for the user to pick from. In non-interactive mode, omitting <template-spec> is an error.

Template selection prompt: When <template-spec> is omitted and stdin is a TTY, Boilerplate lists available templates and prompts for a selection. Selecting a template proceeds to the question prompts; pressing Ctrl+C exits without action (exit code 130), the same cancellation code used everywhere else in the CLI.

The selection prompt MUST NOT make network calls. It operates only on locally cached catalog data. If no templates are found from configured sources, it MUST list first-party templates under the heading 'First-party templates — get started quickly'. The diagnostic message suggesting boilerplate doctor MUST only appear if no templates are found at all, including first-party templates.

Destination behavior: The destination MUST be explicitly provided or interactively prompted. The CLI MUST NOT default to a template-named subdirectory. When --non-interactive is active and no destination is provided, the CLI MUST exit with code 3 and the message Error: destination is required in non-interactive mode.

Options:

Option Short Type Default Description --force -f flag false Overwrite a non-empty destination (no confirmation). Default: false. --non-interactive — flag false Use defaults for all unanswered questions without prompting. Default: false. --dry-run -n flag false Show the composition plan without rendering or writing files. Default: false. --render-to — path null Render the template to the specified directory for inspection without creating a managed project. Default: null. --git-init — flag true Initialize a Git repository in the created project directory. Default: true. Use --no-git-init to skip. --data -d key=value — Forced answer for one question (repeatable). Never prompted for; satisfies the non-interactive required-answer pre-flight. Precedence on collision: --data > --data-file > profile pre-fills > template default. See Answer Presets. --data-file — path null YAML file mapping question name to forced answer, read as UTF-8: an answer preset. Same forced-answer semantics as --data; --data wins on a key collision. --no-tasks — flag false Skip execution of all template tasks (_tasks). Default: false. --yes -y flag false Suppress confirmation prompts for task execution and Jinja2 extension loading. Default: false. For untrusted templates, --allow-tasks (or --allow-untrusted) is additionally required. Does not affect interactive question prompts — use --non-interactive for that.

Trust flags (--allow-extensions, --allow-tasks, --allow-untrusted): see Trust Flags.

--data and --data-file: The flags that supply answers on a single invocation. Both name Copier's own forced-answers flags (--data/-d and --data-file), so the names and the short flag carry over unchanged for anyone already familiar with Copier. Copier's -a and -s mean --answers-file and --skip, so Boilerplate defines neither. Precedence, the YAML format and the handling of _-prefixed keys are in Answer Presets.

--no-tasks is the canonical flag name. --skip-tasks is accepted as an alias for compatibility but is not displayed in help text.

Short flags are reserved for options typed at a prompt, such as -f and -n, and for Copier's own -d. --non-interactive and --no-tasks are scripted, safety-relevant switches and have no short form; -n means dry run here as it does in Copier, make and rsync.

--dry-run vs --render-to: --dry-run shows the composition plan and the list of files that would be created without producing any output. To render files for inspection without committing a managed project, use --render-to <dir>.

--git-init rationale: Git initialization is the default because boilerplate update requires a Git repository.

Reusing a finished run's answers: when the template ships the answers-file stub (04 §Render Behavior), the root template's .copier-answers.<template>.yml that new leaves in the project (the template named on new, not any layer's file) is a complete answer preset, secret answers excepted. Pass it to --data-file.

--force and --non-interactive are independent concerns. --non-interactive means "use defaults for all questions." --force means "overwrite a non-empty destination." Neither implies the other: CI may need --non-interactive without --force (fail if the destination is non-empty), and a retry may need --force while still prompting interactively.

--non-interactive environment variable equivalent: BOILERPLATE_NON_INTERACTIVE mirrors this flag with OR semantics — see the environment variable equivalents note in Global Options.

Behavior: See Project lifecycle for the full creation pipeline. Task execution follows the trust-level rules in the Global Options truth table above and the full safety model in 03-template-system.md §Task Execution Safety.

Key behavioral contracts:

  • --dry-run: Runs resolve and compose, displays the composition plan without rendering. Exits 0 on success.
  • --render-to: Renders to a directory for inspection without creating a managed project. Skips lock file, .boilerplate/, git init, and atomic staging. Tasks are not executed in --render-to mode by default. To execute tasks, pass --allow-tasks; the normal trust-level rules then apply (see Global Options truth table). Requires --force if target is non-empty.
  • --git-init (default true): Initializes a git repo after rendering. Does not create an initial commit. If git init fails, emits a WARNING but does not fail the operation.

Exit codes:

  • 0 — template rendered successfully
  • 1 — rendering failed (template not found, Copier error, etc.)
  • 2 — configuration could not be loaded
  • 3 — input validation failed (missing destination, invalid specifier, etc.)

docs.title: update
docs.text:
Usage: boilerplate update [options]

Update an existing project to a newer template version. The walk runs in a temporary git worktree of the project and lands in the working tree as uncommitted changes, which is what plain Copier leaves (06-project-lifecycle.md §Staging worktree). See Project lifecycle for the full update workflow.

Prerequisite: The project directory MUST be a git repository. The update command requires git access to each layer's template source so that Copier can perform per-layer three-way merge, and uses git for the staging worktree. The working tree MUST have no uncommitted changes, untracked files included, which is Copier's own rule, and a project with submodules (.gitmodules) is refused. Projects created without --git-init that were never placed under git version control cannot be updated. Run git init && git add -A && git commit -m 'Initial project' first.

Limitation: Projects created from Copier-only templates (templates without boilerplate.yml) do not have a boilerplate.lock file and cannot be updated via boilerplate update. Use copier update directly for these projects.

Options:

Option Short Type Default Description --dry-run -n flag false Show update plan and exit without prompting or applying. Default: false. --target-version -t string (repeatable) null Target version. <version> names the root template's target and <layer>@<version> names that layer's, so the option repeats to pin several layers. Default: each layer's latest. A layer the lock does not list stops the run with BP_UPDATE_LAYER_UNKNOWN, and a version another lock layer's extends constraint excludes with BP_UPDATE_TARGET_EXCLUDED; resolution is in 06 §Step 2. Refused when it differs from the targets a pending conflict record names. --data -d key=value — Forced answer for one question (repeatable). Never prompted for. Precedence on collision: --data > --data-file > the recorded answer > template default. See Answer Presets. --data-file — path null YAML file mapping question name to forced answer, read as UTF-8: an answer preset. --data wins on a key collision. --yes -y flag false Skip confirmation prompt; apply immediately. Default: false. --non-interactive — flag false Take every question's default without prompting, a recorded answer being its question's default. Default: false. --skip-answered — flag false Ask only the questions no answers file records. Default: false. --no-tasks — flag false Skip execution of all template tasks (_tasks). Default: false. --template-source — path or URL null Override the template source location used by Copier when its built-in resolution cannot reach the template. Default: null.

Trust flags (--allow-extensions, --allow-tasks, --allow-untrusted): see Trust Flags.

--skip-answered: Ask only the questions no answers file records, as Copier's --skip-answered does; every recorded answer stands without a prompt. Prompting happens inside each layer's step (design 04 §Safe Update).

--non-interactive: Take every question's default without prompting, as Copier's --defaults does. A recorded answer is the default of its question, so existing answers from each layer's .copier-answers.<layer>.yml are reused and a new question takes its declared default.

--data and --data-file: Both are laid over the data each layer's step receives, as Copier's own --data is laid over the answers it reads. A value supplied for a question whose recorded answer the target view rejects replaces that answer, and Copier validates the supplied value instead.

Default behavior: Compute the update plan, display it, then prompt the user for confirmation before applying. This is one command, one flow — not a two-step dry-run-then-apply cycle.

Interactive flow (TTY output):

Update plan for my-project

  Template versions:
    project     0.1.0 -> 0.2.0  MINOR
    streamlit   0.1.0 -> 0.1.1  PATCH

  Files (12 total):
    Modified    pyproject.toml        merge required (template + local changes)
    Modified    src/config.py         clean update (template change only)
    Added       src/middleware.py
    Removed     src/legacy_config.py

  Summary: 12 files affected, 1 merge required, 0 conflicts predicted

Proceed? [y/N]

MAJOR updates MUST include a prominent warning about breaking changes in the plan summary.

--dry-run: Print the plan and exit without prompting or applying. For CI/scripting where you want the plan as output without any interaction.

--yes/-y: Print the plan, skip the prompt, apply immediately. For automation.

Task execution: Follows the same trust-level rules as new (see 03-template-system.md §Task Execution Safety).

Conflicts: When a layer's update produces conflicts, the CLI brings back the layers finished so far with Copier's conflict markers in the affected files, writes no lock file and exits with code 4 (ACTION_REQUIRED, BP_UPDATE_CONFLICT_PAUSED). The user resolves the conflicts and commits as with plain Copier, then reruns boilerplate update, which resumes from the conflict record in .boilerplate/migrations.yml: the record names each layer's target version and the layers already finished, so the rerun skips those layers and walks the rest to the recorded targets. An explicit --target-version that differs from the record is refused until the user sets the partial update aside. How to set it aside, before or after the commit, is in 06 §Setting a partial update aside. A rerun before the user commits stops at the clean working tree check with exit code 3 (06-project-lifecycle.md §Step 5).

Interrupted runs: A run cut off while it copies its result back or finishes is completed by running the same command again, when the working tree holds only what the run wrote and no conflict had paused the run. The rerun finishes that run and ends with its exit code, planning no new update. Otherwise the rerun stops with BP_UPDATE_INTERRUPTED, and the user sets the partial update aside (06 §Setting a partial update aside). No flag is involved.

File status indicators:

TTY Label Non-TTY/JSON Code Meaning Modified M Template changed this file Added A New file from template Removed D File removed in new template version Conflict C Both template and local changes detected (predicted)

TTY output uses full-word labels for immediate comprehension. Non-TTY and JSON output use single-letter codes for parseability. JSON output MUST include both fields: "status": "M" and "status_label": "Modified".

Confirmation rules: MAJOR updates MUST show a risk warning in the plan summary. All updates prompt Proceed? [y/N] unless --yes is active. See Confirmation Contracts.

JSON output: --format json with --dry-run outputs the plan (including updates_available: bool); with --yes outputs the result. --format json without --dry-run or --yes exits with code 3 — JSON mode requires explicit intent.

Exit codes: 0 on success, 1 on failure, 2 on config error, 3 on validation error.

docs.title: add
docs.text:
Usage: boilerplate add <template-spec> [path] [options]

Add one template layer to a project Boilerplate already manages, the way a by-hand copier copy with its own answers file would, and record it in boilerplate.lock. See 06-project-lifecycle.md §Adding a layer for the full workflow.

Arguments:

Argument Required Description template-spec Yes Template reference: name or name@version path No Path to the project directory (defaults to .)

Options:

Option Short Type Default Description --dry-run -n flag false Show the add plan and exit without prompting or applying. Default: false. --data -d key=value — Forced answer for one question (repeatable). Never prompted for. Precedence on collision: --data > --data-file > an ancestor layer's recorded answer > template default. See Answer Presets. --data-file — path null YAML file mapping question name to forced answer, read as UTF-8: an answer preset. --data wins on a key collision. --yes -y flag false Skip confirmation prompt; apply immediately. Default: false. --non-interactive — flag false Use defaults for the layer's questions without prompting. Default: false. --no-tasks — flag false Skip execution of all template tasks (_tasks). Default: false. --template-source — path or URL null Override the template source location used by Copier when its built-in resolution cannot reach the template. Default: null.

Trust flags (--allow-extensions, --allow-tasks, --allow-untrusted): see Trust Flags.

add has no --force: the clean working tree check cannot be skipped.

Preconditions: each failure happens before any file changes and exits with code 3 (VALIDATION_ERROR; ADR-004).

Precondition Error and remediation The project is managed: boilerplate.lock exists BP_UPDATE_PROJECT_NOT_MANAGED: Project is not managed by Boilerplate. Use 'boilerplate adopt' first. The working tree is clean BP_UPDATE_PROJECT_NOT_READY: Working tree has uncommitted changes. Commit them, or run 'git reset' and then 'git stash --include-untracked', before running boilerplate add. The template is not already in the project BP_UPDATE_LAYER_ALREADY_ADDED: Template '{name}' is already in this project. Use 'boilerplate update' instead. Every template the new layer extends, transitively, is already in the lock BP_UPDATE_ANCESTORS_MISSING. The error names each missing layer. Remediation: boilerplate add <ancestor> first. Each such ancestor's recorded version satisfies the new layer's extends constraint BP_UPDATE_ANCESTOR_VERSION_MISMATCH. The error names the ancestor, its recorded version and the constraint. Remediation: boilerplate update first.

add and update stay separate operations: add never changes a layer already in the project.

Interrupted runs: A run cut off while it copies the layer back, runs its tasks, writes the lock or appends the record is completed by running the same command again, when the working tree holds only what the run wrote; the rerun ends with that run's exit code and adds nothing new. Otherwise the rerun stops with BP_UPDATE_INTERRUPTED, and the user sets the partial add aside (06 §Setting a partial update aside). No flag is involved.

Default behavior: Compute the add plan, display it, then prompt for confirmation before applying, as update does. The plan, which --dry-run also prints, lists the layer and its version, the files, the layer's own tasks (each command), the Jinja extensions its scoped view loads, and one line on what undo can and cannot reverse (06 §Undo). --dry-run prints the plan and exits; --yes skips the prompt. The result lands as uncommitted changes, so the user reviews and commits it.

--data and --data-file: Both are laid over the new layer's questionnaire data, as Copier's own --data is.

Task execution: The new layer's tasks run once, before the lock and the record, under the same trust-level rules as new (see 03-template-system.md §Task Execution Safety). A task that fails is handled as for update (design 04 §Safe Update).

Trust: new and add follow one trust rule under ADR-003. The posture keys on the template's source, not the destination, and Copier's own trust check never reads the destination. Under the target trust model, add's plan prompt is its consent prompt for the layer's tasks and extensions: one prompt, shown before any extension loads (03 §Jinja2 Extension Safety).

JSON output: --format json with --dry-run outputs the plan; with --yes outputs the result. --format json without either exits with code 3, as for update.

Exit codes: 0 on success, 1 on failure, 2 on config error, 3 on validation error.

docs.title: list
docs.text:
Usage: boilerplate list [query] [options]

List and search available templates from the catalog. When a query is provided, matching templates are filtered case-insensitively and returned in a deterministic order. Whether or not a query is provided, results use the same stable ordering (see Ordering below).

Arguments:

Argument Required Description query No Keyword search query. Matched case-insensitively against template name, description, and tags.

Options:

Option Description --category <cat> Filter by category. --tag <tag> Filter by tag (repeatable). --trust <state> Filter by trust state: trusted, untrusted. --type <type> Filter by classification: boilerplate-enabled, copier-only. --all-versions Show all versions of each template. Default: latest only. --include-archived Include archived templates in results. Default: excluded. --source <name> Restrict results to a specific catalog source. --refresh Sync remote sources before listing.

Default behavior: Show latest published versions from all sources. Deprecated templates are shown with a warning indicator and successor reference (if declared). Archived templates are hidden.

First-party template fallback: When no configured catalog sources return results (fresh install, empty catalog, or all sources filtered out), list MUST show first-party templates under a First-party templates header. This ensures the "Getting started" path (boilerplate list → boilerplate new) never dead-ends on a fresh install. When truly empty (no first-party templates either), display: No templates found. Run 'boilerplate new' to browse first-party templates interactively, or configure sources. See: boilerplate doctor.

Ordering: Results use the deterministic catalog ordering defined in 03 §Result Ordering — source priority (lower number first), then name, then version (descending). Trust state does not affect ordering; it is displayed in the Trust column. A query only filters the set; it does not reorder it.

Output columns (table format): Name, Version, Type, Trust, State, Description

When --format wide is active, also show: Source, Tags, Path, Last Updated

Empty result behavior: If no results match, print: "No templates found matching '{query}'. Try --refresh to update the catalog or adjust your filters." Exit with code 0.

Exit codes:

  • 0 — command completed (results may be empty)
  • 1 — catalog could not be loaded

docs.title: compose
docs.text:
Usage: boilerplate compose <template-spec> [options]

Show the composition artifact for a template — the merged configuration produced by resolving and combining all template layers.

Arguments:

Argument Required Description template-spec Yes Template reference: name, name@version, or a directory path

Direct path support: Accepts a directory path in addition to catalog-registered template names. See Template Argument Resolution for disambiguation rules. When a path is provided, the template is loaded directly from disk without catalog registration.

Options:

Option Short Type Default Description --questions -Q flag false Show the merged questionnaire (names, types, defaults) for CI discovery. Default: false. --section <name> — string final Composition section to display: final, layers, states, deltas, stats (repeatable). Default: final. --all — flag false Include all composition sections. Default: false. --stats — flag false Shortcut for --section stats. Default: false. --output -o path null Write artifacts to a directory. Default: null.

Default behavior (no flags): Display the final composition section in YAML format.

--section is repeatable: --section layers --section deltas displays both sections. --all is a convenience equivalent to specifying all five sections.

--questions mode: Shows the merged questionnaire — only user-facing questions (no _ directives), displayed as a table of name, type, default, and help text. This is the primary discovery mechanism for CI pipelines building answer presets. With --format json, outputs a machine-readable schema. Each question entry includes name, type, help, default, choices, required, and a default_is_expression boolean (to distinguish Jinja2 expressions from literal defaults).

Composition sections:

Section Content final The fully merged Copier configuration layers Per-layer question values states Per-layer cumulative state deltas Per-layer delta from previous state stats Aggregate statistics about the composition

Output behavior: With --output <dir>, writes each section as a file ({section}.{format}). Without --output, prints to stdout. --output MUST point to a directory.

Exit codes: 0 on success, 1 on failure, 3 on validation error.

docs.title: graph
docs.text:
Usage: boilerplate graph <template-spec> [options]

Show the dependency graph and execution sequence for a template.

Arguments:

Argument Required Description template-spec Yes Template reference: name, name@version, or a directory path

Direct path support: Accepts a directory path in addition to catalog-registered template names. See Template Argument Resolution for disambiguation rules. When a path is provided, the template is loaded directly from disk without catalog registration.

Options:

Option Short Type Default Description --tree — flag false Use tree format instead of numbered table. Default: false.

Default behavior: Show the dependency execution sequence as a numbered table:

#   Layer          Version   Path
1   project        2.1.0     /path/to/project
2   streamlit      1.0.0     /path/to/streamlit

When a diamond dependency pattern is detected (a node reachable via two or more paths), affected nodes are annotated with a [diamond] indicator noting which parent's files take precedence (see Composition engine for the precedence rules).

--tree mode: Hierarchical view of the dependency structure:

streamlit@1.0.0
└── project@2.1.0

When stdout is a TTY, Unicode box-drawing characters are used. When NO_COLOR is set or stdout is not a TTY, ASCII equivalents are used.

Exit codes: 0 on success, 1 on failure, 3 on validation error.

docs.title: validate
docs.text:
Usage: boilerplate validate <template-dir> [options]

Validate that a template directory is well-formed and its references are resolvable.

Arguments:

Argument Required Description template-dir Yes Path to the template directory to validate

Direct path support: Accepts a directory path in addition to catalog-registered template names. See Template Argument Resolution for disambiguation rules.

Checks:

ID Check Severity Description V01 boilerplate.yml present error Required file V02 copier.yml present error Required file V03 boilerplate.yml schema valid error All required fields, valid types V04 name matches ^[a-zA-Z0-9_\-]+$ error Name format validation V05 version is valid PEP 440 error Version format validation V06 extends references resolvable warning Checks against catalog (warns if catalog unavailable) V07 copier.yml loadable by Copier error Parsing is delegated to Copier's own config loader per Template system and discovery; Copier-native constructs such as the !include tag and multi-document files are valid. Loading reads configuration only — _tasks/_migrations are never executed. V08 No duplicate keys in YAML files error YAML spec compliance. For copier.yml the check is structural (node-level scan, no tag construction), so Copier-native tags cannot break it. V09 No custom YAML tags error Security constraint, scoped to boilerplate.yml; copier.yml parsing is delegated to Copier per Template system and discovery. V10 .gitmodules maps extends parents error Only runs when .gitmodules is present: each extends parent maps to a submodule path and submodules are initialized. V11 Version constraints satisfiable error Version constraints across the resolved extends chain are mutually satisfiable. Only runs when extends dependencies are resolvable. V12 Composition merge conflicts error When the validated template has extends dependencies and those dependencies are resolvable from configured sources, validate MUST run the full Resolver → Composer pipeline and report any MergeConflictError as a validation error. This ensures composition issues are caught at authoring time, not at boilerplate new time. V13 File path collisions across layers warning When a derived template provides a file at the same path as a base template, the base file is silently replaced (last layer wins). validate MUST detect these collisions and emit a warning: File 'pyproject.toml' in layer 'streamlit@1.0.0' overrides the same file in 'project@2.1.0'. This is intentional (last layer wins) but may be unexpected. This check only runs when extends dependencies are resolvable. V14 Jinja extensions allowlisted error Declared _jinja_extensions, if any, resolve to packages on the system-wide allowlist (allowed_extension_packages, 09 §Settings). V15 Extension class names unique within the scoped view warning When two layers in the validated template's scoped view declare extensions with the same class name from different import paths, validate MUST warn, naming the class name, both import paths and both layers; the render warns on a runtime replacement (04 §Per-Layer Render Loop). This check only runs when extends dependencies are resolvable. V16 Overrides stay within the overridden question's scope error When a layer overrides a question an ancestor declares, the override's default, when, validator and choices expressions MUST reference only questions in the scoped view of the layer that declares the overridden question, because the ancestor's update step takes the override's definition from the full merged schema and a question only the descendant declares is undefined there. validate MUST report each reference outside that scope, naming the override, the question and the layer. This check only runs when extends dependencies are resolvable. V17 Ancestor question not redeclared unchanged warning When a layer's copier.yml declares a question an ancestor declares and the declaration is identical to the ancestor's, validate MUST warn, naming the question and both layers, because the layer's scoped view already hands the ancestor's question to every render of the layer (03 §Overriding a question in a derived template). It warns rather than fails because merge_questions merges the identical declaration harmlessly. This check only runs when extends dependencies are resolvable.

Check IDs are stable and may be cited in error messages and CI output. This table is the authoritative check registry; 03 §Validation Surface defines the invariants validation must uphold.

--strict flag: When --strict is active, warnings are promoted to errors. validate --strict exits 1 if any check produces a warning or error. This enables CI pipelines to enforce strict template quality: boilerplate validate --strict ./my-template.

Output (unified check-result format):

Validating template at ./my-template...

  PASS  boilerplate.yml present and valid
  PASS  copier.yml present and parseable
  PASS  Name 'my-template' is valid
  PASS  Version '1.0.0' is valid PEP 440
  WARN  extends reference 'base-project' not found in catalog
        -> Refresh catalog: boilerplate list --refresh

5 checks: 4 passed, 1 warning, 0 errors

All check-result commands (validate, doctor, lock verify) use 4-character status labels: PASS, WARN, FAIL. Failures and warnings include inline remediation lines prefixed with ->. See Terminal Accessibility.

Exit codes: 0 valid (warnings only), 1 invalid (errors found or --strict with warnings), 3 path doesn't exist or validation could not run.

docs.title: status
docs.text:
Usage: boilerplate status

Reports the current state of the Boilerplate installation and, if present, the project in the working directory.

Roadmap note: The status command is deferred to Phase 3 per the roadmap. The specification below defines its target behavior; it is not part of the current CLI surface.

Sections:

Section When shown Project When boilerplate.lock exists in the working directory Environment When .boilerplate/environment.yml exists in the working directory Settings Always

Update availability: When a project is present, status MUST check whether newer template versions are available (cached catalog only — no network calls).

When any configured path does not exist, status MUST append: Run 'boilerplate doctor' for diagnostics.

Exit codes: 0 on success. status is informational and MUST report state issues (missing or corrupted boilerplate.lock, missing or corrupted .boilerplate/environment.yml, stale cached catalog) in its output rather than via exit code. The single exception is the universal Settings-load failure: if loading the Settings object fails, the CLI MUST exit with code 2 (CONFIG_ERROR) per §09 Settings — this rule applies to every command including status.

docs.title: adopt
docs.text:
Usage: boilerplate adopt [project-dir] [options]

Import an existing Copier-managed project into Boilerplate lifecycle management.
