When the update exits with code 4 (ACTION_REQUIRED) due to merge conflicts, a conflict record is appended that names each layer's target version and the layers the walk finished, as the restore marker holds them (02 §MigrationRecord). When a task fails after the copy back and the run exits with code 1, a failed record is appended. The status: success value is written only when a run completes every layer.
  • The file MUST be created with the initial created MigrationRecord on project creation (per Step 5 above), not as an empty file. The audit log is complete from inception.
  • Writes to migrations.yml MUST follow the single-file tmp-then-rename recipe in 07 §Atomic Staged Write Pattern; the temporary file is migrations.tmp.{random_suffix}.
  • The record is appended once, when the operation ends, and the restore marker and its ref are removed only after that. Per-status timing:
  • success MUST be written AFTER the lock file has been successfully written. This ordering ensures the lock file is the authoritative source of truth for completed updates. On the rerun after a conflict, success is appended as a new record (per Step 5) and the conflict record stays unmodified.
  • conflict is written at exit 4 (ACTION_REQUIRED) when merge conflicts are detected. No lock file is written on this path per Step 5 — conflict is a deliberate pause state, not a completed update, so the AFTER-lock-write rule does not apply to it.
  • failed is written when a task fails after the copy back of an update or an add and the files are kept: under --non-interactive, and when a terminal user chooses to keep them. The lock file is written on that path. A terminal user who undoes the run (Undo) appends no record, and the marker and the ref are removed.

Known limitation: The lock file write and migration record append are two separate atomic operations with no transactional guarantee across both. The restore marker is removed only after the record, so a crash between the lock and the record leaves the marker at phase recording, and the rerun appends the record (Interrupted copy back); a crash between the record and the marker's removal leaves a marker that rule 1 removes. The migration log is advisory, not authoritative.

Migration invariants:

  • Entries MUST be append-only and chronologically ordered by timestamp. Implementations MUST NOT reorder, delete, or rewrite prior entries.
  • On the update path, boilerplate.lock MUST be regenerated only after a successful update operation; the lock is the authoritative source of completed-update truth.
  • A failed update that stops before the copy back, or whose copy back fails and is undone, MUST leave the project in its pre-update state with no migration record. A failed MigrationRecord is written only when a task fails after the copy back, and it MUST itself be written atomically per §Atomic Staged Write Pattern.

docs.title: Corruption recovery
docs.text:
If migrations.yml cannot be parsed (malformed YAML, truncated file), implementations MUST:

  1. Log a WARNING with the parse error details.
  2. Treat the migration history as empty (zero entries).
  3. Continue the operation — the lock file is the authoritative state; the migration log is advisory.
  4. On the next successful operation that writes a migration record, the corrupted file is replaced with a new file containing only the latest entry.

Implementations MUST NOT abort an update operation solely because migrations.yml is corrupted.

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text: Scenario Expected Outcome --dry-run UpdatePlan printed, no files modified, exit 0 PATCH update, no local changes Files updated, new lock written, migration recorded, exit 0 MINOR update, local changes, no conflicts Local changes preserved, template deltas applied, exit 0 MAJOR update UpdatePlan flags MAJOR, requires explicit confirmation Merge conflict detected Layers finished so far brought back as uncommitted changes with Copier's conflict markers, no new lock written, migration record with conflict status, exit 4 Dirty working tree, untracked files included Error naming the uncommitted changes; no files modified, exit 3 Project with submodules BP_UPDATE_SUBMODULES_UNSUPPORTED naming the paths; no files modified, exit 3 User's checkout changed while the run worked in the staging worktree Worktree discarded, BP_UPDATE_CHECKOUT_CHANGED; no files modified, exit 3 Task fails after the copy back (--non-interactive) Files kept, lock written, failed task named with how to rerun it, failed migration record, exit 1 Recorded answer rejected by the target view's question type or validator (non-interactive) BP_INPUT_ANSWER_REJECTED naming the layer, question and recorded value; the update stops, no lock written, exit 3 Downgrade attempt Rejected before any layer changes, error names the layer, recorded version and target, exit 3 A layer and one of its ancestors both disagree with boilerplate.lock, with no pending conflict record BP_UPDATE_LAYER_DRIFT naming each layer's _commit and the lock's version, with the git revert remediation; no layer runs, no files modified, exit 3 A question of a layer's scoped view at the recorded versions, neither secret nor hidden, has no answer in the layer's own answers file or its declaring layer's BP_UPDATE_ANSWERS_INCOMPLETE naming the layer and the keys, with the git revert remediation; no layer runs, no files modified, exit 3 --target-version differs from the targets of the pending conflict record BP_UPDATE_TARGET_MISMATCH telling the user to set the partial update aside first; no layer runs, no files modified, exit 3 --target-version <layer>@<version> names a layer the lock does not list BP_UPDATE_LAYER_UNKNOWN naming each unknown layer and listing the project's layers; nothing staged, exit 3 --target-version <layer>@<version> names a version another lock layer's extends constraint excludes BP_UPDATE_TARGET_EXCLUDED naming the layer, the version and the constraining layer; nothing staged, exit 3 A layer add introduced, which the root's target version does not reach Stays in the lock, walks to its own target, is not reported as REMOVED A layer add introduced, which the root's target version reaches through extends Keeps joined_via: add, walks to its own target within the extends constraint, is not reported as ADDED or REMOVED Failure mid-update Staging worktree removed, checkout unchanged, no lock and no migration record, remediation guidance printed, exit 1 Copy back fails partway Copy back undone (Undo), worktree kept and named, marker and ref removed, no migration record, BP_UPDATE_COPY_BACK_FAILED, exit 1 Run cut off while copying back or finishing, working tree holds only what it wrote The same update again repeats the copy back, runs the tasks, writes the lock and appends success; exit 0 Run cut off, working tree edited since (a file at a path the run adds included, even one git ignores), or the run was paused by a conflict BP_UPDATE_INTERRUPTED naming the run's targets; nothing changed, exit 3

docs.title: Performance Contracts
docs.text: See Operational quality for all performance targets.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Adding a layer applies one more template to a project Boilerplate already manages and records it in boilerplate.lock. The result MUST equal what one more by-hand copier copy of the layer with its own answers file would produce: Copier's documented idiom for applying multiple templates to the same subproject, which is the reference point the composition answers to (ADR-015). The CLI contract is in 05-cli-reference.md §add.

docs.title: Preconditions
docs.text: The preconditions are the ones in 05-cli-reference.md §add, checked before any file changes, with the working tree check the same as the update Pre-Flight Check, whose operation lock and restore-marker rules run first. Each failure exits with code 3.

docs.title: Add pipeline
docs.text:
1. Resolve  →  Resolve the template and its extends
2. Ask      →  Ask the new layer's own questions
3. Answers  →  Take answers to ancestors' questions as update takes them
4. Render   →  Render the layer's scoped view with Copier's copy
5. Return   →  Bring the result back as uncommitted changes
6. Tasks    →  Run the new layer's tasks once
7. Lock     →  Write boilerplate.lock with the layer appended
8. Record   →  Append a migration record
  1. Resolve the template and its extends.
  2. Ask only the new layer's own questions, with defaults from the merged template of the project's layers plus the new one.
  3. Take answers to ancestors' questions the same way update takes them (design 04 §Safe Update).
  4. Render the layer's scoped view with Copier's copy, using the same staging as update (Staging worktree, Step 5: Failure and conflict).
  5. Bring the result back as uncommitted changes.
  6. Run the new layer's tasks once, as at compose, against the finished project, before the lock and the record as new and update run theirs. A task that fails is handled as for update (design 04 §Safe Update): keeping the files writes the lock and appends a failed record, and undoing (Undo) appends no record.
  7. Write boilerplate.lock with the new layer appended at the end of the lock's layer order and its joined_via set to add. A new layer has no descendants, so last is always valid.
  8. Append a migration record to .boilerplate/migrations.yml. The record carries no classification, as for created and adopted records: no prior version of the layer exists to compare.

The copy back, its failure handling and the restore marker are those of update (Staging worktree, Interrupted copy back), with the marker's operation set to add. The marker passes copy_back, tasks and recording as an update's does, so recovery rules 4, 5 and 6 apply to add unchanged.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: The new layer renders into the existing tree as the by-hand copy would. The new layer's _skip_if_exists applies, because Copier checks it before overwrite (Worker._solve_render_conflict, read at Copier 9.18.1): a file it lists that already exists keeps its content, and any other file another layer already rendered is overwritten and shows in the uncommitted diff, where the user reviews it before committing. new with the layer and add of the layer later can therefore differ for the listed files, because a composed new render ignores every layer's _skip_if_exists (04 §Per-Layer Render Loop) while in the add case the project already owns them. A template intended to be added later SHOULD render only files no other layer renders.

docs.title: Choices inside a layer
docs.text: A layer that offers alternatives (CI providers, docs site generators) SHOULD ask one choice question and render conditional paths: Copier skips any path whose rendered name is empty, so the unchosen alternatives render nothing. Changing the choice later is an answer change on update (--data), merged by Copier's update.

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text: Scenario Expected Outcome Layer added to a managed project with a clean tree Layer rendered as uncommitted changes, its tasks run, lock written with the layer last and joined_via: add, migration recorded, exit 0 Project not managed (boilerplate.lock missing) Error pointing to boilerplate adopt; no files modified, exit 3 Dirty working tree Error naming the uncommitted changes; no files modified, exit 3 Template already in the project Error pointing to boilerplate update; no files modified, exit 3 An ancestor the layer extends is not in the lock Error naming each missing layer with the remediation boilerplate add <ancestor> first; no files modified, exit 3 An ancestor's recorded version fails the layer's extends constraint Error naming the ancestor, its recorded version and the constraint, with the remediation boilerplate update first; no files modified, exit 3 Failure mid-add Staging worktree removed, checkout unchanged, no lock and no migration record, remediation guidance printed, exit 1 Task fails after the copy back (--non-interactive) Files kept, lock written with the layer, failed task named with how to rerun it, failed migration record, exit 1 Task fails after the copy back (terminal), user chooses to keep the files As under --non-interactive: lock written, failed record appended, exit 1 Task fails after the copy back (terminal), user chooses to undo Run undone (Undo), no record; marker and ref removed Run cut off while copying back, running the tasks, writing the lock or recording, working tree holds only what it wrote The same add again finishes the run: the tasks run if they had not finished, lock written, success record appended; exit 0 Run cut off, working tree edited since (a file at a path the layer adds included, even one git ignores) BP_UPDATE_INTERRUPTED naming the layer; nothing changed, exit 3

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Adoption bridges existing Copier-managed projects into Boilerplate lifecycle management. It creates the Boilerplate state files (boilerplate.lock, .boilerplate/migrations.yml) without modifying project files. After adoption, the project can use status, lock verify, and update as if it had been created with boilerplate new.

docs.title: Preconditions
docs.text:
Before adoption can proceed, all of the following MUST hold:

  • At least one Copier answers file MUST exist in the project directory (confirms the project is Copier-managed). Adoption accepts both Copier's default singular .copier-answers.yml (legacy projects without _answers_file:) and per-layer .copier-answers.<layer>.yml files (projects scaffolded from Boilerplate-enabled templates).
  • boilerplate.lock MUST NOT exist (the project is not already managed by Boilerplate). If it exists, fail with exit code 3: "Project already managed by Boilerplate. Use 'boilerplate update' instead."
  • The template referenced by the discovered answers file(s) MUST be resolvable in the catalog

docs.title: Adoption Pipeline
docs.text:
1. Read     →  Parse each `.copier-answers.*.yml` (or the legacy singular `.copier-answers.yml`) for template source and answers
2. Resolve  →  Resolve template in catalog; if boilerplate-enabled, resolve full extends chain
3. Checksum →  Compute template source checksums for each layer
4. Lock     →  Write boilerplate.lock (same schema as creation)
5. Init     →  Write .boilerplate/migrations.yml with initial "adopted" entry

Each pipeline step follows the same rules as creation: the per-layer copier_answers_file_hashes are computed the same way, checksums use the same algorithm, lock files use the same schema and Atomic Staged Write Pattern, and created_at/updated_at are both set to the current UTC timestamp. The migration record uses adopted (not success) as its status value, distinguishing adopted projects from created projects in the audit trail.

docs.title: What Is NOT Done
docs.text:
Adoption is a metadata-only operation. The following actions are explicitly not performed:

  • No files are rendered or written to the project directory (beyond the state files)
  • No template tasks are executed
  • No git operations are performed (no commits, no branching)
  • No environment provisioning is triggered
  • Copier answers files (whichever form the project uses — singular .copier-answers.yml or per-layer .copier-answers.<layer>.yml) are read but never modified

The project's existing files remain exactly as they were before adoption.

Adopted projects MAY use Copier's default singular .copier-answers.yml file. Adopted projects scaffolded by plain Copier (or by Boilerplate before per-layer files were the default) lack the per-layer _answers_file: contract (see 04 §Render Behavior). The boilerplate.lock.copier_answers_file_hashes mapping for an adopted single-layer project carries one entry, with the layer's template name as the key and the singular file's hash as the value.

docs.title: Copier-Only Templates
docs.text:
When the resolved template has no boilerplate.yml, it is a Copier-only template. Adoption still succeeds, but with reduced capabilities:

  • A minimal lock file is written with a single layer and no composition metadata (no extends chain)
  • The project can use status and lock verify to check template version and checksum integrity
  • The project cannot use composition features (compose, graph) because there is no boilerplate.yml defining the composition
  • update delegates entirely to Copier's single-template update mechanism

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text: Scenario Expected Outcome Valid Copier project, template in catalog boilerplate.lock and .boilerplate/migrations.yml written, exit 0 Project already has boilerplate.lock Rejected with "Project already managed by Boilerplate", exit 3 No Copier answers file found (neither singular .copier-answers.yml nor any .copier-answers.<layer>.yml) Rejected with "No Copier answers file found", exit 3 Template not found in catalog BP_RESOLVE_TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND, exit 1 Copier-only template (no boilerplate.yml) Minimal lock file written (single layer, no composition), exit 0

docs.title: Performance Contracts
docs.text:
See Operational quality for all performance targets.

Cross-reference: See CLI reference for the full adopt CLI specification.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Ejection is the exact inverse of adoption: it removes the Boilerplate-owned management state from a project, leaving every rendered file in place. After ejection, the directory is no longer Boilerplate-managed — update, status, and lock verify no longer apply — but it remains a usable plain Copier project (or plain files). Like adoption, ejection never modifies the project's rendered output.

docs.title: What Is Removed
docs.text:
Ejection deletes only Boilerplate-owned artifacts:

  • boilerplate.lock (if present).
  • The entire .boilerplate/ directory (project-domain migrations.yml, and the environment-domain environment.yml if present).

docs.title: What Is Kept
docs.text:
• The Copier answers files — per-layer .copier-answers.<layer>.yml, or the legacy singular .copier-answers.yml — are Copier-owned and left untouched. An ejected project can still be managed directly with copier update.
  • All rendered project files.
  • .prototools and any proto-installed tools. Ejection NEVER touches proto state. Tool teardown is proto's responsibility: the proto install store is shared across projects, so removing it on one project's behalf is unsafe. This mirrors the ownership boundary that adoption respects in the other direction — Boilerplate manages only the files it owns.

docs.title: Idempotency
docs.text: Ejection is a no-op only when NEITHER boilerplate.lock NOR .boilerplate/ is present: it warns and exits 0. Otherwise it removes whichever of the two exist — boilerplate.lock (if present) and the entire .boilerplate/ directory. The directory is checked independently because env apply can create .boilerplate/environment.yml with no lock present (an environment-only project); keying the no-op on boilerplate.lock alone would orphan that state. This makes ejection safe to run repeatedly and safe to script.

docs.title: Concurrency and Locking
docs.text: Ejection is a mutating operation and MUST acquire the standard advisory mutex on the project before removing state, under the universal rule in §Concurrency (same as new, update, add, adopt, and env apply). The lock target is the existing-project target under §Concurrency; for an environment-only project (no lock, only .boilerplate/) that is not a git repository, the mutex falls back to the new-style sentinel (.boilerplate-lock-{destination_name} in the project's parent directory).

docs.title: No Recovery Needed
docs.text: Ejection is a delete, not a staged write: there is no staging directory, no intent journal, and no backup to roll back or resume. Consequently it reuses none of update's merge or staging-worktree machinery. A user who ejects by mistake can re-adopt the project — adoption regenerates boilerplate.lock and .boilerplate/migrations.yml from the existing Copier answers files (see Part 2.5).

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
Scenario Expected Outcome Managed project (boilerplate.lock present) boilerplate.lock and .boilerplate/ removed; rendered files and .copier-answers.* kept; exit 0 Environment-only project (.boilerplate/ present, no boilerplate.lock) .boilerplate/ removed; rendered files and .copier-answers.* kept; exit 0 Neither boilerplate.lock nor .boilerplate/ present No-op: warning emitted, nothing removed, exit 0 --dry-run Removal list printed, nothing removed, exit 0 Filesystem/permission failure during removal BP_FILESYSTEM_PERMISSION, exit 1

Cross-reference: See CLI reference for the full eject CLI specification.

docs.title: Part 3: Artifact Fetching
docs.text:
For remote templates (not local directories), the system MUST:

  1. Fetch template artifacts from remote git hosting services (e.g., GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket)
  2. Cache fetched artifacts locally with SHA-256 integrity validation
  3. Initialize git submodules before any YAML parsing
  4. Retry transient network failures with exponential backoff (max 3 attempts by default)
  5. Detect and report missing or broken submodule references with recovery suggestions

Caching: Templates fetched from remote repositories MUST be cached by their checksum. Subsequent operations with the same checksum MUST use the cached artifact without re-fetching.

Retry policy: See Operational quality for the full retry specification.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Cross-cutting operational quality controls that apply to every feature slice: stable error codes, error attribution, structured logging, performance contracts, retry policy, the Atomic Staged Write Pattern, concurrency control, and platform portability. The security model itself lives in Security model.

docs.title: Design Principles
docs.text:
1. Error codes MUST be stable once published — from 1.0. During 0.x (pre-release; see Versioning & Compatibility) codes MAY still change as the surface settles, and the rename to the BP_{PHASE}_{DESCRIPTOR} scheme is pre-1.0 hygiene, not a frozen contract. From 1.0, a published code MUST NOT change its meaning.
  2. Each code MUST map to exactly one root cause.
  3. Each code MUST carry: phase, severity, retryable flag, and remediation guidance.
  4. Codes MUST NOT leak sensitive internal details.

docs.title: Code Namespace
docs.text:
All error codes use the prefix BP_ followed by the phase and a short descriptor:

BP_{PHASE}_{DESCRIPTOR}

docs.title: Phase Prefixes
docs.text:
Phase prefix Scope BP_RESOLVE_ Template resolution and dependency traversal BP_VERSION_ Version parsing and constraint evaluation BP_GRAPH_ Dependency graph building and validation BP_LOCK_ Lock file reading, writing, and validation BP_RENDER_ Template rendering and staging BP_INPUT_ User input validation BP_CONFIG_ Configuration loading BP_FETCH_ Remote template fetching (network, authentication) BP_GIT_ Git binary availability and Git command failures BP_ENV_ Environment provisioning (env apply command group) BP_CONCURRENCY_ Operation-level concurrency control: advisory-lock acquisition and mutex contention. Distinct from BP_LOCK_, which is content-level operations on the lock file artifact. BP_FILESYSTEM_ Local filesystem failures (permission denial, path-length limits) raised by Boilerplate's I/O routines independent of pipeline stage. Example: BP_FILESYSTEM_PERMISSION. BP_BUNDLE_ Integrity verification for archive and wheel-bundle template sources (archive extraction failures, checksum mismatches). Example: BP_BUNDLE_CHECKSUM_FAILED. The prefix covers all non-Git archive-based sources. BP_UPDATE_ The update walk and adding a layer: drift between the lock and the answers files, an incomplete answers file, a resume whose targets differ from the paused update's, a resolved source that diverges from the lock (BP_UPDATE_SOURCE_DIVERGED, 10 §Verification Pipeline), staging preconditions, and a task that fails after the copy back. Example: BP_UPDATE_LAYER_DRIFT. BP_COPIER_ Copier-engine compatibility failures (version mismatch, unsupported Copier feature). Example: BP_COPIER_COMPAT_FAILED.

Mapping to pipeline stages: Error code phases are orthogonal to the operational pipeline stages defined in Project lifecycle. The creation pipeline stages (Resolve → Compose → Render → Lock → Init) may trigger errors from multiple phases: the Resolve stage may produce BP_RESOLVE_*, BP_VERSION_*, or BP_GRAPH_* errors; the Render stage may produce BP_RENDER_* or BP_GIT_* errors; the Lock stage may produce BP_LOCK_* errors. Error code phases group errors by their root cause domain, not by the pipeline stage in which they occur.

docs.title: Error Code Registry
docs.text:
When new error conditions are identified during implementation, they MUST be added to the relevant design document before being implemented. Each phase prefix has a set of error codes following the principles above. Registered codes and representative examples illustrating the pattern:

Code Severity Retryable Description BP_RESOLVE_TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND error no Template reference cannot be found in the catalog BP_RESOLVE_DEP_NOT_FOUND error no A template referenced in extends cannot be found in the catalog. Attribution: Template Author BP_RESOLVE_MERGE_CONFLICT error no Two layers declare incompatible values for the same configuration key. Exit code 1. Attribution: Template Author BP_RESOLVE_METADATA_INVALID error no Template metadata (boilerplate.yml) is malformed, missing required fields, or inconsistent. Exit code 3. Attribution: Template Author BP_RESOLVE_VERSION_CONFLICT error no Diamond dependency at incompatible versions. Attribution: Template Author BP_RESOLVE_PROFILE_MISSING error no Template's requires_profile is not satisfied: the named profile is absent from the project's environment state, or its version does not satisfy the profile-version constraint. Exit code 3. Attribution: User / Template Author BP_VERSION_INVALID error no A version string is not PEP 440 compliant. Exit code 3. Attribution: User BP_GRAPH_CYCLE error no The template dependency graph contains a cycle. Exit code 1. Attribution: Template Author BP_LOCK_READ_FAILED error no boilerplate.lock cannot be read as a lock file: unparseable YAML, a truncated write or a body that does not match the schema. Boilerplate does not repair it; the message gives the recreate remediation (06 §Lock File Recovery). Attribution: User BP_LOCK_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED error no Lock file's schema_version major exceeds the major supported by the running tool (the project was created by a newer Boilerplate). Fail closed; do not read or mutate. Attribution: User BP_RENDER_STAGING_FAILED error yes Rendering failed during staging; staging was cleaned up BP_RENDER_UNSAFE_EXTENSION error no A Jinja2 extension is not on the allowed list. Attribution: User / Template Author BP_RENDER_DEST_NOT_EMPTY error no The render destination exists and is non-empty, and --force was not provided. Exit code 3. Attribution: User BP_RENDER_PROMPT_FAILED error no Copier's prompt machinery failed because the environment cannot host interactive prompts. Exit code 1. Attribution: System BP_RENDER_USER_CANCELLED error no The user cancelled an interactive prompt (e.g. Ctrl+C). Exit code 130. Attribution: User BP_INPUT_SPECIFIER_INVALID error no A template specifier (name@version) fails name or version validation. Exit code 3. Attribution: User BP_INPUT_FORCE_REQUIRED error no A multi-layer render in non-interactive mode requires --force. Exit code 3. Attribution: User BP_INPUT_ANSWERS_MISSING error no Non-interactive render cannot proceed: required questions have no default and no supplied answer. Exit code 3. Attribution: User / Template Author BP_INPUT_ANSWER_REJECTED error no update cannot proceed: a recorded answer fails the target view's question type, choices or validator (a retyped question or a tightened validator). The check runs inside the layer's step, after its migrations and Copier's re-read of the answers file, so a migration that repairs the answer clears it first; the message names the layer, the question and the recorded value (04 §Safe Update). A value for the question supplied by --data or --data-file replaces the recorded answer, so the check applies only to a recorded answer nothing replaces; the message names the remediation --data <question>=<value>. In a terminal, the question's prompt shows why the answer is rejected and asks for a valid one. Exit code 3. Attribution: User / Template Author BP_INPUT_TTY_REQUIRED error no Interactive render requested but stdin is not a TTY, so prompts can never be answered. Exit code 3. Attribution: User BP_INPUT_DEST_REQUIRED error no Non-interactive render names no destination; the current directory is never assumed. Exit code 3. Attribution: User BP_INPUT_DATA_INVALID error no --data/--data-file input fails validation: a malformed or empty --data key, an underscore-prefixed (Copier-reserved) --data key (the same key in a --data-file is skipped with a warning), an unreadable or non-UTF-8 --data-file, invalid YAML, a non-mapping document, or a non-string YAML key. Exit code 3. Attribution: User BP_UPDATE_TASK_FAILED error no A task failed after the update's files were copied back. Under --non-interactive the update keeps the files, writes the lock, and names the failed task and how to rerun it (04 §Safe Update). Exit code 1. Attribution: Template Author BP_UPDATE_ANSWERS_INCOMPLETE error no update found, before any layer ran, a question of a layer's scoped view at the recorded versions that is neither secret nor hidden (04 §Safe Update defines hidden) that neither the layer's own answers file nor its declaring layer's file records, so the walk has no answer to fill the old copy with. The message lists the layer and the keys and the remediation: undo the hand-run update that trimmed the file, with git revert of the commit that holds it, then run boilerplate update again (04 §Safe Update); doctor reports a trimmed file and any key no layer records. Exit code 3. Attribution: User BP_UPDATE_LAYER_DRIFT error no update found, before any layer ran and with no pending conflict record to resume, a layer and one of its ancestors that both disagree with boilerplate.lock. The message names each layer's _commit and the lock's version, and the remediation: undo the hand-run updates with git revert of the commits that hold them, then run update again (04 §Safe Update). Exit code 3. Attribution: User BP_UPDATE_TARGET_MISMATCH error no An explicit --target-version differs from the targets the pending conflict record names. The message tells the user to set the partial update aside first, with git revert of the commit that holds it, and run update again (04 §Safe Update). Exit code 3. Attribution: User BP_UPDATE_LAYER_UNKNOWN error no update was given a target (--target-version <layer>@<version>) for a layer the project's boilerplate.lock does not list. Nothing is staged. The message names the unknown layers, and the remediation lists the project's layers (06 §Step 2; 05 §update). Exit code 3. Attribution: User BP_UPDATE_TARGET_EXCLUDED error no update was given an explicit --target-version <layer>@<version> that the extends constraint of another layer in the project's boilerplate.lock excludes. Nothing is staged. The message names the layer, the requested version and the constraining layer (06 §Step 2). Exit code 3. Attribution: User BP_UPDATE_CONFLICT_PAUSED error no A layer's update left merge conflicts, so update stopped the walk. The layers finished so far are in the working tree with Copier's conflict markers, no lock is written, and a conflict record is appended. The message lists each conflicted file path and its originating layer, and the remediation: resolve the conflicts and commit, then run boilerplate update again, or set the partial update aside (06 §Setting a partial update aside). Exit code 4. Attribution: User BP_UPDATE_DOWNGRADE_REJECTED error no update found, before any layer changed, a target older than the version a layer's answers file records in _commit, or a recorded _commit that yields no version. There is no override; the message names the layer, its recorded version and the target (06 §Step 2: Resolve Target). Exit code 3. Attribution: User BP_UPDATE_PROJECT_NOT_READY error no update or add found that the project is not a git repository root with at least one commit, or that its working tree has uncommitted changes, untracked files included (Copier's own rule: git status --porcelain is not empty). The staging worktree is not created (06 §Pre-Flight Check). Exit code 3. Attribution: User BP_UPDATE_PATH_OBSTRUCTED error no Before the copy back, a path the walk added already exists in the checkout as a file or directory git ignores. The checkout is unchanged; the message names each path (06 §Staging worktree). Exit code 3. Attribution: User BP_UPDATE_INTERRUPTED error no The restore marker shows that an earlier update or add was cut off while restoring its result into the working tree, and the rerun cannot finish it: the marker's operation differs from the command, HEAD is not the run's starting commit, the working tree differs from the run's result (a file at a path the run adds counts, even one git ignores), or a conflict had paused the run, or the marker file does not parse. The message says the run was cut off while restoring its result into the working tree, names the run's targets, and gives the remediation to set the partial update aside (06 §Setting a partial update aside) and then run the command again; for a different operation it names the command to rerun (06 §Interrupted copy back, rules 3 and 4 and the unparseable-marker stop). Exit code 3. Attribution: User BP_UPDATE_COPY_BACK_FAILED error no Copying the staging worktree back into the checkout failed partway. The copy back is undone (06 §Undo), the staging worktree is kept and the message names its path so the walk's result is not lost, and the restore marker and its ref are removed. No migration record is appended (06 §Staging worktree). Exit code 1. Attribution: System BP_UPDATE_PROJECT_NOT_MANAGED error no add found no boilerplate.lock in the project. Nothing is staged, and the message itself says to use boilerplate adopt (05 §add). Exit code 3. Attribution: User BP_UPDATE_LAYER_ALREADY_ADDED error no add named a template the project's lock already lists. The message itself says to use boilerplate update (05 §add). Exit code 3. Attribution: User BP_UPDATE_ANCESTORS_MISSING error no add found that a template the new layer extends, directly or transitively, is not in the lock. The message names each missing layer, and the remediation is boilerplate add <ancestor> first (05 §add). Exit code 3. Attribution: User BP_UPDATE_ANCESTOR_VERSION_MISMATCH error no add found an ancestor whose recorded version fails the new layer's extends constraint. The message names the ancestor, its recorded version and the constraint, and the remediation is boilerplate update first (05 §add). Exit code 3. Attribution: User BP_UPDATE_SUBMODULES_UNSUPPORTED error no update or add found a .gitmodules file in the project. The staging worktree is not created, and the message names the submodule paths (06 §Pre-Flight Check). Exit code 3. Attribution: User BP_UPDATE_CHECKOUT_CHANGED error no The user's checkout changed after the staging worktree was created, so the copy back would overwrite work. The worktree is discarded and nothing is written (06 §Staging worktree). Exit code 3. Attribution: User BP_CONFIG_DIR_INVALID error no A required directory path is missing, not a directory, or otherwise invalid. Exit code 2. Attribution: User BP_CONFIG_PROFILE_INVALID error no profile.toml exists but is not valid TOML, or a reserved section is not a table. Exit code 1. Attribution: User BP_CONCURRENCY_CONTENTION error yes Another Boilerplate process may be operating on the same project BP_FETCH_NETWORK_FAILED error yes Network error when fetching a remote template source BP_GIT_AUTH_FAILED error no Git authentication failed. Attribution: Git BP_ENV_APPLY_FAILED error yes Environment provisioning failed. Attribution: Boilerplate / proto BP_FILESYSTEM_PERMISSION error no Insufficient filesystem permissions. Attribution: System

Each error code carries severity, retryable flag, a human-readable description, remediation guidance, and attribution. The registry grows as new failure modes are identified, but published codes are immutable from 1.0 (see Design Principle 1). Domain-specific codes are documented in their owning specification (e.g., BP_ENV_* in §08 Environment Provisioning).

docs.title: Error Message Format
docs.text:
Every error emitted to the user MUST include the following components, presented in inverted pyramid order (most actionable first):

  1. Error description: A concise, human-readable Error: ... line with the BP_* code as a bracketed suffix
  2. Reason: The root cause or context (indented below)
  3. Fix: A concrete, actionable remediation step (indented, labeled "Fix:")
  4. Code: The stable BP_* code (shown as suffix on the Error line)
  5. Attribution: Which component owns the failure — shown only in --verbose mode
  6. Exit code: Shown only in --verbose mode

For interactive (TTY) output, error messages MUST use the inverted pyramid pattern — lead with the human-readable description, promote the fix, demote metadata:

Error: Render failed while processing template "streamlit-app".   [BP_RENDER_TEMPLATE_FAILURE]
  Missing include file _base/project/copier.yml.
  Fix: git submodule update --init --recursive

For verbose mode (--verbose), the full diagnostic format is shown:

Error: Render failed while processing template "streamlit-app".   [BP_RENDER_TEMPLATE_FAILURE]
  Missing include file _base/project/copier.yml.
  Fix: git submodule update --init --recursive
  Attribution: YAML
  Exit code: 1

For JSON output (--format json), all fields are included in the JSON error object.

Multi-step remediation. When the fix requires more than one action, the Fix: line MAY expand into a multi-line block introduced by → arrows:

Error: Template not found in catalog: pyhton-web   [BP_RESOLVE_TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND]
  Searched catalogs: official, community.
  Did you mean 'python-web' (92% match)?
  Fix:
    → boilerplate catalog sync
    → boilerplate new python-web

Each arrow is a discrete remediation step. The arrow prefix is reserved for remediation-step lines; other guidance uses normal indentation.

docs.title: Error Attribution
docs.text:
Attribution Meaning Boilerplate The failure is in Boilerplate's own logic Copier Copier reported a rendering or task error Git A git operation failed YAML YAML parsing or include resolution failed User The error is due to invalid user input Network A remote operation failed due to connectivity System A required system dependency is missing or misconfigured proto The proto toolchain manager reported an error Template Author The error is due to a defect in template configuration

Attribution decision rules for boundary cases:

  • Copier fails due to invalid Jinja2 in a template → Template Author (the template has a syntax error)
  • Copier fails due to an internal bug → Copier (Boilerplate has no control over Copier internals)
  • Git authentication fails → User if credentials are misconfigured; Network if the server is unreachable
  • Template declares an invalid _min_copier_version → Template Author (the template metadata is wrong)
  • Lock file checksum mismatch → System (disk corruption or external modification)

When multiple parties are involved, attribute to the root cause — the party whose action or configuration caused the failure, not the component that reported it.

docs.title: Logging Levels
docs.text: Level When to use ERROR Operation failed; user action required WARNING Non-fatal issue the user should know about INFO Normal progress and completion events DEBUG Detailed diagnostic information (enabled by --verbose)

docs.title: Required Log Fields
docs.text:
Every structured log event MUST include: the operation phase, the specific operation, the template being processed (if applicable), a correlation ID (request_id), success/failure status, duration, and the BP_* error code on failure.

Task execution events MUST additionally include the command executed, the source template, execution order, exit code, and duration. Task stdout and stderr MUST be captured and logged at DEBUG level to enable post-incident investigation of what tasks ran and which template authored them.

Privacy invariants: - Logs MUST NOT contain secrets, passwords, API tokens, or PII - Personal data MUST be redacted before emission - Only structural identifiers (template names, versions, paths) are permitted

docs.title: Redaction
docs.text: Log redaction MUST be systematic rather than per-log-statement. A centralized redaction mechanism MUST scrub sensitive patterns (credentials, tokens, URL userinfo) from all log output, including captured subprocess output, before emission. Sensitive values MUST use a type that refuses to serialize to string representations, preventing accidental leakage.

docs.title: Log Output
docs.text:
Terminal: When stderr is a TTY and NO_COLOR is not set, use rich-formatted output with colors and structured layout. Non-TTY stderr receives a single JSON object per log event.

Structured output: All machine-readable log output is emitted as JSON to stderr. Logging is stderr-only by design — no file-based logging, rotation, or external aggregation. Consumers that need persistence may redirect stderr.

Correlation ID passthrough: When BOILERPLATE_REQUEST_ID is set in the environment, its value MUST be used as the correlation ID for all log entries in that invocation, overriding any auto-generated ID. This enables parent service correlation in pipeline and orchestration contexts.

docs.title: Subprocess Correlation
docs.text:
The per-invocation request_id MUST be propagated to all subprocesses as the environment variable BOILERPLATE_REQUEST_ID. When BOILERPLATE_REQUEST_ID is already set in the environment (e.g., by a parent orchestration process), Boilerplate MUST use the provided value rather than generating a new one. This enables correlation with parent process traces and distributed tracing systems. While external tools (Copier, Git, proto) do not consume this variable, it enables:

  • Correlation of Boilerplate's structured logs with subprocess output captured at DEBUG level
  • External log aggregation systems to group all activity from a single Boilerplate invocation

All subprocess stdout and stderr MUST be captured and logged at DEBUG level with the request_id and phase fields attached.

docs.title: Phase Vocabulary
docs.text: The phase log field uses a closed enum aligned with the operation pipeline: resolve, fetch, render, update, lock, catalog, env_apply, plus internal for events outside any pipeline phase (bootstrap, configuration loading, third-party library records). Implementations MUST NOT emit phase values outside this set without first extending the enum here. This pipeline-phase vocabulary is distinct from the error-code phase prefixes defined above.

docs.title: Logging Invariants
docs.text:
• There MUST be exactly one terminal log event per high-level request (success or failure). Step-level events MAY occur en route, but the terminal event is the canonical record.
  • Every terminal log event with success: false MUST carry a BP_* error_code field. No anonymous failures.
  • duration_ms MUST appear only on the terminal log event, never on step events.

docs.title: Performance Contracts
docs.text:
Invariants:

  • DX commands (status, validate, shell completions) MUST complete within 500ms on a developer machine with a local catalog of up to 200 templates.
  • Long-running operations MUST show progress feedback.
  • Algorithmic complexity MUST be linear in the size of the template graph.

docs.title: Retry Policy
docs.text:
Only errors marked retryable: true in the error code registry MAY be retried. Non-retryable errors (validation failures, not-found, cycles, conflicts) MUST fail immediately.

Retryable errors use exponential backoff with jitter. Between retry attempts, the staging directory MUST be completely removed and recreated to prevent corrupted results from partial output.

Default parameters:

Parameter Value Description Base delay 1 second Initial delay before first retry Maximum delay 30 seconds Cap on exponential growth Maximum attempts 3 Total attempts including the initial try Jitter Full jitter Random value between 0 and the computed delay (delay = random(0, min(max_delay, base * 2^attempt)))

These defaults apply to all retryable operations (network fetches, transient subprocess failures). Individual operations MAY override max_attempts via configuration but MUST NOT disable jitter.

Transient vs. deterministic classification: Rendering failures (BP_RENDER_TEMPLATE_FAILURE) are retryable only for transient causes (subprocess timeout, OOM kill). Deterministic failures (Jinja2 syntax errors, missing variables) MUST fail immediately. Implementations MUST classify the error before deciding retryability.

docs.title: Network Timeouts
docs.text: All network operations MUST enforce a configurable timeout to prevent an operation from waiting indefinitely on unresponsive servers. Network timeouts and rendering timeouts are independent and independently configurable.

docs.title: Security Model
docs.text: The full security model lives in Security model. Operational invariants that gate the security checks (atomic-write pattern, concurrency control, retry policy, redaction mechanism, structured logging) remain in this document; the security rules cite them where needed.

docs.title: Atomic Staged Write Pattern
docs.text:
Both project creation (§06) and environment provisioning (§08) follow the same staged-write-with-intent-journal pattern. This section defines the shared invariants; each feature documents its specific file names, phase values, and recovery procedures.

Core invariant: All destructive operations follow a stage → validate → commit sequence. Work is performed in an isolated staging directory. An intent journal tracks the current phase for crash recovery. On success, staged output is atomically moved into place and the journal is deleted. On failure or interruption, the staging directory is cleaned up and the project directory is left in its pre-operation state. For update and add the commit step is the copy back, which is not atomic: a copy back that fails is undone (06 §Undo), and one cut off midway is finished or set aside as the restore marker directs (06 §Interrupted copy back).

Stale cleanup: Before creating a new staging directory, stale staging directories (older than 1 hour; see Project lifecycle) from previous interrupted operations are detected and cleaned up. For update and add, whose staging directory holds a git worktree (06 §Staging worktree), the cleanup removes only worktrees Boilerplate created, identified by the journal and the owner check, and then runs git worktree prune in the project the journal's destination names, which drops the registration of a worktree whose folder is gone. A staging folder is stale only when it is older than the window and no running operation holds the exclusive lock each operation takes on its journal for the operation's lifetime: age alone would remove an update that is waiting at a prompt. git worktree prune runs only in this cleanup, never when an operation removes its own worktree, so the user's own worktree registrations are left alone.

Intent journal invariants:

  • Written atomically and updated before each phase transition.
  • Deleted on successful completion.
  • If present but unparseable after a crash: left for user inspection without automated recovery.

Restore marker: For update and add, the state of a copy back cut off midway is kept in a restore marker in the project's git directory, not in the staging folder and not in the intent journal, so it outlives the stale cleanup. It is written and rewritten with the single-file invocation below (06 §Interrupted copy back).

Signal handling: Process termination signals MUST trigger the same cleanup as a failure. Untrappable signals are handled by stale cleanup and journal recovery on the next invocation.

Retry behavior: On retry, the previous attempt's staging directory and intent journal are cleaned up before creating a new staging directory.

Single-file invocation: When the staged unit is a single append-only file rather than a directory tree, the same stage → validate → commit principle applies via tmp-then-rename: read existing content, construct the updated content in memory, write to a sibling temporary file (<filename>.tmp.{random_suffix}) in the same directory, then atomically rename it to the target name. This prevents a crash during write from leaving a truncated file. Used by .boilerplate/migrations.yml and similar single-file audit logs.

docs.title: Concurrency Control
docs.text: Boilerplate does not support concurrent mutating operations on the same target. Before any mutating operation, Boilerplate MUST acquire a platform-native advisory file lock (POSIX fcntl/flock; Windows LockFileEx) with a configurable timeout (default: 60 seconds, BOILERPLATE_LOCK_TIMEOUT). If the lock cannot be acquired, fail with BP_CONCURRENCY_CONTENTION. The lock is held for the duration of the operation and MUST be released when the operation completes or the holding process exits (the OS releases advisory file locks on process termination). On POSIX, ownership means the lock file's UID matches the effective UID. On Windows, ACL-based ownership applies.

docs.title: Platform Portability
docs.text: Cross-cutting platform constraints that apply across all Boilerplate operations.

docs.title: Path Limits (Windows)
docs.text: Boilerplate MUST fail fast before rendering if any rendered file path would exceed the Windows path limit and long paths are not enabled. boilerplate doctor MUST check this setting.

docs.title: Filesystem Differences
docs.text:
• Line endings: first-party templates carry a .gitattributes with * text=auto eol=lf, and third-party templates should (03 §Template Authoring Constraints). boilerplate doctor SHOULD validate that the file is present and declares it.
  • Git submodule paths can be problematic on NTFS. Submodule initialization failures MUST produce clear errors with remediation (see Project lifecycle).

docs.title: Network Filesystems
docs.text: Advisory file locking is unreliable on network filesystems. boilerplate doctor MUST detect network filesystems and warn. Staging directories SHOULD be created on local storage when possible.

docs.title: WSL2 Cross-Filesystem Access
docs.text: Accessing Windows filesystems from WSL2 incurs significant I/O overhead. Template sources and project directories on the native WSL2 filesystem perform significantly better.

docs.title: Environment Variables (Windows)
docs.text: Windows treats environment variables as case-insensitive. This cannot be enforced for BOILERPLATE_-prefixed variables on Windows.

docs.title: Exit Code Reference
docs.text: Exit codes are defined in Data models. An implementer MUST use those codes exactly -- no custom codes beyond those defined in §02.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: boilerplate env apply and boilerplate env status: resolving the EnvironmentProfile extends chain, merging tool versions and packages across profile layers, generating .prototools in proto's native format, invoking proto for tool installation, and writing the .boilerplate/environment.yml provenance record.

docs.title: State Files
docs.text:
A Boilerplate-managed environment contains the following state files after a successful env apply:

File Owner Purpose .prototools Boilerplate (generated) / proto (runtime) Declares resolved tool versions for proto; generated by Boilerplate from the merged profile .protolock proto Records exact resolved tool versions and checksums; written by proto after install .boilerplate/environment.yml Boilerplate Records which profile was applied, the resolved extends chain, and a hash of .protolock

Ownership invariants: - Boilerplate MUST NOT write to .protolock. That file is owned by proto. - External tools MUST NOT write to .boilerplate/environment.yml. That file is owned by Boilerplate. - .boilerplate/environment.yml MUST only be written after a fully successful provisioning operation. It MUST never reflect a partial state. - boilerplate-env.yml is the declarative input owned by the profile author. Boilerplate reads it; it MUST NOT be modified during provisioning.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Profile resolution transforms the root EnvironmentProfile and its extends chain into a flat, ordered list of profiles and a single merged tool version map ready for .prototools generation.

docs.title: Resolution Algorithm
docs.text:
Resolution takes the root profile specifier and a catalog as inputs, and produces a flat, ordered list of profiles (base-first, derived-last) as output. The algorithm performs a depth-first traversal of the extends chain, resolving each profile from the catalog.

Inputs: Root profile specifier, profile catalog.

Output: Ordered profile chain (base-first, derived-last; root profile always last).

Invariants:

  • Cycle detection: A cycle in the extends chain MUST be detected and reported as BP_ENV_EXTENDS_CYCLE with the full cycle path (e.g., base -> python -> base).
  • Diamond deduplication: A profile reachable via multiple paths is included once, at the position first encountered during traversal.
  • Missing profiles: If the root profile cannot be found, fail with BP_ENV_PROFILE_NOT_FOUND. If a parent in the extends chain cannot be found, fail with BP_ENV_EXTENDS_NOT_FOUND.
  • Determinism: Given the same profile definitions, the resolved chain MUST always be identical. Traversal order is determined by the extends declaration order in each profile. This parallels the template composition tie-breaking rule in §04 Composition Engine.

docs.title: Tool Version Merging
docs.text:
After the profile chain is resolved, tool versions are merged across all layers using a last-writer-wins policy: the chain is walked base-first, and each profile's tool declarations overwrite earlier values for the same tool name. The most-derived profile (last in topological order) wins for any given tool.

This is simpler than template composition's four named merge strategies (see §04) because tool versions are simple scalars, not the complex nested structures that template configurations contain.

The result is a flat {tool_name: version_string} map covering every tool declared in any profile in the chain.

docs.title: packages Field Merging
docs.text:
After tool version merging, the packages field (map of platform key to list of PackageRequirement) is merged across the extends chain:

  • For each platform key, PackageRequirement lists are accumulated in topological order (base first, derived last).
  • When multiple profiles declare the same package (by name) for the same platform, the last-writer-wins: the most-derived profile's version constraint replaces earlier entries for that package name.
  • The result is a flat {platform: [PackageRequirement, ...]} map. Platform keys not present in a profile are inherited unchanged from ancestor profiles.
  • Tools with version constraints (e.g., >=3.10) that cannot be resolved to a single exact version MUST cause BP_ENV_VERSION_UNRESOLVABLE. Constraint-only entries are not valid for .prototools generation. Implementations SHOULD emit a descriptive error: "Profile '{name}' declares tool '{tool}' with version constraint '{constraint}' which cannot be resolved to an exact version. Declare an exact version for provisioning."

docs.title: allowed_proto_plugins Enforcement
docs.text:
After tool version merging, the combined allowlist is computed by intersecting all non-empty allowed_proto_plugins lists across the chain.

Enforcement rules: - An empty allowed_proto_plugins list on a profile means no restriction from that layer — not "block all tools." - If ALL profiles in the chain have an empty allowed_proto_plugins (the default), the combined allowlist is empty, meaning no restriction applies and all resolved tools are permitted. - If ANY profile in the chain declares a non-empty allowed_proto_plugins, the combined allowlist is the intersection of all non-empty lists across the chain. This ensures that a base profile's allowlist acts as a ceiling — derived profiles can only narrow the set, never expand it. - After computing the combined allowlist: for each tool in the resolved tool map, if the combined allowlist is non-empty and the tool name does NOT appear in the combined allowlist, raise BP_ENV_PLUGIN_NOT_ALLOWED. - Error message MUST identify the disallowed tool, the requesting profile, and the restricting profile: "Tool '{tool}' is not in the allowed_proto_plugins intersection. Requested by profile '{requesting_profile}'. Not present in allowlist defined by profile '{restricting_profile}'. Contact the platform team to update the base allowlist."

Note (non-normative): intersection is a ceiling, not a floor — derived profiles can only narrow the allowlist, never expand it (expansion would be privilege escalation through profile composition). A tool absent from the base allowlist requires the platform team to update the base profile.

Trust model scope: Environment profiles do not use the template trust gate (trusted/untrusted) because the security surface differs. Template tasks execute arbitrary shell commands gated by trust. Proto plugins execute in a WASM sandbox with constrained host access. The allowed_proto_plugins intersection mechanism is the security control for profiles — it provides an equivalent ceiling guarantee (base profiles restrict derived profiles) without requiring task-trust classification.

docs.title: Part 2: .prototools Generation
docs.text: Boilerplate generates proto's native configuration file (.prototools) from the merged tool version map. The generated file is written to the project root.

docs.title: Generation Rules
docs.text:
• Only tools with resolved exact versions are included. Unresolvable versions MUST have already caused BP_ENV_VERSION_UNRESOLVABLE during the merge step.
  • Tool entries MUST be sorted lexicographically by name for deterministic output and clean diffs.
  • Path values MUST use forward slashes on all platforms for cross-platform compatibility.

docs.title: Ownership and Versioning
docs.text:
• .prototools is a generated output owned by Boilerplate in the provisioning context; boilerplate-env.yml is the declarative input.
  • .prototools MAY be committed to version control as a development convenience -- proto reads it at runtime to determine which tool versions to activate.
  • The output is reproducible: re-running boilerplate env apply with the same profile produces an identical .prototools.
  • Entries added manually to .prototools outside of Boilerplate are not tracked and will be overwritten on the next env apply.

docs.title: Proto Binary Discovery
docs.text:
• proto MUST be discoverable via PATH.
  • boilerplate doctor MUST verify proto is installed and emit an actionable message if not found.
  • If proto is not found during env apply, the operation MUST fail immediately with BP_ENV_PROTO_NOT_FOUND before any staging or I/O occurs.

docs.title: ProtoWorker Interface
docs.text:
The ProtoWorker abstracts proto's CLI behind a stable contract owned by Boilerplate. Implementations MUST isolate all proto invocations behind this interface so that proto version upgrades require changes only in the worker implementation.

install_tool(tool_name, version, timeout) → InstallResult

Parameter Type Description tool_name string Tool identifier (e.g., python, node) version string Exact version to install timeout integer Maximum seconds for this installation

InstallResult:

Field Type Description success boolean Whether installation completed tool_name string The tool that was installed version string The exact version installed error string or null Error message on failure

trigger_proto_lockfile() → path

Invokes proto's native lockfile generation (proto writes .protolock; Boilerplate does NOT) and returns the path to the resulting file. The method exists so the worker can report the lockfile path to caller code that needs to compute proto_lock_hash for the EnvironmentProvisionRecord. The worker MUST NOT itself write or modify .protolock.

Behavioral contracts:

  • The worker MUST NOT modify .prototools — that file is generated by Boilerplate and consumed by proto.
  • If install_tool fails, the error message MUST identify the specific tool and version.
  • Proto availability MUST be verified before any installation attempt; if proto is not found, fail with BP_ENV_PROTO_NOT_FOUND.

docs.title: Invocation
docs.text: Boilerplate invokes proto to install the resolved tools. All resolved tools MUST be installed before the commit phase proceeds. Implementations SHOULD invoke proto per-tool for granular error attribution. Bulk invocation MAY be used when per-tool invocation is impractical, but the error message MUST still identify the specific tool and version that failed.

docs.title: Timeout
docs.text: Proto installation is subject to a configurable timeout, independent of the rendering timeout. Proto installation is network-bound (downloading tool binaries), so the timeout must accommodate cold-cache downloads of large toolchains.

docs.title: Failure Handling
docs.text:
• If any proto install invocation fails, the provisioning MUST fail with BP_ENV_APPLY_FAILED.
  • The proto error output MUST be included in the structured log.
  • The human-readable error message MUST identify the specific tool and version that failed.

docs.title: .protolock Relationship
docs.text:
proto writes .protolock to the project root after successful installation, recording exact tool versions, checksums, and platform metadata.

Ownership boundaries: - Boilerplate MUST NOT write, modify, or delete .protolock. It is owned by proto. - Boilerplate reads .protolock after a successful install to compute the proto_lock_hash field for .boilerplate/environment.yml. - If proto did not write .protolock, proto_lock_hash is null. - boilerplate env status reads both .boilerplate/environment.yml and .protolock to report the current environment state.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: After profile resolution and tool version merging, the merged packages map is evaluated for the current platform. This section specifies how declared PackageRequirement entries are handled during env apply and related commands.

docs.title: Platform Detection
docs.text: Boilerplate detects the current platform (Windows, WSL2, Linux, macOS) and evaluates only packages declared for that platform. Packages for other platforms are silently ignored.

docs.title: Behavior During env apply
docs.text:
A declared package installs when the system-package provider kind covers it, under the trust gate ADR-009 §Trust specifies (ADR-009); Boilerplate MUST NOT invoke a package manager outside that gate, because an ungated install would violate the "orchestrate, don't replace" principle and introduce privilege escalation and safety concerns.

For a package with no covering provider, requirements stay advisory, not automatically installed. Boilerplate validates that the package is present on the system by checking for binaries on PATH or querying the platform's package manager. Missing packages produce a WARNING with the recommended install command. Success is silent.

docs.title: Pipeline Integration
docs.text:
• Plan display: When packages are declared for the current platform, the provisioning plan MUST include a Package requirements: section listing each package with the provider that installs it, or the command to install it by hand when no provider covers it. This gives the user visibility before confirming.
  • Post-install check: Covered packages install with the tools in step 4; a failed covered install raises BP_ENV_APPLY_FAILED, the same as a failed tool install: no record is written, and rerunning recovers. Uncovered packages are still checked after the installs and before the provenance record is written, and a missing one only warns. Warnings are appended to the success-path output and also surface via env status.

docs.title: env status Integration
docs.text: The env status command SHOULD check package availability for the current platform and report missing packages as warnings, using the same detection logic described above.

docs.title: Part 4: Provisioning Pipeline
docs.text: boilerplate env apply runs a single linear flow under an advisory lock. The provenance record (.boilerplate/environment.yml) is written only after a fully successful install, so it never reflects a partial state. If a step fails, the lock is released and the user re-runs env apply; because .prototools generation and proto install are idempotent, re-running converges to the resolved state.

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
1. Resolve       →  Load profile, resolve extends chain, merge tool versions, enforce allowlist
2. Plan/Confirm  →  Diff current vs. resolved; prompt for confirmation
3. Generate      →  Acquire advisory lock; write .prototools via staged write
4. Proto Install →  Invoke proto install for all resolved tools; install covered packages through their provider
5. Record Write  →  Write .boilerplate/environment.yml; release lock

docs.title: 1 — Resolve
docs.text:
Loads the target profile, resolves the extends chain (see §Profile Resolution), merges tool versions (last-writer-wins), and enforces the plugin allowlist. Produces a resolved tool map and ordered profile chain.

Failures at this step (BP_ENV_PROFILE_NOT_FOUND, BP_ENV_EXTENDS_CYCLE, BP_ENV_EXTENDS_NOT_FOUND, BP_ENV_VERSION_UNRESOLVABLE, BP_ENV_PLUGIN_NOT_ALLOWED) are validation errors — no files are modified.

docs.title: 2 — Plan and Confirm
docs.text:
Computes the diff between the current environment state (from .boilerplate/environment.yml, if present) and the resolved tool map. Displays a provisioning plan showing installs, upgrades, and unchanged tools.

Behavioral rules: - No differences: report "already up to date" and exit with no changes. - --dry-run: display the plan and exit without writing. - --format json without --yes or --dry-run: fail (JSON mode requires explicit intent to prevent interactive prompts in automation). - --yes or --ci: proceed without prompting. - Otherwise: prompt for confirmation (default: No). - Major version boundary crossings MUST be annotated with a warning.

docs.title: 3 — Generate .prototools
docs.text: Acquires the advisory lock per 07-operational-quality.md §Concurrency Control, then writes the resolved .prototools to the project root using the staged write (temp file + rename) from the Atomic Staged Write Pattern. All subsequent steps occur under the lock.

docs.title: 4 — Proto Install
docs.text:
Invokes proto to install each resolved tool, subject to the timeout defined in §Proto Integration. It also installs covered packages through their provider (see §Part 3.5), with the same failure rule. Progress is reported when running interactively.

If any installation fails, tool or covered package: the lock is released and BP_ENV_APPLY_FAILED is raised with the failing tool or package name, version, and installer output. The provenance record is not written; re-running env apply is the recovery path.

docs.title: 5 — Record Write
docs.text: Computes the proto_lock_hash from .protolock (if present), writes .boilerplate/environment.yml atomically (see §.boilerplate/environment.yml Schema), and releases the advisory lock. Emits a completion summary (profile, tools installed, duration) in both human-readable and JSON output formats.

docs.title: Signal Handling
docs.text: Signal handling follows the Atomic Staged Write Pattern. The advisory lock MUST be released on cleanup. An interrupted env apply leaves no provenance record; the recovery story is to run env apply again.

docs.title: Part 5: .boilerplate/environment.yml Schema
docs.text: The .boilerplate/environment.yml schema is defined in 02-data-models.md §EnvironmentProvisionRecord. The .boilerplate/ directory is created if it does not exist. Key write invariants:

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
schema_version: "boilerplate/environment@1"
boilerplate_version: "0.3.0"
profile_name: python-dev
profile_version: "1.2.0"
extends_chain:
  - base@1.0.0
  - python-dev@1.2.0
applied_at: "2026-03-20T14:30:00Z"
tools:
  node: "20.11.0"
  python: "3.12.2"
proto_lock_hash: "a3f1c9b2d8e4f7a1c3e5b7d9f2a4c6e8b0d2f4a6c8e0b2d4f6a8c0e2b4d6f8a0"

docs.title: Write Invariants
docs.text:
• The file MUST be written atomically (temp file + rename).
  • The file MUST only be written after proto has successfully installed all tools (step 4 of the provisioning flow).
  • Keys MUST be sorted deterministically for clean diffs.
  • The tools map keys MUST be sorted lexicographically.

docs.title: Schema Versioning
docs.text: The schema_version field enables forward-compatible evolution. Boilerplate MUST parse any environment.yml sharing the same major version (boilerplate/environment@1). Minor version bumps add optional fields; major bumps may change semantics. When Boilerplate encounters a file with an unrecognized major version, it MUST warn and treat the file as absent rather than failing hard — the environment may still be usable even if the record cannot be interpreted.

docs.title: Part 6: Concurrency
docs.text: Environment provisioning follows the shared concurrency control pattern. See 07-operational-quality.md §Concurrency Control. The lock is acquired when .prototools is generated and released after the provenance record is written (or on failure). Network filesystem caveats apply (see 07-operational-quality.md §Platform Portability).

docs.title: Part 7: Platform-Specific Behaviors
docs.text:
General platform portability rules are in 07-operational-quality.md §Platform Portability. This section covers environment-provisioning-specific platform details.

  • Windows: where file rename is not atomic, the staged write uses a copy-verify-replace pattern. Tool names in .prototools MUST be lowercase for case-insensitive filesystem compatibility.
  • WSL2: boilerplate doctor MUST detect Windows-hosted proto and warn about path mapping issues. Recommend installing proto natively within WSL2.
  • All platforms: proto MUST be on PATH.

docs.title: boilerplate env status
docs.text: Reports the current environment state by reading .boilerplate/environment.yml and .protolock. Shows the applied profile, tools, and whether the protolock hash is consistent. Warns if no environment record exists or if the protolock hash has drifted since the last apply.

docs.title: Part 9: Error Reference
docs.text: Environment provisioning uses the BP_ENV_* error code family, plus BP_CONCURRENCY_CONTENTION and BP_FILESYSTEM_* for infrastructure failures. See 07-operational-quality.md §Phase Prefixes for the phase registry and 07-operational-quality.md §Error Message Format for the standard message format.

docs.title: Part 10: Profile Lifecycle, Drift, and Compatibility
Profile Lifecycle Phases
docs.text:
A profile passes through several phases during its useful life. Each phase produces a distinct artifact and has distinct failure modes:

Phase Trigger Primary output Typical failures Authoring Author edits boilerplate-env.yml Profile draft Schema validation failure; unsatisfiable extends chain Publication Catalog ingest assigns immutable version Published profile Duplicate version; missing required sections Installation boilerplate env apply .prototools, .protolock (proto), .boilerplate/environment.yml BP_ENV_PROFILE_NOT_FOUND, BP_ENV_PLUGIN_NOT_ALLOWED, proto install failure Update boilerplate env apply against a newer profile version Updated state + refreshed .boilerplate/environment.yml Breaking change; lock conflict Removal (Future scope) Tool removal via proto Cleanup record Out of scope

Phase events feed structured logging (per §07 Phase Vocabulary, where the relevant phase is env_apply).

docs.title: Drift
docs.text: After a profile is applied, the live environment can diverge from the recorded state — for example, a tool version drifts from .protolock, the recomputed .protolock hash no longer matches EnvironmentProvisionRecord.proto_lock_hash, a declared tool is missing, the cached profile version differs from the catalog, or the host OS/arch differs from provision time. boilerplate env status reports such drift as warnings. The remediation in every case is to re-run boilerplate env apply.

docs.title: Template-Profile Compatibility
docs.text: When a template declares requires_profile, applying or updating it verifies compatibility with the project's environment state: the required profile resolves in the catalog, the project's resolved profile name and version satisfy the template's range, and the tools the template depends on are present in the resolved profile chain. These checks are owned by the resolve/composition path (§04 Composition Engine) at new and update time. On read-only commands a mismatch is a warning surfaced via env status, not a hard failure.

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text: Scenario Expected Outcome Valid single-profile apply .prototools written, proto succeeds, environment.yml written, exit 0 Profile with extends chain Chain resolved base-first, versions merged (last-writer-wins), exit 0 Profile not found BP_ENV_PROFILE_NOT_FOUND, no files modified, exit 3 Cycle in extends chain BP_ENV_EXTENDS_CYCLE with full cycle path, exit 3 Tool not in allowed_proto_plugins BP_ENV_PLUGIN_NOT_ALLOWED, no files modified, exit 3 proto install fails BP_ENV_APPLY_FAILED, environment.yml not written, exit 1 --dry-run Plan displayed, no files modified, exit 0 No changes detected "Environment is already up to date.", exit 0 Interrupted env apply No provenance record written; re-running env apply completes provisioning proto not installed BP_ENV_PROTO_NOT_FOUND, immediate exit 3 before any I/O Concurrent env apply Second invocation fails with BP_CONCURRENCY_CONTENTION after timeout

docs.title: Performance Contracts
docs.text: See §07 Operational Quality for all performance targets. Environment provisioning is I/O and network intensive; the dominant cost is proto downloading tool binaries. Boilerplate's own orchestration overhead (profile resolution, diff computation, .prototools generation) MUST be negligible relative to proto install time.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The user-authored runtime configuration surface: the Settings object, a per-user profile (profile.toml), and the boilerplate-sources.yml catalog-source file — the YAML and environment-variable inputs the operator owns, separate from the domain schemas in Data models.

See Product overview for the glossary. See Security model for the security constraints that apply to the configuration files specified here (YAML tag rejection, path traversal validation).

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
The Settings object holds all runtime configuration. It is loaded once at CLI startup and passed to all application services. Settings MUST be immutable after construction.

Loading order (later sources override earlier): 1. Compiled-in defaults 2. .env file in the current working directory (if present) — standard KEY=VALUE format, one assignment per line, # for comments 3. OS environment variables

All Settings field names are prefixed with BOILERPLATE_ when read from the environment, using the flat field name directly (e.g. BOILERPLATE_DEBUG). Profile has no environment-variable layer — it is TOML-file-only.

Field Env Var Type Default Description default_templates_dir BOILERPLATE_DEFAULT_TEMPLATES_DIR path {user_data_dir}/boilerplate/templates The user's standing template directory, searched before extra_template_dirs. Starts empty; first-party templates do not live here. extra_template_dirs BOILERPLATE_EXTRA_TEMPLATE_DIRS list of paths [] Additional template directories searched after default_templates_dir. OS environment values are split on the platform path separator. When both sources provide extra_template_dirs, OS environment entries are placed before .env file entries in the resulting list (giving OS entries higher search priority). Deduplication preserves the first occurrence. debug BOILERPLATE_DEBUG boolean false Enable debug-level logging; overridden to true by --verbose flag render_timeout BOILERPLATE_RENDER_TIMEOUT integer 300 Maximum seconds for a single template render proto_timeout BOILERPLATE_PROTO_TIMEOUT integer 600 Maximum seconds for a proto install invocation. See §08. fetch_timeout BOILERPLATE_FETCH_TIMEOUT integer 60 Maximum seconds for a single network operation. See §07. lock_timeout BOILERPLATE_LOCK_TIMEOUT integer 60 Maximum seconds to acquire advisory lock. See §06. allowed_extension_packages BOILERPLATE_ALLOWED_EXTENSION_PACKAGES list of string [] System-wide allowlist of Python package names whose Jinja2 extensions are permitted during rendering. See §03 Template System. request_id BOILERPLATE_REQUEST_ID string or null null Correlation ID for structured log events. When set (typically by CI pipelines or orchestration tools), the value is included in every structured log event as the request_id field. See §07 Operational Quality. accessible BOILERPLATE_ACCESSIBLE boolean false When enabled (any value except unset, empty, whitespace-only, 0, or false, case-insensitive), activates all accessibility accommodations: no color, append-mode progress, text-only status labels, no banner. See §05 CLI Reference.

template_dirs (computed, not configurable): the concatenation of [default_templates_dir] + extra_template_dirs. This is the ordered list of directories the catalog build process searches. First-party templates — the published per-template git repositories (ADR-006) — are registered by the catalog build as an implicit final source after all template_dirs entries — see 03 §Template Directory Resolution Order; they are not a Settings path.

{user_data_dir} resolves to the platform-appropriate user data directory (e.g., %LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows, ~/.local/share on Linux).

If loading the Settings object fails for any reason, the CLI MUST print an error and exit with code 2 (CONFIG_ERROR).

docs.title: Profile
docs.text:
Per-user default answers for template questions, read from profile.toml at the config root. Grammar: [defaults] (any template) and [templates.<name>] (one template, overrides [defaults]). Keys are open — they are template question names; boilerplate validates none of them. Loader: boilerplate.settings.profile.load_profile(template_name); missing file yields {}, malformed TOML raises ProfileError.

The config root is platform-specific: %APPDATA%\boilerplate on Windows, and $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/boilerplate (falling back to ~/.config/boilerplate) on POSIX.

Precedence, high to low: the user's interactive answer › [templates.<name>] › [defaults] › the template's own default. Defaults pre-fill prompts — the user can still override at the prompt; --non-interactive takes them as-is.

docs.title: Catalog Source Configuration File
docs.text:
File location: {user_data_dir}/boilerplate/boilerplate-sources.yml

This file defines the template and profile catalog sources that Boilerplate searches during resolution. It is a single YAML document with one top-level key.

Top-level structure:

Field Type Required Description sources list of SourceEntry Yes Ordered list of catalog source definitions

SourceEntry schema:

Field Type Required Default Constraints name string Yes — Human-readable source identifier.
